They follow the rules of the labels of a server ([SetServerLabels](#setserverlabels)): at most 64, a key of 1 to 63 of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, and `-` that starts with a letter, and a value of at most 255 bytes of UTF-8 without control characters. |

The response `CreateSizeResponse` has the field `size`, the new `Size`.

### GetSize

Returns one size, also a retired one.

| Item              | Value                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.SizeService/GetSize`                                         |
| Policy action     | `size.get`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions) |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                             |
| Audit entry       | action `size.get`, target kind `size`, target ID the name of the size          |

The request `GetSizeRequest` has the field `name`, the name of the size. The response `GetSizeResponse` has the field `size`, a `Size`.

### ListSizes

Returns the sizes, smallest first: by vCPUs, then RAM, then name. The list has no pages. [ListMachineSizes](/reference/machine-api/#listmachinesizes) gives the users the same list without the retired sizes, and without the pools and the labels.

| Item              | Value                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.SizeService/ListSizes`                                        |
| Policy action     | `size.list`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions) |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                              |
| Audit entry       | action `size.list`, no target                                                   |

The request `ListSizesRequest` has the field `include_retired`, a bool. With `true`, the list also holds the retired sizes. The response `ListSizesResponse` has the field `sizes`, a list of `Size`.

### RetireSize

Stops new machines of a size. A create with the size fails from then on ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#createmachine)). A create takes a share lock on the row of its size, so the retirement waits for each create that read the size before it, and a create that starts during the retirement waits and then fails. The machines of the size keep running, and keep their size. A retirement of a retired size changes nothing, and its row version stays.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.SizeService/RetireSize`                                                                                              |
| Policy action     | `size.retire`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                      |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call changes nothing.                                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `size.retire`, target kind `size`, target ID the name of the size, detail `already`: `true` for a size that was retired already |

The request `RetireSizeRequest` has the field `name`, the name of the size. The response `RetireSizeResponse` has the field `size`, the `Size` after the change.

### Errors of SizeService

| Error                                                                                                                              | Cause                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid_argument` with `invalid argument: invalid size: ...`                                                                      | `CreateSize` with numbers out of bounds. The rest of the message names the field and the bound. |
| `invalid_argument` with `invalid argument: invalid name: the size name ...` or `invalid argument: invalid name: the pool name ...` | `CreateSize` with a name that is not a lowercase DNS label.                                     |
| `invalid_argument` with `invalid argument: invalid label: ...`                                                                     | `CreateSize` with a label that breaks a rule.                                                   |
| `invalid_argument` with `idempotency: invalid key: this method needs an Idempotency-Key header`                                    | `CreateSize` without an idempotency key.                                                        |
| `not_found` with `not found: no pool is named "<pool>"`                                                                            | `CreateSize` with a pool that no live pool has.                                                 |
| `already_exists` with `already exists: a size is named "<name>" already. A retired size keeps its name, so pick a new name`        | `CreateSize` with the name of a size, also of a retired one.                                    |
| `not_found` with `not found: no size is named "<name>"`                                                                            | `GetSize` or `RetireSize` of an unknown name.                                                   |
| `failed_precondition` with `failed precondition: the size default stays, because a create without a size takes it`                 | `RetireSize` of the size `default`.                                                             |

Example:

```sh
sudo curl -s --unix-socket /run/hopbox/admin.sock \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"name":"large","vcpus":8,"memoryBytes":"34359738368","diskBytes":"200000000000","pool":"big","labels":{"disk":"nvme"}}' \
  http://hopboxd/hopbox.admin.v1.SizeService/CreateSize
```

## OrgService

`hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService` lets instance admins see the metadata of every org, suspend an org, and set the usage limits of orgs. It shows no member and no resource of an org. [The org API](/reference/org-api/) covers the calls of the members of an org. Each call that acts on one org writes its audit entry with that org, so the owners of the org see it.

The message `Org` holds the metadata of one org:

| Field                 | Type                        | Description                                                            |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                  | string                      | The UUID of the org.                                                   |
| `name`                | string                      | The name of the org.                                                   |
| `personal_account_id` | string                      | The UUID of the account of a personal org, or empty for another org.   |
| `member_count`        | int64                       | The number of members.                                                 |
| `suspended`           | bool                        | `true` while the org is suspended.                                     |
| `suspend_time`        | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The start of the suspension. Unset for an org that is not suspended.   |
| `suspend_reason`      | string                      | The reason of the suspension, or empty.                                |
| `limits`              | `OrgLimits`                 | The limits that apply: each override, else the default of the install. |
| `limit_overrides`     | `OrgLimitOverrides`         | The limits of this org that replace the defaults.                      |
| `usage`               | `OrgUsage`                  | What the org uses now.                                                 |
| `version`             | int64                       | The version of the org ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#org)).       |
| `create_time`         | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The creation time of the org.                                          |

`OrgLimits` and `OrgUsage` have the fields `machines` (int32), `vcpus` (int32), `memory_bytes` (int64), and `disk_bytes` (int64), as in [the org API](/reference/org-api/#orglimits-and-orgusage). `OrgLimitOverrides` has the same fields, each one `optional`. A field that is not set takes the default of the install. A limit of 0 allows nothing.

### ListOrgs

Lists every org of the install, oldest first, one page at a time.

| Item              | Value                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/ListOrgs`                                             |
| Policy action     | `org.list_all`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions) |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                 |
| Audit entry       | action `org.list_all`, no org, no target                                           |

| Field        | Type   | Default | Description                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `page_size`  | int32  | 100     | The most orgs in one response, 1 to 1000.                                        |
| `page_token` | string | empty   | The `next_page_token` of the response before. Leave it empty for the first page. |

The response `ListOrgsResponse` has the fields `orgs`, a repeated `Org`, and `next_page_token`. The token is empty on the last page. A page size out of range, or a page token that does not decode, gets `invalid_argument`.

### SuspendOrg

Suspends an org, for example to handle abuse ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#suspension)). A suspended org stays as it is, with its first reason, and the call succeeds again without a change.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/SuspendOrg`                                                                                                                                               |
| Policy action     | `org.suspend`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                                                                      |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call changes nothing.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `org.suspend`, org the org, target kind `org`, details `reason` and `already`. The reason is that of the suspension. `already` is `true` for an org that was suspended already. |

| Field    | Type   | Description                                                                                                                              |
| -------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id` | string | The UUID of the org.                                                                                                                     |
| `reason` | string | The reason, which the members of the org see. At most 256 characters, without control characters. The server drops the spaces around it. |

The call stops the resources of the org in its transaction, through `OrgSuspending` ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#what-a-member-leaves-behind)). It sets the target `stopped` on each machine of the org, except a hibernated one. Each machine that it changes gets an entry `machine.stop` with the detail `reason` (`org suspended`). The response `SuspendOrgResponse` has the field `org`, the `Org` after the change.

| Error                                                  | Code               |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| `org_id` is not a UUID, or the reason breaks a rule    | `invalid_argument` |
| No org has the ID: `not found: no org has the ID <id>` | `not_found`        |

### UnsuspendOrg

Ends the suspension of an org. Its machines stay stopped until their users start them. An org that is not suspended stays as it is, and the call succeeds.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/UnsuspendOrg`                                                                                            |
| Policy action     | `org.unsuspend`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                   |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                    |
| Audit entry       | action `org.unsuspend`, org the org, target kind `org`, details `old_reason` and `already` (`true` for an org that was not suspended) |

The request `UnsuspendOrgRequest` has the field `org_id`. The response `UnsuspendOrgResponse` has the field `org`. The errors are those of `SuspendOrg`.

### SetOrgLimits

Replaces the limit overrides of one org. A limit that the request leaves out takes the default of the install. So a request without overrides puts the org back on the defaults. A new limit below the usage of the org stops nothing. The org then creates and starts no more machines until its usage fits.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/SetOrgLimits`                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Policy action     | `org.set_limits`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                                                                                                                             |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call sets the same overrides again.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Audit entry       | action `org.set_limits`, org the org, target kind `org`. The details are `machines`, `vcpus`, `memory_bytes`, and `disk_bytes`, then the same keys with the prefix `old_`. Each value is a number, or `default` for a limit without an override. |

| Field              | Type                | Description                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id`           | string              | The UUID of the org.                                                                                                                  |
| `limit_overrides`  | `OrgLimitOverrides` | The new overrides. Each field is 0 or more.                                                                                           |
| `expected_version` | optional int64      | The `version` of the org that the caller read. If the org has another version now, the call fails with `aborted` and changes nothing. |

The response `SetOrgLimitsResponse` has the field `org`. A limit below 0 gets `invalid_argument`, for example `invalid argument: invalid limit: the vCPU limit -1 is below 0`. An unknown org gets `not_found`.

### GetDefaultOrgLimits

Returns the limits of every org without an override. They live in the row of `install_config` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#install_config)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/GetDefaultOrgLimits`                                             |
| Policy action     | `org_limits.get_defaults`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions) |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | action `org_limits.get_defaults`, no target                                                   |

The request `GetDefaultOrgLimitsRequest` has no fields. The response `GetDefaultOrgLimitsResponse` has the field `defaults`, a `DefaultOrgLimits`:

| Field                  | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `limits`               | `OrgLimits`                 | The default limits. A fresh install has 3 machines, 6 vCPUs, 24 GiB of RAM, and 300 GB of disk.                                 |
| `max_orgs_per_account` | int32                       | The most orgs that one account owns besides its personal org ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#createorg)). The default is 10. |
| `version`              | int64                       | The version of the whole install config ([GetInstallConfig](#getinstallconfig)).                                                |
| `update_time`          | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the last change of the install config.                                                                              |

### SetDefaultOrgLimits

Changes the limits of every org without an override, and returns them. A limit that the request leaves out keeps its value. A change adds 1 to the version of the install config.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.OrgService/SetDefaultOrgLimits`                                                                                                                                |
| Policy action     | `org_limits.set_defaults`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                                                    |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Audit entry       | action `org_limits.set_defaults`, no target. The details are the new limits and the old ones, as for `SetOrgLimits`, with `max_orgs_per_account` and `old_max_orgs_per_account`. |

| Field                  | Type           | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `machines`             | optional int32 | The most machines of an org, 0 or more.                                                                                                                     |
| `vcpus`                | optional int32 | The most vCPUs of an org, 0 or more.                                                                                                                        |
| `memory_bytes`         | optional int64 | The most RAM of an org, in bytes, 0 or more.                                                                                                                |
| `disk_bytes`           | optional int64 | The most disk of an org, in bytes, 0 or more.                                                                                                               |
| `max_orgs_per_account` | optional int32 | The most orgs that one account owns besides its personal org, 0 or more. A lower value deletes no org. It only refuses new orgs above it.                   |
| `expected_version`     | optional int64 | The `version` of the install config that the caller read. If the install config has another version now, the call fails with `aborted` and changes nothing. |

A request that sets no limit gets `invalid_argument` with the message `invalid argument: the update sets no limit`. The response `SetDefaultOrgLimitsResponse` has the field `defaults`.

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin org default-limits set --machines 5
machines  5
vcpus  6
memory_bytes  25769803776
disk_bytes  300000000000
max_orgs_per_account  10
version  4
update_time  2026-10-16T15:50:02Z
```

## MachineService

`hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService` lets instance admins see the machines of every org, and stop or delete any of them. This also works in a suspended org, for example to handle abuse. It never opens a shell in a machine and never reads its secrets. [The machine API](/reference/machine-api/) covers the calls of the members of an org.

The message `Machine` of this service is a machine with the facts that only instance admins see:

| Field       | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `machine`   | `hopbox.v1.Machine` | The machine as its users see it ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#machine)), but without its `start_command`, which is always empty here. A start command can hold data of the org, and an instance admin sees the metadata of an org, not its contents. |
| `server_id` | string              | The UUID of the node of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `address`   | string              | The IPv4 address of the machine on the network of its node, such as `10.240.0.2` ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#addresses)). Only `ListMachines` fills it. It is empty in the responses of `StopMachine` and `DeleteMachine`.                       |

A call on one machine names it with `id` or `name`, as in the public API ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#naming-a-machine)). The admin calls skip the role check and the suspension check of the public API.

### ListMachines

Lists the machines of every org, or of one org, one page at a time, in the order of their IDs. A machine whose current state is `deleted` is not in the list. The list holds metadata only. A machine of a deleted org stays in the list of every org until its executor deleted it. Its `org_id` is then empty.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService/ListMachines`                                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `machine.list_all`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                                                 |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `machine.list_all`, no target. With `org_id`, the entry has that org and the detail `org_id`. Without it, the entry has no org. |

| Field        | Type            | Default | Description                                                                      |
| ------------ | --------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id`     | optional string | none    | Lists only the machines of this org.                                             |
| `page_size`  | int32           | 100     | The most machines in one response, 1 to 1000.                                    |
| `page_token` | string          | empty   | The `next_page_token` of the response before. Leave it empty for the first page. |

The response `ListMachinesResponse` has the fields `machines`, a repeated `Machine` of this service, and `next_page_token`. The token is empty on the last page. A page size out of range, a page token that does not decode, or an `org_id` that is not a UUID gets `invalid_argument`. An `org_id` that names no org gets an empty list.

### StopMachine

Sets the target of any machine to `stopped`, and waits for it for up to 60 s. It works as `StopMachine` of the public API ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#stopmachine)), also in a suspended org. A hibernated machine refuses the stop with `failed_precondition` and the message `failed precondition: machine action not allowed: cannot stop a hibernated machine: wake it first`.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService/StopMachine`                                                                   |
| Policy action     | `machine.admin_stop`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)                        |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call finds the target `stopped`, and changes nothing.                                              |
| Audit entry       | action `machine.admin_stop`, org the org of the machine, target kind `machine`, details `name` and `old_target` |

The request `StopMachineRequest` names the machine. The response `StopMachineResponse` has the fields `machine` (a `Machine` of this service), `duration`, and `done`, as in [the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#lifecycle-calls). The call gets the default deadline of 61 s, and waits as the public call does ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-wait)).

### DeleteMachine

Sets the target of any machine to `deleted`, and waits for it for up to 60 s. It works as `DeleteMachine` of the public API ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#deletemachine)), also in a suspended org. The name and the SSH port of the machine stay reserved for its org for 7 days.

| Item              | Value                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService/DeleteMachine`                                                  |
| Policy action     | `machine.admin_delete`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions)       |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call fails with `failed_precondition`.                                              |
| Audit entry       | action `machine.admin_delete`, org the org of the machine, target kind `machine`, details `name` |

The request `DeleteMachineRequest` names the machine. The response `DeleteMachineResponse` has the fields `machine`, `duration`, and `done`. A machine whose target is `deleted` already gets `failed_precondition` with the message `failed precondition: machine action not allowed: cannot delete a machine that is being deleted`.

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin machine stop --name box1
id  01a1460c-1f6e-7b8a-9c42-3d5e7f8a9b10
name  box1
state  pending
target_state  stopped
duration  39.001s
done  false
```

## ImageService

`hopbox.admin.v1.ImageService` manages the images that new machines start from: the metadata of image artifacts ([Artifact format](/reference/artifact-format/)). The images live in the table `images` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#images)). A create takes the newest image of the name that it asks for, `default` by default ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#createmachine)). The service holds only the metadata. The URL of an image tells the nodes where to download the compressed disk. An empty URL serves a node that has the image in its cache already.

The message `Image` holds one image:

| Field           | Type                        | Description                                                                        |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | string                      | The UUID of the image.                                                             |
| `name`          | string                      | The name of the image, for example `default`.                                      |
| `digest`        | string                      | `sha256:` and the sha256 of the bytes of the `artifact.json` of the image, in hex. |
| `arch`          | string                      | The CPU architecture of the image, `x86_64`.                                       |
| `kernel_sha256` | string                      | The sha256 of the guest kernel that the image needs, in hex.                       |
| `disk_size`     | int64                       | The size of the disk of the image, in bytes.                                       |
| `disk_sha256`   | string                      | The sha256 of the disk of the image, in hex.                                       |
| `url`           | string                      | The https URL from which nodes download the compressed disk, or empty.             |
| `build_time`    | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the build: `created_at` of `artifact.json`.                            |
| `register_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the registration.                                                      |

### RegisterImage

Adds an image from the bytes of its `artifact.json`. The newest image of a name is the one that new machines of that name take. The control role also registers the default image of its release at each start ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#the-default-image-of-the-release)). The same bytes a second time change nothing, and return the image that exists. A call to this method records no release on the image, so the control role never skips because of it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#the-default-image-of-the-release)). The control role registers the default image of its release with the release of its `hopboxd`, and skips it when the install has an image of the same name from a newer release. Two registrations of the same bytes at the same time also give one image: the second one gets `registered` `false`.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.ImageService/RegisterImage`                                                                                                                                    |
| Policy action     | `image.register`: `local_root` and `admin_key`                                                                                                                                   |
| Idempotent option | no. A second call with the same bytes changes nothing.                                                                                                                           |
| Audit entry       | action `image.register`, no org, target kind `image`, target ID the image ID. The details are `name`, `digest`, and `already`: `true` for an image that the install had already. |

| Field      | Type   | Description                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `metadata` | bytes  | The bytes of the `artifact.json` of the image, unchanged. Their sha256 is the digest, so a reformat makes another image. |
| `url`      | string | An https URL of the compressed disk, or empty.                                                                           |

The call reads `metadata` with the rules of `internal/artifact` ([Artifact format](/reference/artifact-format/#artifactjson)). Format version 1 knows only the kind `image`. The response `RegisterImageResponse` has these fields:

| Field        | Type    | Description                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `image`      | `Image` | The image.                                                                                                                       |
| `registered` | bool    | `true` for a new image. `false` for an image that the install had already. A second call with another `url` keeps the first URL. |

| Error                                                                                                                                     | Code               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `metadata` breaks a rule of the artifact format, for example `invalid argument: invalid artifact metadata: kind "snapshot", want "image"` | `invalid_argument` |
| `metadata` has a `format_version` other than 1: `invalid argument: unsupported artifact format version ...`                               | `invalid_argument` |
| `url` is not an https URL with a host: `invalid argument: the image URL "<url>" is not an https URL`                                      | `invalid_argument` |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin image register bin/image/artifact.json --url https://dl.example.org/images/default/disk.raw.zst
id  01a1460a-7c21-7d4e-8f90-1a2b3c4d5e6f
name  default
digest  sha256:422d31d7a4fd5e6958162b22e3d772f71b5a1465cbd6255d253ae8c087873dc8
registered  true
```

### ListImages

Lists the images of the install, by name, newest first.

| Item              | Value                                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.admin.v1.ImageService/ListImages`                                       |
| Policy action     | `image.list`: `local_root`, `admin_key`, and an [admin session](#admin-sessions) |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                               |
| Audit entry       | action `image.list`, no target                                                   |

The request `ListImagesRequest` has no fields. The response `ListImagesResponse` has the field `images`, a repeated `Image`. The list has no pages.

# The API server

> The API server: its listener, the request gate, callers and the policy matrix, the interceptors, idempotency keys, error codes, reflection, health, and InstallService.

The control role serves the API of hopbox with Connect. This page covers the listener, the protocols, the request gate, and the callers and the policy check. It also covers the chain of interceptors, idempotency keys, the error codes, reflection, health, and `InstallService`. [The sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/) covers the sign-in, account, and audit calls. [The org API](/reference/org-api/) covers the org, member, and invitation calls. [The machine API](/reference/machine-api/) covers the machine calls. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/) covers the admin API and the admin socket. [The internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/) covers the internal listener, which serves the cluster API to the servers of the install over TLS. The chain of a call, the gate, the policy, and the errors of this page apply to it too. The code is in `internal/api` and `internal/service`.

## Listener

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Address           | `control.api_listen` of the bootstrap config, by default `127.0.0.1:7080` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Transport         | TCP without TLS. The address must be a loopback address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| HTTP versions     | HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Protocols         | Connect, gRPC, and gRPC-Web, with the binary protobuf and JSON codecs, and gzip                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Services          | Every service of `hopbox.v1`: `InstallService`, `AuthService`, `AccountService`, `AuditService`, `OrgService`, `APIKeyService`, `SSHKeyService`, `MachineService`, and `VarService` ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/)). The services of the admin API, with `hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService` and `hopbox.admin.v1.ImageService` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#where-the-admin-api-is-served)). gRPC reflection and gRPC health. |
| Browser endpoints | `GET /auth/github/start`, `GET /auth/github/callback`, `GET /auth/google/start`, and `GET /auth/google/callback`: plain HTTP for the sign-in with GitHub and Google, outside of the chain of a call ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#endpoints)). `GET /auth/machine`: plain HTTP for the sign-in of a private machine URL ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)).                                         |
| Console           | every other `GET` or `HEAD` request whose first path segment has no dot, outside of the chain of a call ([Console](/reference/console/#where-hopboxd-serves-it)). Any other request with an unknown path gets `404`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

gRPC needs HTTP/2. Without TLS, a client must start HTTP/2 with prior knowledge, for example `curl --http2-prior-knowledge` or `grpcurl -plaintext`. The Connect protocol also works over HTTP/1.1.

The clients of the install do not reach this listener. They reach the edge servers, which forward the requests of the domain of the install to the internal listener of the control role ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests)). The internal listener serves these requests with the same handler as this listener, with the address of each client as the peer ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#forwarded-requests)). This listener stays on loopback for the processes and the SSH tunnels of the server. Its peers are loopback addresses, so the rate limits of a client skip them ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits)).

The listener serves the admin API too, for admin API keys and for the Admin area of the console. The edge servers forward it too, so the admin API is public behind the edge. On this listener, the policy refuses every admin call of every other caller ([Callers and policy](#callers-and-policy)). The Admin area calls a part of the admin API with an admin session: the session of an instance admin with a sign-in within the last 10 minutes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#admin-sessions)). Root on the server calls the admin API through the admin socket ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#the-admin-socket)).

| HTTP server setting               | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header read timeout               | 10 s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Body read timeout of a unary call | 30 s from the start of the request, until the whole body arrives. A request without a body, such as a Connect `GET`, has no such bound. A stream has none, and neither has a connection that a handler takes over, such as a WebSocket. A read that runs out of time fails with the code `deadline_exceeded` and the message `the request body did not arrive in time`. |
| Idle connection timeout           | 2 min                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Largest request message           | 4 MiB. A larger message gets `resource_exhausted` before any handler reads it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| HTTP/2 streams of one connection  | at most 100 at once (`api.MaxClientStreams`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| HTTP/2 receive window             | 256 KiB for each stream, and 25 MiB for the connection. The window of the connection holds every stream at once. So a stream whose reads stop, such as an upload to a slow node, never stalls the other calls of the connection.                                                                                                                                        |

A path that names no service gets HTTP status 404.

The listener also serves the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` of exec over HTTP/1.1 ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)). It also serves the MCP server of hopbox at `/mcp`, for AI agents with a CLI token or an API key ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/)). Each tool of the MCP server calls the API in the process, through the chain of a call below.

## The chain of a call

Every call passes these steps, in this order:

1. **Request ID.** The server makes a new UUIDv7 for each HTTP request. It puts the ID in the response header `Hopbox-Request-Id`, in the logs of the call, and in the audit entries of the call. The server never takes an ID from the client, so an ID always names one request.
2. **Metrics and access log.** After the call ends, the server counts it in the metrics ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-the-api)) and writes one log record ([Logs](#logs)).
3. **Error mapping.** The server turns each error into a Connect error with a code ([Errors](#errors)).
4. **Default deadline.** A unary call whose client sent no deadline gets a deadline of 30 s. A lifecycle call of a machine gets 61 s instead (`api.LifecycleTimeout`), so its wait of up to 60 s fits ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-wait)). These calls are `StartMachine`, `StopMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, and `DeleteMachine` of `hopbox.v1.MachineService`, and `StopMachine` and `DeleteMachine` of `hopbox.admin.v1.MachineService`. A deadline from the client stays as it is, longer or shorter. The client sends a deadline with the header `Connect-Timeout-Ms` or `grpc-timeout`. A stream gets no default deadline.
5. **Maintenance mode.** In maintenance mode, the server refuses each call that can change the install ([Maintenance mode](#maintenance-mode)).
6. **Request gate.** The gate names the caller of the call ([Request gate](#request-gate)).
7. **Idempotency.** A method with the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` runs once for each idempotency key ([Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys)).
8. **Handler.** The handler calls one operation of the service layer. The operation checks the policy first, then its input, then acts.

Reflection and health pass the same steps, except the idempotency step. In place of a service operation, they run the policy check with their own actions ([Callers and policy](#callers-and-policy)).

## Request gate

The request gate is the one place where every call proves who calls. It holds a chain of credential resolvers. Each resolver knows one kind of credential. The gate asks each resolver in turn:

1. A resolver that does not find its kind of credential passes the call to the next resolver.
2. A resolver that finds its kind of credential, and that credential proves a caller, decides. The call goes on with that caller.
3. A resolver that finds its kind of credential, but the credential proves no caller, ends the call with `unauthenticated` and the message `the credential is not valid`. Examples are an unknown, expired, revoked, or malformed key.
4. Sometimes a resolver cannot check the credential, for example because the control store does not answer. It then ends the call with `unavailable` and the message `the server failed to check the credential. Retry later`. The SDKs retry this call, because its answer carries `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1` ([Answers of calls that changed nothing](#answers-of-calls-that-changed-nothing)).
5. If no resolver decides and the call has an `Authorization` header, the gate ends the call with `unauthenticated` and the message `the credential is not valid`. A credential that the server cannot check never passes as anonymous.
6. If no resolver decides and the call has no `Authorization` header, the caller is anonymous.

The client always gets the fixed messages above. The cause goes only to the log, with the request ID ([Logs](#logs)).

The gate only names the caller. The policy check in the service layer decides what the caller can do.

| Listener          | Resolvers, in order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API listener      | the session cookie `__Host-hopbox_session` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)), then CLI access tokens, API keys, and admin API keys in the header `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#how-the-request-gate-reads-them)) |
| Admin socket      | the peer of the socket, which proves the caller `local_root` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#the-admin-socket))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Internal listener | the server certificate of the TLS connection, which proves the caller `server` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/))                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

On the internal listener, a step after the gate refuses an anonymous caller on every procedure but `/hopbox.cluster.v1.EnrollmentService/Enroll`, before the policy check. The call gets `unauthenticated` with the message `this call needs a server certificate`. This covers gRPC health and reflection there too. On the other listeners, an anonymous caller reaches every procedure, and the policy decides.

### The contract of a resolver

The API listener has a resolver for each credential that hopbox issues: sessions, CLI access tokens, API keys, and admin API keys. Each of the last three reads only the bearer credentials of its own prefix ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#forms-and-prefixes)). The resolver of server certificates exists on the internal listener. It reads the certificate of the TLS connection from the context, and ties it to a server of the registry. It refuses an unknown, expired, foreign, or decommissioned certificate with `the credential is not valid` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). A resolver is a Go value with the method `Resolve(ctx, credentials) (caller, ok, err)` in `internal/api`. It gets the request headers and the peer, and must keep these rules:

| Case                                                                                         | It returns                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The request does not carry its kind of credential.                                           | `ok` false, no error                                                                                            |
| The credential proves a caller.                                                              | the caller, `ok` true, no error                                                                                 |
| The credential is of its kind but proves no caller: unknown, expired, revoked, or malformed. | an error that wraps `api.ErrCredentialRefused`. The resolver of the session cookie is the one exception, below. |
| It cannot check the credential, for example because the control store does not answer.       | any other error                                                                                                 |

An error of a resolver goes to the log, so it must never hold a secret, such as the credential itself.

A browser sends a cookie on its own, also long after its session ended. So the resolver of the session cookie treats a cookie that names no live session as no credential. The gate then goes on to the next resolver. The resolver also adds the clear of the cookie to `ResponseHeader` of the credentials. The response carries the clear, unless the handler sets the cookie itself ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). A stale cookie thus never blocks the next sign-in. A live session from a call that fails the check against cross-site requests is refused, as the contract says.

## Callers and policy

Each call has one typed caller. Its kind is also the actor kind of its audit entries ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#audit_log)).

| Kind         | Caller                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Proved by                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `anonymous`  | A caller without a credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | no credential                                                                                                                                     |
| `session`    | A user signed in to the console. The caller also says whether the account is an instance admin.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | the session cookie ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/))                                                                 |
| `cli_token`  | A user through the hopbox CLI. It acts as its account in every org of the account. The caller also says whether the account is an instance admin.                                                                                                                                                                                         | a CLI access token ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens))                                     |
| `member_key` | A member API key, which acts as its account, only in the org of the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | an API key ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys))                                               |
| `org_key`    | An org API key: a service credential of one org, with the rights of a member without personal resources.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | an API key ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys))                                               |
| `admin_key`  | An admin API key, with install scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | an admin API key ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#admin-api-keys))                                   |
| `local_root` | Root, or the user of `hopboxd`, on a control server.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | the peer of the admin socket                                                                                                                      |
| `server`     | A server of the install, for itself. The caller carries the roles of its certificate, such as `node` or `dns`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | a server certificate on the internal listener ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/))                                            |
| `control`    | Another control process of the install, for forwarding a data stream. It has no account and no credential ID. It may do only `control.forward_stream`, besides the actions that every caller may do.                                                                                                                                      | the control certificate of its internal listener, which names `hopbox://control` ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#callers)) |
| `ssh_key`    | An account through the SSH front door. No request of the API carries it. The service layer makes it only to check an SSH connection, for `machine.ssh` ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#who-opens-a-machine)). It is the actor of the audit entry `machine.ssh` ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#audit)). | a signature with an SSH key of the account, which the edge server checked                                                                         |

Every operation of the service layer calls one policy check, `policy.Authorize(caller, action, resource)`, before it reads or changes anything. An action without a rule is refused for every caller. This matrix lists every action and the callers that it allows. Every other caller is refused.

| Action                                | Operation                                                                                                                                                                    | Resource                                                                    | Allowed callers                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `install.get_info`                    | `InstallService.GetInstallInfo`                                                                                                                                              | the install                                                                 | every caller, also `anonymous`                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `install_config.get`                  | `InstallConfigService.GetInstallConfig`                                                                                                                                      | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `install_config.update`               | `InstallConfigService.UpdateInstallConfig`                                                                                                                                   | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `certificate.get`                     | `CertificateService.GetCertificate`                                                                                                                                          | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `smtp_config.get`                     | `InstallConfigService.GetSMTPConfig`                                                                                                                                         | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `smtp_config.set`                     | `InstallConfigService.SetSMTPConfig`                                                                                                                                         | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `smtp_config.clear`                   | `InstallConfigService.ClearSMTPConfig`                                                                                                                                       | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `oauth_config.get`                    | `InstallConfigService.GetOAuthConfig`                                                                                                                                        | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `oauth_config.set`                    | `InstallConfigService.SetOAuthClient`                                                                                                                                        | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `oauth_config.clear`                  | `InstallConfigService.ClearOAuthClient`                                                                                                                                      | the install                                                                 | `local_root`, `admin_key`, an admin `session`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `keyring.rotate`                      | `KeyringService.RotateKEK`                                                                                                                                                   | the install                                                                 | `local_root` only                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The `server.*` actions of the control channel and of the edge role have a server as their resource. The policy allows them only to a caller of kind `server` whose server is that resource. So the certificate of one server never acts for another ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)).

Each key-encryption key file lives on one control server, so only root on that server can rotate it, stage it, promote it, list it, or rewrap with it. An admin API key reaches whichever control server answers the call, so it cannot touch a keyring. The first-admin login link is for root on a control server only.

An `org_key` acts as a member without private machines, and is never an org admin. An instance admin has only the rights of its own roles in the `machine.*` rules of the public API. A caller that `machine.get` refuses gets `not_found` instead of `permission_denied`, so it learns nothing about the private machines of others ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#who-can-do-what)). For an org, the service layer reads the role of the caller in the org before the check. A caller that is not a member has no role. The check then refuses an org that does not exist in the same way as an org of others. Some changes in an org, such as a role change, lock the org first. They then read the role of the caller again, and run the check again ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#every-org-keeps-an-owner)). A member key has the role of its account, and only in the org of the key. An org key has no role. It has the rights of a member in its own org, without personal resources. So it can read its org with `org.get`, `org.get_usage`, and `org.member_list`. It can also list the shared and all values of the org with `var.list`. Only people manage keys: no key makes, lists, or deletes an API key or an admin API key. A call without an `org_id` acts in the org of its API key, or else in the personal org of the caller.

Health and reflection do not call the service layer, so the API runs the policy check for them before their handler.

An admin `session` is the `session` of an instance admin whose sign-in is at most 10 minutes old ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). The Admin area of the console calls the admin API with it. Every other `session` is refused on these actions, and so is the `cli_token` of an instance admin. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#admin-sessions) lists the calls.

A refused `anonymous` caller gets `unauthenticated` with the fixed message `this call needs a credential`, which names no action. Any other refused caller gets `permission_denied`, and the message names the caller kind and the action. One case is different. Sometimes the check refuses the `session` of an instance admin only because its sign-in is too old. The check then returns the error of a recent sign-in instead ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). That error has the detail `hopbox.v1.RecentSignInRequired`, so the console asks the person to sign in again.

## Idempotency keys

A method with the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#definitions)) runs once for each idempotency key. Today these are `KeyringService.RotateKEK`, `ServerService.CreateEnrollmentToken`, `OrgService.CreateOrg`, `AdminKeyService.CreateAdminKey`, `AdminKeyService.RegisterAdminKey`, `APIKeyService.CreateAPIKey`, `SSHKeyService.AddSSHKey`, and `MachineService.CreateMachine`. The responses of `CreateEnrollmentToken`, `CreateAdminKey`, and `CreateAPIKey` hold a secret, so the server keeps no copy of them. A replay of these methods fails with `already_exists` instead of the first response ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createenrollmenttoken)).

| Header                | Direction | Value                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Idempotency-Key`     | request   | 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters without spaces, for example a UUID. Required on an idempotent method. |
| `Idempotent-Replayed` | response  | `true` on a response that the server replayed from an earlier call. Absent on a first call.               |

The server handles an idempotent call in these steps:

1. An anonymous caller gets `unauthenticated` with the message `an idempotent call needs a credential, so that its key belongs to one caller`.
2. A call without the `Idempotency-Key` header gets `invalid_argument`.
3. The server claims the key for the caller in a transaction ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#run-an-idempotent-call)). The key covers the method and the request body, encoded as deterministic protobuf.
4. For a new key, the handler runs in the same transaction. Its change, its audit entry, the key, and the response commit together. If the handler fails, nothing commits, and a retry with the same key runs again.
5. For a known key with the same method and body, the server returns the first response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The handler does not run.
6. For a known key with another method or body, the call gets `invalid_argument`.

Each key belongs to one scope, so two callers never share a key:

| Caller                 | Scope of its keys                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `session`, `cli_token` | `account:<account ID>`. These credentials act as the account, so they share its keys.       |
| `member_key`           | `member_key:<key ID>`. Each script has its own key, so two scripts never replay each other. |
| `org_key`              | `org_key:<key ID>`                                                                          |
| `admin_key`            | `admin_key:<key ID>`                                                                        |
| `server`               | `server:<server ID>`. No method of the cluster API has the idempotent option.               |
| `local_root`           | `local_root`, one scope for every local call                                                |

The server keeps each key for 24 hours. The leader deletes the expired keys every 10 minutes ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)).

An `unavailable` error on a busy key means that the first call with the key still runs. A retry with the same key gets the result of that call, and the SDKs retry `unavailable`.

### Answers of calls that changed nothing

Some answers carry the header `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1`. The header says that the call changed nothing on the server. A client can then run the call again, also a call that changes state and has no idempotency key. The Go client and the TypeScript SDK do this for `unavailable`, `resource_exhausted`, and `deadline_exceeded` ([Go client](/reference/go-client/#retries), [TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/#retries)).

These answers carry the header:

| Answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Code                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Each refusal of the request gate: a credential that a resolver refused or failed to check, and an `Authorization` header that no resolver knows ([Request gate](#request-gate))                                                                                                                                       | `unauthenticated` or `unavailable`                       |
| Each rate limit of the table above, the rows with “Too many”. Also the limits of open access calls to the node of a machine, for one caller and for one org ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#who-can-call-them)). The service layer checks each limit before it writes, and a refused call commits nothing. | `resource_exhausted`                                     |
| An idempotency key that another call holds for more than 10 s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `unavailable`                                            |
| A refusal of an edge server for too many open requests ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#listeners))                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | HTTP 429 or 503, which a client reads as `unavailable`   |
