| An edge server that got no connection to the control role ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests))                                                                                                                                                                                                      | HTTP 502, which a client reads as `unavailable`          |
| Each refusal of maintenance mode ([Maintenance mode](#maintenance-mode))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `unavailable`, or HTTP 503 on a route that is not a call |

Every other answer can follow a call that ran, also an `unavailable` answer. An example is a sign-in link whose mail failed after the server stored the link. A usage limit, such as the most orgs of one account, carries no header, because a retry soon after gets the same refusal.

Some refusals are not answers of a call, so they carry no header:

* The WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` reports an error with a close code and a reason ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)).
* The MCP server reports the error of a tool call in the result of the tool ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#errors)).
* The limit of certificate renewals of a server answers on the control channel, not with an error of a call ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#certificate-renewal)).

```text
$ curl -si -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer hbx_unknown' -d '{}' \
    https://example.com/hopbox.v1.OrgService/ListOrgs
HTTP/2 401
hopbox-not-run: 1
...
{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"the credential is not valid"}
```

The message of an error that the service layer refuses, such as a bad domain, says which rule the request broke. Every other error gets a fixed message. So it never shows the internals of the server to a client, such as the address of the database:

| Code                  | Message                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deadline_exceeded`   | `the call ran out of time`                                                                  |
| `canceled`            | `the call was canceled`                                                                     |
| `internal`            | `internal error. The server log has the details under the request ID`                       |
| a code from a library | `the call failed with the code <code>. The server log has the details under the request ID` |

The server writes the cause of these errors only to its log, with the request ID ([Logs](#logs)).

Connect refuses some requests before any interceptor runs. Examples are a body that does not decode, a message larger than 4 MiB, and an unknown content type. These errors keep the text of Connect, such as `protocol error: incomplete envelope`, because the error mapping never sees them. Their text describes only the request, never the server. They count only in `hopbox_http_requests_total`, not in `hopbox_api_calls_total` ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/#metrics-of-the-api)). They get no `api call` log record.

### Enum names in JSON

In the JSON codec, an enum value is its full name, such as `VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE`. A request with a name that the enum does not know gets `invalid_argument`, also a name in lowercase, such as `private`. The handler never runs. The message names the field and lists the values of the enum:

```text
unmarshal message: scope is "VAR_SCOPE_PRIVAT", which is not a value of VarScope. Use one of VAR_SCOPE_SHARED, VAR_SCOPE_PRIVATE, VAR_SCOPE_ALL
```

The JSON codec of Connect drops an unknown name, and the field then holds its unspecified value. For some fields, the unspecified value is the default. Examples are the shared scope of `SetVar` and `DeleteVar`, the member kind of `CreateAPIKey`, and the restart policy `always` of `CreateMachine`. So without the check, a typo runs the call with a choice that the client did not make. The API listener, the internal listener, and the admin socket all make this check.

The JSON codec still drops an unknown field, so a client with a newer schema keeps working. The unspecified value itself, or an enum number, passes the codec. The service layer takes the unspecified value as the default of the field, or refuses it where the field has no default. It refuses a number that the enum does not know. The binary protobuf codec carries numbers, not names, so it needs no such check.

The check runs in the codec, before the request gate, as for any body that does not decode. So an anonymous call with an unknown name gets `invalid_argument`, not `unauthenticated`. The same call with a known name gets `unauthenticated`. The refusal counts only in `hopbox_http_requests_total`, as the paragraph “Connect refuses some requests before any interceptor runs” in [Errors](#errors) says.

### When a listener stops

When a listener stops, it lets each running unary call finish. A unary call that still reads its request body gets 2 s more for the read. Then the read fails, so a stalled upload cannot hold the stop. A lifecycle call of a machine that waits for its machine ends its wait at once. It answers with the machine as it is and `done` false ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-wait)). A stream ends at once: the server cancels its context and ends every read of its request body. So a stream that waits for the client, such as a reflection stream, ends too ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). A shutdown of the HTTP server does not track a connection that a handler took over. So the listener ends each open WebSocket itself, with the close code 1001 and the reason `the server shuts down. Connect again`. A running tool call of the MCP server ends at once, as a stream does ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#when-the-listener-stops)).

Example:

```text
$ curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:7080/hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService/GetInstallConfig
{"code":"unauthenticated","message":"this call needs a credential"}
```

### Streams and their credential

The gate checks the credential of a call once, at its start. A stream can run for hours, so it checks its credential again while it runs. `Service.GuardStream` of `internal/service` gives each stream a context. The context ends with the credential:

* At the expiry of the credential ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/)). For a session, that is the end of its lifetime, or 7 days after its last use, whichever comes first ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/)). For a CLI token, it is the end of the newest live access token of its CLI sign-in. So a stream lives on while the CLI refreshes its tokens. For an API key, it is the expiry of the key.
* At the first check that finds the credential ended. Examples are a sign-out of a session, and the end of a CLI sign-in. The reuse of an old refresh token ends a CLI sign-in too, with its whole family. Others are the revoke of an API key, the leave of the account of a member key from its org, and an expiry. The check runs every 30 s (`service.DefaultCredentialRecheck`). A check that cannot reach the control store keeps the stream. It logs `the check of the credential of a stream failed` at level warn with `component=service` and `err`, and tries again at the next check.

The stream then ends with `unauthenticated` and the message `the credential of this stream ended. Sign in again: ...`. `WatchMachines`, `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`, and the WebSocket of exec run under such a guard. A session, a CLI token, a member key, and an org key can hold a stream. Any other kind of caller gets `unauthenticated` at once.

## Maintenance mode

Maintenance mode stops every change of the install through the API and the control channels, so that `hopboxd admin db export` can copy a control store that no longer changes ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-maintenance-on)). It is a flag of the install config ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#install_config)). Only root on a control server turns it on or off, with `SetMaintenance` on the admin socket ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)). The code is in `internal/api/maintenance.go` and `internal/service/maintenance.go`.

In maintenance mode, every listener of the control role refuses each call that can change the control store: the API listener, the admin socket, and the internal listener, also for the requests that the edge servers forward. The maintenance gate sorts each call into one of three kinds:

* A call of gRPC health or of gRPC reflection ([Reflection and health](#reflection-and-health)), and `SetMaintenance`, pass as they are. The policy lets only `local_root` call `SetMaintenance`, so the admin socket always takes it. No other write could turn maintenance mode off.
* A call whose method has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#hopboxv1read_only)) runs as a read call. Each write that it makes runs under the maintenance mode of the process, such as its audit entry, or the last use of a machine for its auto-delete timeout. In maintenance mode, the call fails at that write, before the write, with the refusal below. A read call that writes nothing works in maintenance mode.
* Every other call is refused before the request gate, so it reads no credential and changes nothing.

So these calls work in maintenance mode:

| Service                                | Calls                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `hopbox.v1.InstallService`             | `GetInstallInfo`                                                         |
| `hopbox.v1.AccountService`             | `GetAccount`, `ListSignInMethods`, `ListCLISignIns`                      |
| `hopbox.v1.AuditService`               | `ListAuditEntries`                                                       |
| `hopbox.v1.APIKeyService`              | `ListAPIKeys`                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.MachineService`             | `GetMachine`, `ListMachines`, `ListMachineSizes`, `WatchMachines`        |
| `hopbox.v1.OrgService`                 | `GetOrg`, `ListOrgs`, `GetOrgUsage`, `ListOrgMembers`, `ListInvitations` |
| `hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService`              | `ListSSHKeys`                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.VarService`                 | `ListVars`                                                               |
| `hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService` | `SetMaintenance`                                                         |
| gRPC health and reflection             | every call                                                               |

Each other call is refused, also these reads: every read of the admin API, such as `GetInstallConfig` and `ListServers`, because it writes its audit entry ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/)), and `Download` and `StreamMachineLogs`, because each records a use of its machine. Their node channels are closed in maintenance mode anyway. The audit log thus never loses an access that it would have recorded.

Each refusal changes nothing. It has the code `unavailable`, the message `the install is in maintenance mode, so it takes only reads. Retry later`, and the headers `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1` and `Retry-After: 30`:

```text
$ curl -si -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"ann@example.org"}' \
    https://example.com/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RequestMagicLink
HTTP/2 503
hopbox-not-run: 1
retry-after: 30
...
{"code":"unavailable","message":"the install is in maintenance mode, so it takes only reads. Retry later"}
```

The plain HTTP routes that can change the install answer HTTP 503 with the same headers and message: the sign-in with GitHub and Google at `/auth/<provider>/start` and `/auth/<provider>/callback` ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/)), the sign-in of private machine URLs at `/auth/machine` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)), and the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec`. The console, health, and the MCP endpoint keep serving. Each tool of the MCP server calls the API, so it gets the refusal of its call.

The last use of a session, an API key, an admin API key, or a CLI token is a write of the request gate too, but a lost time of a last use is harmless. So in maintenance mode, the request gate skips that write, and the call goes on ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#lifetimes)).

A read call can run while maintenance mode turns on. Each of its writes either ends before `SetMaintenance` returns, or is refused before it changes anything. So no write of a read call comes after the turn to on either. A stream such as `Download` that runs at the turn ends at its next record of the use of its machine.

When maintenance mode turns on, the control process ends each call without the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)` that still runs: the unary calls, the streams such as `Exec`, and the control channels of the servers ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#maintenance-mode)). A call that maintenance mode ended gets `unavailable` with the message `the install went into maintenance mode, which ended this call. Retry later`, and no `Hopbox-Not-Run` header, because it can have changed something before its end. The leader also pauses its jobs ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)). A turn to on with `SetMaintenance` succeeds only after each of these ended in every live control process of the install while maintenance mode stayed on, so no change of the API or of a server comes after it. The other control processes report this in their rows of `control_processes` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)). The call gives up with `unavailable` after at most 30 s, the deadline of the call, and maintenance mode stays on. If maintenance mode turns off during the wait, for example by a second root on the socket, the turn to on fails with `unavailable: unavailable: maintenance mode turned off while it waited for the calls, control channels, and leader jobs to end`, because the work runs again. `hopboxd admin db export` also reads the flag in the snapshot of its dump, and refuses a store out of maintenance mode.

The request gate checks a server certificate on the internal listener, also for health and reflection. The first use of a certificate, which retires the other certificates of its server, and the alarm of a retired certificate write to the store. In maintenance mode, the gate refuses such a call with the refusal above, before the write ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)).

When maintenance mode turns off, the listeners take every call again, the servers dial their control channels again, and the leader runs its jobs again. Each control process reads the flag at its start, and again at each change event `install.maintenance_changed` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#events)). So a control process that starts on a store in maintenance mode, such as a copy of `hopboxd admin db export`, starts in maintenance mode too.

## Reflection and health

gRPC server reflection is on, so `grpcurl` can list and call the services. The server serves the reflection services `grpc.reflection.v1.ServerReflection` and `grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection`. They list the services of their listener.

The health service is `grpc.health.v1.Health`, with the methods `Check` and `Watch`. A check can name the whole server, with an empty service name, or one service of the listener. It returns `SERVING` while the control store answers a ping within 2 s, and `NOT_SERVING` otherwise. A check of an unknown service gets `not_found`. `Watch` sends the status at once. Then it checks again every 5 s, and sends the status each time that it changes. Each listener serves at most 64 open `Watch` calls. One more gets `resource_exhausted`.

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 list
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 grpc.health.v1.Health/Check
```

## InstallService

`hopbox.v1.InstallService` describes the install to a client before it signs in. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/).

### GetInstallInfo

`GetInstallInfo` returns the facts that a client needs before its first call. It needs no credential. It has no side effects, so the Connect protocol also serves it with HTTP GET.

| Item              | Value                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo` |
| Policy action     | `install.get_info`, every caller           |
| Idempotent option | no                                         |
| Audit entry       | none                                       |

The request `GetInstallInfoRequest` has no fields. The response `GetInstallInfoResponse` has these fields:

| Field             | Type                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `domain`          | string                  | The domain of the install, for example `example.com`. It is empty until an instance admin sets it with `UpdateInstallConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#updateinstallconfig)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `sign_in_methods` | repeated `SignInMethod` | The sign-in methods that anyone can use on the install ([the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/#signinmethod)). `SIGN_IN_METHOD_EMAIL_LINK` is in the list while the install has an SMTP config ([SMTP config](/reference/smtp/)) or the file mail transport ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GITHUB` and `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GOOGLE` are in it while the install has a domain and the client of the provider ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#config)). The first-admin login link is never in it, because only root can make one. |
| `ssh_host_key`    | string                  | The public host key of the SSH front door, in the `authorized_keys` format, for example `ssh-ed25519 AAAA...`. The edge servers show it on every SSH port ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#keys)). It is empty until a control process made the keys of the front door, which needs a key-encryption key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `version`         | string                  | The version of `hopboxd` on the server that answered, for example `v0.1.0` ([the version command](/reference/version/#version-format)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `mail_to_files`   | bool                    | `true` on a dev or test install with the file mail transport ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). Then no magic link or invitation reaches its recipient by email. The console uses it to tell the person to ask the operator for the link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, so an empty `domain` does not appear.

Example with the Connect protocol and HTTP GET:

```text
$ curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge \
    'http://127.0.0.1:7080/hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo?encoding=json&message=%7B%7D'
{"domain":"example.com","version":"v0.1.0"}
```

Example with gRPC:

```sh
grpcurl -plaintext 127.0.0.1:7080 hopbox.v1.InstallService/GetInstallInfo
```

## Logs

The API writes these records with `component=api`. The access log record covers every call, also refused ones.

| Message                       | Level | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `api call`                    | info  | `procedure`, `protocol`, `peer`, `caller`, `code`, `duration`, and `request_id`. `protocol` is `connect`, `grpc`, `grpcweb`, or `websocket` for the WebSocket endpoint of exec. `peer` is the address of the client, empty on the admin socket. `code` is `ok` or the error code. `caller` is the caller kind, or `unresolved` after the gate refused the credential. A call of a tool of the MCP server also has `mcp_request_id`, the request ID of its MCP request ([the MCP server](/reference/mcp/#logs)). |
| `api call failed`             | error | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For an `internal` error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `api call failed`             | warn  | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For a Connect error from a library, which keeps its code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `api call stopped`            | info  | `procedure`, `err`, `request_id`. For `deadline_exceeded` and `canceled`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `api credential refused`      | info  | `err`, `request_id`. A resolver refused a credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `api credential check failed` | error | `err`, `request_id`. A resolver failed to check a credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `machine URL sign-in failed`  | error | `err`, `request_id`. `GET /auth/machine` failed with `500` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#answers-of-authmachine)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `websocket upgrade failed`    | info  | `path`, `err`, `request_id`. The upgrade of a request to the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws/exec` failed ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#the-websocket-endpoint)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The HTTP server writes its own errors, such as a protocol error of a client, at level warn with `component=http`.

# The sign-in, account, and audit API

> The sign-in, account, audit, API key, and SSH key calls of the public API: AuthService with the device flow, AccountService, AuditService, APIKeyService, and SSHKeyService, with their audit entries.

These services of the public API `hopbox.v1` sign people in to the console and the hopbox CLI. They also manage the account of the caller with its API keys and SSH keys, and read the audit log. [The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, and the error codes. [Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/) covers the session cookie, the check against cross-site requests, the links, and the rate limits. [Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/) covers the sign-in with GitHub and Google, which runs on browser endpoints, not on calls of this API. [CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/) covers the device flow, CLI tokens, API keys, and SSH keys. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/).

| Service                    | Calls                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox.v1.AuthService`    | `RequestMagicLink`, `VerifyMagicLink`, `VerifyLoginLink`, `SignOut`, `StartDeviceAuthorization`, `GetDeviceAuthorization`, `ApproveDevice`, `PollDeviceAuthorization`, `RefreshCLIToken` |
| `hopbox.v1.AccountService` | `GetAccount`, `UpdateAccount`, `DeleteAccount`, `ListSignInMethods`, `RemoveSignInMethod`, `ListCLISignIns`, `EndCLISignIn`                                                              |
| `hopbox.v1.AuditService`   | `ListAuditEntries`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `hopbox.v1.APIKeyService`  | `CreateAPIKey`, `ListAPIKeys`, `RevokeAPIKey`                                                                                                                                            |
| `hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService`  | `AddSSHKey`, `ListSSHKeys`, `RemoveSSHKey`                                                                                                                                               |

A call with the session cookie must carry the header `Origin` with the origin of the install, and the header `Connect-Protocol-Version: 1` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie)). The examples on this page use curl against a laptop install with the domain `example.com`, as in [First sign-in on a new install](/guide/first-sign-in/). Each example of a call with the cookie uses these shell variables:

```sh
API=http://127.0.0.1:7080
COOKIE='__Host-hopbox_session=<token>'
browser() {
  curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Connect-Protocol-Version: 1' \
    -H 'Origin: https://example.com' -H "Cookie: $COOKIE" "$@"
}
```

## Messages

### Account

| Field             | Type                        | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`              | string                      | The UUID of the account.                                                    |
| `display_name`    | string                      | The name that the person chose. It can be empty.                            |
| `emails`          | repeated `AccountEmail`     | The emails of the account.                                                  |
| `instance_admin`  | bool                        | `true` for an instance admin.                                               |
| `personal_org_id` | string                      | The UUID of the personal org of the account.                                |
| `version`         | int64                       | The version of the account. It starts at 1 and grows by 1 with each change. |
| `create_time`     | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the first sign-in.                                              |

### AccountEmail

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`       | string                      | The address, in lower case.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `verified`    | bool                        | `true` for an email that a sign-in method proved. Only a verified email links other sign-in methods to the account, and only while the account has no identity of GitHub or Google ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). The email of a login link stays unverified, until a link from a session proves it ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)). |
| `verify_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the proof. It is unset for an email that is not verified.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### SignInMethod

The enum `SignInMethod` names a kind of sign-in. `GetInstallInfo` lists the kinds that anyone can use ([the API server](/reference/api/#getinstallinfo)).

| Value                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                | In `GetInstallInfo`                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SIGN_IN_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response.                                                                                                                                   | never                                                                                                      |
| `SIGN_IN_METHOD_EMAIL_LINK`  | A magic link that hopbox sends by email.                                                                                                               | while the install has an SMTP config or the file mail transport ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)) |
| `SIGN_IN_METHOD_LOGIN_LINK`  | A first-admin login link that root prints.                                                                                                             | never, because only root can make one                                                                      |
| `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GITHUB`      | A sign-in with the GitHub OAuth app of the install ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/)). A browser starts it at `/auth/github/start`. | while the install has a domain and a GitHub client                                                         |
| `SIGN_IN_METHOD_GOOGLE`      | A sign-in with the Google OAuth client of the install, through OpenID Connect. A browser starts it at `/auth/google/start`.                            | while the install has a domain and a Google client                                                         |

### LinkedSignInMethod

| Field           | Type                        | Description                                        |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | string                      | The UUID of the method on this account.            |
| `method`        | `SignInMethod`              | The kind of sign-in.                               |
| `email`         | string                      | The email that the method names.                   |
| `last_use_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the last sign-in with the method.      |
| `create_time`   | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the link of the method to the account. |

### DeviceAuthorizationState

The enum `DeviceAuthorizationState` is the answer of `PollDeviceAuthorization`.

| Value                                    | Meaning                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response.                                                                                                  |
| `DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_PENDING`     | Nobody approved the code yet. Poll again after `interval_seconds`.                                                    |
| `DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_SLOW_DOWN`   | The poll came less than the interval after the poll before. The interval grew by 5 s, and holds for every later poll. |
| `DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_APPROVED`    | A person approved the code. The response holds the CLI tokens.                                                        |

### CLITokens

The tokens of a CLI sign-in ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). The install keeps only their hashes.

| Field                       | Type                        | Description                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `access_token`              | string                      | Starts with `hbxat_`. It goes in the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. |
| `access_token_expire_time`  | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the access token, 1 hour after its issue.                         |
| `refresh_token`             | string                      | Starts with `hbxrt_`. It works once, with `RefreshCLIToken`.                 |
| `refresh_token_expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the refresh token, 30 days after its issue.                       |
| `account_id`                | string                      | The UUID of the account of the tokens.                                       |
| `cli_sign_in_id`            | string                      | The UUID of the CLI sign-in. Every refresh keeps it.                         |

### RecentSignInRequired

The detail of the `permission_denied` error of a call that needs a recent sign-in, such as `ApproveDevice` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). A client reads it without parsing the message. The console then sends the person to sign in again.

| Field     | Type                       | Description                                                        |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `max_age` | `google.protobuf.Duration` | How long a session counts as recent after its sign-in: 10 minutes. |

### APIKey

An API key without its secret ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)).

| Field                | Type                        | Description                                                                        |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                 | string                      | The UUID of the key.                                                               |
| `org_id`             | string                      | The UUID of the org of the key.                                                    |
| `kind`               | `APIKeyKind`                | `API_KEY_KIND_MEMBER` or `API_KEY_KIND_ORG`.                                       |
| `name`               | string                      | The name that its creator gave the key, such as `ci`.                              |
| `account_id`         | string                      | The UUID of the account of a member key. Empty for an org key.                     |
| `creator_account_id` | string                      | The UUID of the account that made the key. Empty after the delete of that account. |
| `expire_time`        | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the key.                                                                |
| `last_use_time`      | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The last call with the key, exact to a minute. Unset for a key without a call.     |
| `create_time`        | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The creation of the key.                                                           |

The enum `APIKeyKind` has the values `API_KEY_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`, which a request takes as a member key, `API_KEY_KIND_MEMBER`, and `API_KEY_KIND_ORG`. The enum `APIKeyLifetime` has the values `API_KEY_LIFETIME_UNSPECIFIED` (90 days), `API_KEY_LIFETIME_30_DAYS`, `API_KEY_LIFETIME_90_DAYS`, and `API_KEY_LIFETIME_365_DAYS`.

### SSHKey

A public key of an account ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#ssh-keys)).

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | string                      | The UUID of the key.                                                                      |
| `name`        | string                      | The name of the key, such as `ann@laptop`. It can be empty.                               |
| `type`        | string                      | The key type, such as `ssh-ed25519`.                                                      |
| `bits`        | int32                       | The size of the key: 256 for Ed25519, the curve size for ECDSA, the modulus size for RSA. |
| `public_key`  | string                      | The key in the `authorized_keys` form, without its comment.                               |
| `fingerprint` | string                      | The SHA-256 fingerprint, as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it.                                    |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The addition of the key.                                                                  |

## AuthService

### RequestMagicLink

Sends a sign-in link to an email ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#magic-links)). It answers the same for an email with or without an account, so the call tells nothing about who has an account. With `link`, it sends a link that adds the email as a sign-in method of the account of the session instead ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RequestMagicLink`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Policy action     | `auth.request_magic_link`: `anonymous` and `session`. With `link`: `account.link_sign_in_method`, the `session` of the account, with a sign-in within the last 10 minutes ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). |
| Idempotent option | no. Each call sends a new link.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Audit entry       | action `auth.request_magic_link`, actor the caller, target kind `magic_link`, target ID the UUID of the link, details `email` and `client_ip`. With `link`, also `purpose` with the value `link`.                                                        |

The request `RequestMagicLinkRequest` has these fields. The response `RequestMagicLinkResponse` has no fields.

| Field   | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email` | string | The address that gets the link, such as `ann@example.org`. The server takes the email in lower case, without spaces around it ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#emails)). |
| `link`  | bool   | `true` for a link that adds the email to the account of the session. Only that session can use the link. The email has the subject `Add your email to your account on <domain>`. |

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Code                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The email breaks a rule, such as `Ann <ann@example.org>`                                                                                                                                                        | `invalid_argument`    |
| `link` without a session: `this call needs a credential`                                                                                                                                                        | `unauthenticated`     |
| `link` with a caller that is not a session, such as a CLI token                                                                                                                                                 | `permission_denied`   |
| `link` with an email that the account signs in with already. The call sends no mail.                                                                                                                            | `already_exists`      |
| `link` with a session whose sign-in is more than 10 minutes old: `permission denied: this action needs a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. Sign in again, then retry`, with the detail `RecentSignInRequired` | `permission_denied`   |
| The install has no SMTP config and the transport `smtp`: `failed precondition: this install has no SMTP config, so it sends no sign-in links`                                                                   | `failed_precondition` |
| The install has no domain                                                                                                                                                                                       | `failed_precondition` |
| The SMTP password does not open, for example after the loss of its key-encryption key                                                                                                                           | `internal`            |
| A rate limit ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits))                                                                                                                         | `resource_exhausted`  |
| The SMTP server failed, or the file transport failed to write the file: `unavailable: the server failed to send the email. Retry later`                                                                         | `unavailable`         |

The server logs the cause of a failed email as `the magic link email failed`, at level error, with `component=service` and `err`. With the file mail transport, the call writes the email to a file on the server and sends nothing ([Mail](/reference/mail/#the-file-transport)). A rate limit applies first ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits)).

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"ann@example.org"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RequestMagicLink
```

```json
{}
```

A link of an email to the account of the session:

```sh
browser -d '{"email":"ann.work@example.org","link":true}' $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RequestMagicLink
```

### VerifyMagicLink

Signs in with the token of a magic link, and sets the session cookie ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). The link works once, within 15 minutes. The token of a link from `RequestMagicLink` with `link` adds the email to the account of the session that asked for it, and sets no cookie ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/VerifyMagicLink`                                                                                                     |
| Policy action     | `auth.verify_magic_link`: `anonymous` and `session`                                                                                          |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                           |
| Audit entries     | `account.create` for a new account, then `auth.sign_in` ([Audit entries](#audit-entries)). A link writes only `account.link_sign_in_method`. |

The request `VerifyMagicLinkRequest` has the field `token`, a string: the value after `#token=` in the link. The response `VerifyMagicLinkResponse` has these fields, and the header `Set-Cookie` with the session cookie. A link has no `Set-Cookie`.

| Field                 | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `account`             | `Account`                   | The account of the new session, or the account that the link added the email to.                                                |
| `new_account`         | bool                        | `true` for an account that this sign-in created.                                                                                |
| `session_expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the session, 30 days after the sign-in. After 7 days without a call, the session ends before that. Unset for a link. |
| `linked`              | bool                        | `true` when the link added its email to the account of the session. No new session starts, and the session cookie stays.        |

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| The call does not carry the `Origin` of the install and the Connect protocol header. The link stays unused.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `permission_denied`   |
| The token is unknown, used, or expired: `the sign-in link is not valid: it is unknown, used, or expired. Ask for a new link`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `unauthenticated`     |
| The account of the email has GitHub or Google, and no email method for this email ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)): `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: the account of ann@example.org signs in with GitHub or Google, so a new sign-in method joins it only through a link. ...` | `failed_precondition` |
| A link, and the caller is not the session that asked for it. The link stays unused: `permission denied: this link adds an email to the account of the session that asked for it. Open it in the browser where you asked for it, while you are signed in there`                                                                                               | `permission_denied`   |
| A link, and another account signs in with the email: `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: this email ann.work@example.org signs in to another account. Remove it from that account first`                                                                                                                                            | `failed_precondition` |
| A link, and another account holds the email as verified: `the sign-in conflicts with a sign-in method of the account: the email kim@example.org is a verified email of another account, so it signs in only to that account`                                                                                                                                 | `failed_precondition` |
| A link, and the account has the email method already                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | `already_exists`      |
| A link, and the session that asked for it ended: `this call needs a credential: the session that started the link ended. Sign in again, then link the method again`                                                                                                                                                                                          | `unauthenticated`     |

### VerifyLoginLink

Signs in with the token of a first-admin login link, and sets the session cookie. The link works once, within 15 minutes. It reaches the account of earlier login links for the same email, or a new account, and makes that account an instance admin. The email stays unverified ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/VerifyLoginLink`                                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `auth.verify_login_link`: `anonymous` and `session`                                                                              |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                               |
| Audit entries     | `account.create` for a new account, `auth.sign_in`, and `instance_admin.grant` for an account that was not an instance admin yet |

The request `VerifyLoginLinkRequest` has the field `token`. The response `VerifyLoginLinkResponse` has the fields of `VerifyMagicLinkResponse`, and the header `Set-Cookie` with the session cookie. The errors are those of `VerifyMagicLink`.

```sh
curl -s -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Connect-Protocol-Version: 1' \
  -H 'Origin: https://example.com' -d '{"token":"<token>"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/VerifyLoginLink
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Hopbox-Request-Id: 01a143f9-1cee-7170-bd72-5ceae51d8bc8
Set-Cookie: __Host-hopbox_session=6s6pHx8zxuTK_v6pj2KCmDxYvkEWEgE5hqOBhfvXs_c; Path=/; Expires=Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:09:21 GMT; Max-Age=2591999; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax


{"account":{"id":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6", "emails":[{"email":"root@example.org"}], "instanceAdmin":true, "personalOrgId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec1-a648-71fea47ae54f", "version":"1", "createTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z"}, "newAccount":true, "sessionExpireTime":"2026-11-15T09:09:21.774252Z"}
```

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, so the unverified email has no `verified` field.

### SignOut

Ends the session of the caller and clears the session cookie.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/SignOut`                                                                                                                                              |
| Policy action     | `auth.sign_out`: `session` and `cli_token`                                                                                                                                    |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | action `auth.sign_out`, org the personal org, target kind `session` and the UUID of the session. With a CLI token, target kind `cli_sign_in` and the UUID of the CLI sign-in. |

The request `SignOutRequest` and the response `SignOutResponse` have no fields. The response has the header `Set-Cookie` with `Max-Age=0`. The sign-out of a session also deletes the tokens of the private machine URLs that the session made, and publishes the change event `edge.access_changed`. So each edge server checks the machine URLs of the browser again ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)).

```sh
browser -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/SignOut
```

### StartDeviceAuthorization

Starts the device flow of the hopbox CLI ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#the-device-flow)). It needs no credential. The CLI shows the user code and the verification URI, then polls with the device code.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/StartDeviceAuthorization`                                                                                             |
| Policy action     | `auth.start_device_authorization`: every caller, also `anonymous`. The device code is the credential of the flow.                             |
| Idempotent option | no. Each call starts a new device sign-in.                                                                                                    |
| Audit entry       | action `auth.start_device_authorization`, actor the caller, no org, target kind `device_authorization`, details `client_name` and `client_ip` |

The request `StartDeviceAuthorizationRequest` has the field `client_name`, a string such as `hopbox CLI on ann-laptop`. It has at most 64 characters, and can be empty ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#credential-names)). The console shows it at the approval. The response `StartDeviceAuthorizationResponse` has these fields:

| Field                       | Type                        | Description                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `device_code`               | string                      | The secret with which the CLI polls: 43 characters of base64url. The CLI must not show it. |
| `user_code`                 | string                      | The code that the person types in the console, such as `QJTL-PHNV`.                        |
| `verification_uri`          | string                      | The console page that approves the code: `https://<domain>/device`.                        |
| `verification_uri_complete` | string                      | The same page with the code in it: `https://<domain>/device?code=<user_code>`.             |
| `expire_time`               | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the device sign-in, 10 minutes after its start.                                 |
| `interval_seconds`          | int32                       | The least time between two polls: 5.                                                       |

| Error                                                                                                                                 | Code                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The client name breaks a rule                                                                                                         | `invalid_argument`    |
| The install has no domain: `failed precondition: the install has no domain, and the console page that approves the sign-in needs one` | `failed_precondition` |
| A limit of starts ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#limits-of-the-device-flow))           | `resource_exhausted`  |

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"clientName":"hopbox CLI on ann-laptop"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/StartDeviceAuthorization
```

```json
{"deviceCode":"<device code>","userCode":"QJTL-PHNV","verificationUri":"https://example.com/device","verificationUriComplete":"https://example.com/device?code=QJTL-PHNV","expireTime":"2026-10-16T17:24:56.701147Z","intervalSeconds":5}
```

### GetDeviceAuthorization

Returns the client that waits for a user code. The console page `/device` calls it first and shows the client name, the IP address, and the start time to the person. Only then does the person approve. Without this step, a person who got a code from someone else can sign that party in to their own account (RFC 8628 section 5.4).

| Item              | Value                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/GetDeviceAuthorization` |
| Policy action     | `auth.get_device_authorization`: `session` only |
| Idempotent option | no                                              |
| Audit entry       | none                                            |

The request `GetDeviceAuthorizationRequest` has the field `user_code`, a string. Case, dashes, and spaces do not matter. The response `GetDeviceAuthorizationResponse` has these fields:

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                                     |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client_name` | string                      | The name that the CLI gave at its start.                        |
| `client_ip`   | string                      | The IP address that started the device sign-in, or empty.       |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The start of the device sign-in. `ApproveDevice` needs it back. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The end of the device sign-in.                                  |

The errors are those of `ApproveDevice`, apart from the refusal of an old sign-in. The lookup takes a session of any age. A wrong code counts against the limit of wrong codes of the account.

```sh
browser -d '{"userCode":"QJTL-PHNV"}' $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/GetDeviceAuthorization
```

```json
{"clientName":"hopbox CLI on ann-laptop","clientIp":"127.0.0.1","createTime":"2026-10-16T17:14:56.701147Z","expireTime":"2026-10-16T17:24:56.701147Z"}
```

### ApproveDevice

Approves a user code for the account of the session. The console page `/device` calls it after `GetDeviceAuthorization`, with the start time that the lookup showed. The next poll of the CLI then gets CLI tokens of that account.

The session needs a recent sign-in: at most 10 minutes old ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). The approval makes a CLI sign-in whose refresh token lives 30 days and renews with each use. So without this rule, someone who takes over an old session can make a CLI sign-in that outlives the session.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/ApproveDevice`                                                                                        |
| Policy action     | `auth.approve_device`: `session` only. A CLI token or a key never approves a device.                                          |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                            |
| Audit entry       | action `auth.approve_device`, org the personal org, target kind `device_authorization`, details `client_name` and `client_ip` |

The request `ApproveDeviceRequest` has these fields:

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `user_code`   | string                      | The code that the CLI shows. Case, dashes, and spaces do not matter.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The `create_time` of `GetDeviceAuthorizationResponse` for the code. The approval fails unless it matches, so the console approves only a client that it showed. The time has microsecond precision, so the console passes it back unchanged and never rounds it. |

The response `ApproveDeviceResponse` has these fields:

| Field         | Type                        | Description                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `client_name` | string                      | The name that the CLI gave at its start.                  |
| `client_ip`   | string                      | The IP address that started the device sign-in, or empty. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The start of the device sign-in.                          |

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Code                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The call carries no session cookie, or the cookie call fails the check against cross-site requests ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#calls-with-the-cookie))                                                                                                                  | `unauthenticated`     |
| A CLI token or a key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `permission_denied`   |
| The sign-in of the session is more than 10 minutes old: `permission denied: this action needs a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. Sign in again, then retry`. The error has the detail [`RecentSignInRequired`](#recentsigninrequired). It does not count as a wrong code, and the code keeps waiting. | `permission_denied`   |
| No device sign-in waits for the code: it is wrong, approved already, or expired, also between the lookup and the approval. `not found: no device sign-in waits for this code. Check the code in the terminal, or start the sign-in again`. The wrong code counts against the limit of the account.       | `not_found`           |
| The `create_time` does not match the device sign-in of the code: `failed precondition: the start time does not match the device sign-in of this code. Look the code up again, check the client, then approve it`. It counts as a wrong code.                                                             | `failed_precondition` |
| The account entered 10 wrong codes in the last hour ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#limits-of-the-device-flow))                                                                                                                                            | `resource_exhausted`  |

```sh
browser -d '{"userCode":"QJTL-PHNV","createTime":"2026-10-16T17:14:56.701147Z"}' $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/ApproveDevice
```

```json
{"clientName":"hopbox CLI on ann-laptop","clientIp":"127.0.0.1","createTime":"2026-10-16T17:14:56.701147Z"}
```

The same call with a session whose sign-in is more than 10 minutes old gets HTTP status 403:

```json
{"code":"permission_denied","message":"permission denied: this action needs a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. Sign in again, then retry","details":[{"type":"hopbox.v1.RecentSignInRequired","value":"CgMI2AQ","debug":{"maxAge":"600s"}}]}
```

### PollDeviceAuthorization

Asks whether a person approved the device code. The first poll after the approval starts a CLI sign-in and returns its tokens, once.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/PollDeviceAuthorization`                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Policy action     | `auth.poll_device_authorization`: every caller, also `anonymous`. The device code is the credential.                                                                                                                         |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Audit entry       | for the poll that takes the tokens: action `auth.sign_in` by the new CLI sign-in, actor kind `cli_token`. Org the personal org, target kind `cli_sign_in`. Details `method` (`device`), `client_name`, and `device_sign_in`. |

The request `PollDeviceAuthorizationRequest` has the field `device_code`, a string. The response `PollDeviceAuthorizationResponse` has these fields:

| Field              | Type                       | Description                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `state`            | `DeviceAuthorizationState` | The answer of the poll ([DeviceAuthorizationState](#deviceauthorizationstate)).                              |
| `interval_seconds` | int32                      | The least time until the next poll.                                                                          |
| `tokens`           | `CLITokens`                | The tokens of the new CLI sign-in, for `DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_APPROVED` only ([CLITokens](#clitokens)). |

| Error                                                                                                                                                      | Code                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The device code is unknown or malformed, or a poll took its tokens already: `the device code is not valid: it is unknown or used. Start the sign-in again` | `unauthenticated`     |
| The device code expired: `failed precondition: the device code expired before its approval. Start the sign-in again`                                       | `failed_precondition` |

Two polls at the same time run one after the other, so only one of them gets the tokens.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"deviceCode":"<device code>"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/PollDeviceAuthorization
```

```json
{"state":"DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION_STATE_PENDING","intervalSeconds":5}
```

### RefreshCLIToken

Trades a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token of the same CLI sign-in. Each refresh token works once. A replaced refresh token that comes back ends the whole CLI sign-in ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). The one exception is a race of two refreshes: the newest replaced token works once more within 10 s.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RefreshCLIToken`                                                                                                        |
| Policy action     | `auth.refresh_cli_token`: every caller, also `anonymous`. The refresh token is the credential.                                                  |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                              |
| Audit entry       | none for a refresh. A reuse writes `auth.end_cli_sign_in` with the detail `reason` (`refresh token reuse`), in the personal org of the account. |

The request `RefreshCLITokenRequest` has the field `refresh_token`, the newest refresh token of the CLI sign-in. The response `RefreshCLITokenResponse` has the field `tokens`, a `CLITokens` with the same `cli_sign_in_id`. Send no `Authorization` header: an expired access token in it fails the call before the refresh.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                        | Code              |
