| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| The refresh token is unknown, malformed, replaced, expired, or of a CLI sign-in that ended: `the refresh token is not valid: it is unknown, used, or expired. Sign in again` | `unauthenticated` |

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"refreshToken":"hbxrt_<token>"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.AuthService/RefreshCLIToken
```

```json
{"tokens":{"accessToken":"hbxat_<token>","accessTokenExpireTime":"2026-10-16T18:15:15.785548Z","refreshToken":"hbxrt_<token>","refreshTokenExpireTime":"2026-11-15T17:15:15.785548Z","accountId":"01a145b5-ad29-70a3-9065-fc2498a5d006","cliSignInId":"01a145b5-d8d5-71a9-a7ea-4d5f0c7a43f1"}}
```

## AccountService

Each call of `AccountService` acts on the account of the session or the CLI token that calls it. Another caller, even an instance admin, cannot reach the account. A member key can read the account that it acts as, with `GetAccount`, but it cannot change it. An org key has no account.

### GetAccount

Returns the account of the caller.

| Item              | Value                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/GetAccount`                                    |
| Policy action     | `account.get`: the `session`, `cli_token`, or `member_key` of the account |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                        |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                      |

The request `GetAccountRequest` has no fields. The response `GetAccountResponse` has the field `account`, an `Account`.

```sh
browser -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.AccountService/GetAccount
```

```json
{"account":{"id":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6", "emails":[{"email":"root@example.org"}], "instanceAdmin":true, "personalOrgId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec1-a648-71fea47ae54f", "version":"1", "createTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z"}}
```

### UpdateAccount

Changes the fields that the request sets, and keeps the others. It returns the account after the change.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/UpdateAccount`                                                                           |
| Policy action     | `account.update`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account                                                       |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                  |
| Audit entry       | action `account.update`, org the personal org, target kind `account`, details `display_name` and `old_display_name` |

| Field              | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `display_name`     | optional string | The new display name ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#display-names)). Leave it out to keep the name.                                 |
| `expected_version` | optional int64  | The `version` of the account that the caller read. If the account has another version now, the call fails with `aborted` and changes nothing. |

A request that sets no field gets `invalid_argument` with the message `invalid argument: the update sets no field`. The response `UpdateAccountResponse` has the field `account`.

```sh
browser -d '{"displayName":"Ann Root","expectedVersion":"1"}' $API/hopbox.v1.AccountService/UpdateAccount
```

### DeleteAccount

Deletes the account, its personal org, its sessions, its emails, and its sign-in methods, and clears the session cookie. It takes the account out of each other org. In each one, it also deletes what the account made and did not share ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#what-a-member-leaves-behind)). The delete also removes the CLI sign-ins, member keys, and SSH keys of the account.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/DeleteAccount`                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `account.delete`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Audit entries     | action `account.delete`, target kind `account`, details `personal_org`. Each other org of the account gets the action `org.member_remove`, with the account as its target. Its details are `role` and `reason` (`account deleted`). The owners of the org see it. |

The request `DeleteAccountRequest` and the response `DeleteAccountResponse` have no fields.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Code                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The account is the only owner of an org other than its personal org: `failed precondition: the account is the only owner of the org "<name>" (<id>). Make another member an owner, or delete the org, first`                                                                                                           | `failed_precondition` |
| The account is the last instance admin: `failed precondition: the account is the last instance admin, and an install keeps at least one. Make another account an instance admin first`                                                                                                                                 | `failed_precondition` |
| The personal org of the account, or another org of the account, is suspended: `failed precondition: org suspended: an instance admin suspended an org of the account, and nothing deletes its data until the suspension ends. Ask for the end of the suspension first` ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#suspension)) | `failed_precondition` |

An instance admin that is not the last one loses the role with the delete. The delete locks the account, then each org of the account, before the check ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#orgs)). So two owners of one org that delete their accounts at the same time leave one owner.

### ListSignInMethods

Lists the sign-in methods of the account, oldest first.

| Item              | Value                                                                       |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/ListSignInMethods`                               |
| Policy action     | `account.list_sign_in_methods`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                          |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                        |

The request `ListSignInMethodsRequest` has no fields. The response `ListSignInMethodsResponse` has the field `methods`, a repeated `LinkedSignInMethod`.

```sh
browser -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.AccountService/ListSignInMethods
```

```json
{"methods":[{"id":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec2-8d2e-1c5d4f0b8a11", "method":"SIGN_IN_METHOD_LOGIN_LINK", "email":"root@example.org", "lastUseTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z", "createTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z"}]}
```

### RemoveSignInMethod

Removes one sign-in method of the account. An account keeps at least one. The emails of the account stay. While the account has no identity of GitHub or Google, a later sign-in that proves a verified email links its method again ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)). The removal does not end the sessions or the CLI sign-ins that the method started. End them with `SignOut` and [EndCLISignIn](#endclisignin).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/RemoveSignInMethod`                                                                         |
| Policy action     | `account.remove_sign_in_method`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account                                           |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                     |
| Audit entry       | action `account.remove_sign_in_method`, org the personal org, target kind `sign_in_method`, details `kind` and `email` |

The request `RemoveSignInMethodRequest` has the field `id`, the UUID of the method. The response `RemoveSignInMethodResponse` has no fields.

| Error                                                                                                             | Code                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| The ID is not a UUID                                                                                              | `invalid_argument`    |
| The account has no method with the ID                                                                             | `not_found`           |
| It is the last method: `failed precondition: an account keeps at least one sign-in method. Add another one first` | `failed_precondition` |

### ListCLISignIns

Lists the CLI sign-ins of the account, oldest first: each device that holds CLI tokens ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). The account finds a sign-in that is not its own here, for example one on a lost laptop.

| Item              | Value                                                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/ListCLISignIns`                            |
| Policy action     | `auth.list_cli_sign_ins`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                    |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                  |

The request `ListCLISignInsRequest` has no fields. The response `ListCLISignInsResponse` has the field `sign_ins`, a repeated `CLISignIn`:

| Field           | Type                        | Description                                                                                    |
| --------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`            | string                      | The UUID of the CLI sign-in, the `cli_sign_in_id` of its tokens.                               |
| `client_name`   | string                      | The name that the CLI gave at the start of the device flow.                                    |
| `client_ip`     | string                      | The IP address that started the device flow, or empty.                                         |
| `last_use_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The last call with an access token of the sign-in, exact to a minute.                          |
| `create_time`   | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The start of the CLI sign-in.                                                                  |
| `last_use_ip`   | string                      | The IP address of the last call with an access token of the sign-in. It starts as `client_ip`. |

```sh
browser -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.AccountService/ListCLISignIns
```

### EndCLISignIn

Ends one CLI sign-in of the account at once, with all of its tokens. Only the console calls it, so a stolen CLI token cannot end the other sign-ins of its owner. A CLI ends its own sign-in with `SignOut`.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AccountService/EndCLISignIn`                                                                                  |
| Policy action     | `auth.end_cli_sign_in`: the `session` of the account                                                                      |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                        |
| Audit entry       | action `auth.end_cli_sign_in`, org the personal org, target kind `cli_sign_in`, details `reason` (`ended by the account`) |

The request `EndCLISignInRequest` has the field `id`, the UUID of the CLI sign-in. The response `EndCLISignInResponse` has no fields.

| Error                                      | Code               |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| The ID is not a UUID                       | `invalid_argument` |
| The account has no CLI sign-in with the ID | `not_found`        |

## AuditService

### ListAuditEntries

Returns entries of the audit log ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#audit_log)), newest first. Org owners and org admins read the entries of their org. Instance admins read the entries of every org and of the whole install.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.AuditService/ListAuditEntries`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Policy action     | `audit.list_org` for one org: a `session` or `cli_token` with the role `owner` or `admin` in the org. Also a `member_key` of such an account, in the org of the key, and a `cli_token` of an instance admin. Also the `session` of an instance admin with a sign-in within the last 10 minutes. `audit.list_install` for the whole install: a `cli_token` of an instance admin, or the `session` of an instance admin with a sign-in within the last 10 minutes ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)). |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Audit entry       | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

The request `ListAuditEntriesRequest` has these fields:

| Field           | Type            | Default                                                         | Description                                                                          |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `org_id`        | optional string | the org of a member key, or else the personal org of the caller | The UUID of the org whose entries to read.                                           |
| `whole_install` | bool            | `false`                                                         | Reads the entries of every org and of the install. `org_id` must then be left out.   |
| `page_size`     | int32           | 50                                                              | The most entries in one response, 1 to 500.                                          |
| `page_token`    | string          | empty                                                           | The `next_page_token` of the response before. Leave it empty for the newest entries. |

The response `ListAuditEntriesResponse` has the fields `entries`, a repeated `AuditEntry`, and `next_page_token`. The token is empty on the last page.

| `AuditEntry` field | Type                        | Description                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`               | string                      | The UUID of the entry.                                                                              |
| `org_id`           | optional string             | The UUID of the org of the action. It is unset for an action on the whole install.                  |
| `actor`            | `AuditActor`                | `kind`, such as `session` or `local_root`, then `account_id` and `credential_id`, or empty strings. |
| `action`           | string                      | The action, such as `auth.sign_in`.                                                                 |
| `target_kind`      | string                      | The kind of object, such as `account`, or empty.                                                    |
| `target_id`        | string                      | The ID or the name of the object, or empty.                                                         |
| `details`          | map of string to string     | More facts. They never hold a secret value.                                                         |
| `request_id`       | string                      | The ID of the API request, or empty.                                                                |
| `create_time`      | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the action.                                                                             |

| Error                                                                                                                                         | Code                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A caller without the role in the org, or a member. The org can also not exist.                                                                | `permission_denied`                                                                                                                                |
| `whole_install` from a caller that is not an instance admin                                                                                   | `permission_denied`                                                                                                                                |
| A session of an instance admin whose sign-in is more than 10 minutes old, with `whole_install` or an org where it is not an owner or an admin | `permission_denied` with the detail `hopbox.v1.RecentSignInRequired` ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)) |
| `whole_install` with `org_id`                                                                                                                 | `invalid_argument`                                                                                                                                 |
| An `org_id` that is not a UUID                                                                                                                | `invalid_argument`                                                                                                                                 |
| A page size out of range                                                                                                                      | `invalid_argument`                                                                                                                                 |
| A page token that this call did not return                                                                                                    | `invalid_argument`                                                                                                                                 |

```sh
browser -d '{"wholeInstall":true,"pageSize":2}' $API/hopbox.v1.AuditService/ListAuditEntries
```

```json
{"entries":[{"id":"01a143f9-1cf1-73f3-a6ea-4a65c92b2116", "actor":{"kind":"session", "accountId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6", "credentialId":"01a143f9-1cf0-7418-a8f1-b79af67c1449"}, "action":"instance_admin.grant", "targetKind":"account", "targetId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6", "details":{"login_link":"01a143f9-0545-7bae-a957-716b4710a8c0"}, "requestId":"01a143f9-1cee-7170-bd72-5ceae51d8bc8", "createTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z"}, {"id":"01a143f9-1cf0-78f1-8413-dbe73566e206", "orgId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec1-a648-71fea47ae54f", "actor":{"kind":"session", "accountId":"01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6", "credentialId":"01a143f9-1cf0-7418-a8f1-b79af67c1449"}, "action":"auth.sign_in", "targetKind":"session", "targetId":"01a143f9-1cf0-7418-a8f1-b79af67c1449", "details":{"email":"root@example.org", "login_link":"01a143f9-0545-7bae-a957-716b4710a8c0", "method":"login_link", "new_account":"true"}, "requestId":"01a143f9-1cee-7170-bd72-5ceae51d8bc8", "createTime":"2026-10-16T09:09:21.774252Z"}], "nextPageToken":"AaFD-Rzwfviy4yXwHf2rvA"}
```

## APIKeyService

`hopbox.v1.APIKeyService` manages the API keys of an org ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). Only a `session` or a `cli_token` calls it, so no API key makes, lists, or deletes another key. The examples use the access token of a CLI sign-in:

```sh
TOKEN=hbxat_<token>
cli() { curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$@"; }
```

### CreateAPIKey

Makes an API key. Any member makes a member key for itself. The org admins and owners make org keys. The response holds the only copy of the key.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/CreateAPIKey`                                                                                                                                                        |
| Policy action     | `api_key.create`: a `session` or `cli_token` with a role in the org. A member key needs the role `member` or more. An org key needs `admin` or `owner`.                                        |
| Idempotent option | yes. The install keeps no copy of the secret. So a retry with the same idempotency key fails with `already_exists` and the ID of the key ([the API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys)). |
| Audit entry       | action `api_key.create`, org the org of the key, target kind `api_key`, details `kind`, `name`, and `expire_time`                                                                              |

The request `CreateAPIKeyRequest` has these fields:

| Field         | Type                        | Default                        | Description                                                                                             |
| ------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org_id`      | optional string             | the personal org of the caller | The UUID of the org of the key.                                                                         |
| `kind`        | `APIKeyKind`                | `API_KEY_KIND_MEMBER`          | The kind of the key.                                                                                    |
| `name`        | string                      | none, required                 | A name of 1 to 64 characters, such as `ci` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#credential-names)). |
| `lifetime`    | `APIKeyLifetime`            | 90 days                        | A preset lifetime. Give it or `expire_time`, not both.                                                  |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | none                           | A custom end, in the future and at most 365 days ahead.                                                 |

The response `CreateAPIKeyResponse` has the fields `key`, an `APIKey`, and `secret`, the key itself, which starts with `hbx_`.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Code                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| The caller is a key, or has no role or too low a role in the org. The org can also not exist.                                                                                                                                                                                                           | `permission_denied`  |
| No name, a bad name, an unknown kind or lifetime, or an expiry in the past or more than 365 days ahead: `invalid argument: the expiry date <time> must be in the future and at most 365 days ahead`. The policy check comes first, so a caller that cannot make a key gets `permission_denied` instead. | `invalid_argument`   |
| An org key in a personal org: `invalid argument: a personal org has no shared machines, so it takes no org key. Make a member key, or an org key in a team org`                                                                                                                                         | `invalid_argument`   |
| The org holds 100 API keys, expired ones included: `usage limit exceeded: an org holds at most 100 API keys. Revoke one first`                                                                                                                                                                          | `resource_exhausted` |
| A retry with an idempotency key that made a key already                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `already_exists`     |

```sh
cli -H 'Idempotency-Key: 0b2c5e1a-key-ci' -d '{"name":"ci","lifetime":"API_KEY_LIFETIME_30_DAYS"}' \
  $API/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/CreateAPIKey
```

```json
{"key":{"id":"01a145b6-1aaf-7620-989d-f244cbd2aba6","orgId":"01a145b5-ad29-70a4-becc-5f6e654b8efa","kind":"API_KEY_KIND_MEMBER","name":"ci","accountId":"01a145b5-ad29-70a3-9065-fc2498a5d006","creatorAccountId":"01a145b5-ad29-70a3-9065-fc2498a5d006","expireTime":"2026-11-15T17:15:24.718683Z","createTime":"2026-10-16T17:15:24.718683Z"},"secret":"hbx_<key>"}
```

### ListAPIKeys

Lists the API keys of an org that the caller manages, oldest first: the own member keys for a member, and every key of the org for an org admin or owner.

| Item              | Value                                                             |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/ListAPIKeys`                            |
| Policy action     | `api_key.list`: a `session` or `cli_token` with a role in the org |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                |
| Audit entry       | none                                                              |

The request `ListAPIKeysRequest` has the field `org_id`, an optional string. The default is the personal org of the caller. The response `ListAPIKeysResponse` has the field `keys`, a repeated `APIKey`. An expired key stays in the list for 30 days. Then the leader deletes it.

```sh
cli -d '{}' $API/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/ListAPIKeys
```

### RevokeAPIKey

Deletes an API key at once. A member deletes its own member keys. An org admin or owner deletes any key of the org.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/RevokeAPIKey`                                                                                                              |
| Policy action     | `api_key.revoke`: a `session` or `cli_token`. Its own member key needs the role `member` or more. Any other key of the org needs `admin` or `owner`. |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                                                   |
| Audit entry       | action `api_key.revoke`, org the org of the key, target kind `api_key`, details `kind` and `name`                                                    |

The request `RevokeAPIKeyRequest` has the field `id`, the UUID of the key. The response `RevokeAPIKeyResponse` has no fields.

| Error                                                                      | Code                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| The ID is not a UUID                                                       | `invalid_argument`  |
| No key has the ID, or the key is in an org in which the caller has no role | `not_found`         |
| A member and a key of another account, or an org key                       | `permission_denied` |

```sh
cli -d '{"id":"01a145b6-1aaf-7620-989d-f244cbd2aba6"}' $API/hopbox.v1.APIKeyService/RevokeAPIKey
```

## SSHKeyService

`hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService` manages the SSH keys of the account of the caller ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#ssh-keys)). Each call acts on the account of the `session` or the `cli_token`. A member key or an org key cannot call it, because an SSH key works in every org of its account.

### AddSSHKey

Adds a public key to the account. A key that an account of the install holds already is refused, so each key works for one account only.

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService/AddSSHKey`                                                                                 |
| Policy action     | `ssh_key.add`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account                                                           |
| Idempotent option | yes. A retry with the same idempotency key returns the first response.                                               |
| Audit entry       | action `ssh_key.add`, org the personal org, target kind `ssh_key`, details `fingerprint`, `type`, `bits`, and `name` |

The request `AddSSHKeyRequest` has these fields:

| Field        | Type   | Default                | Description                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `public_key` | string | none, required         | One line of the `authorized_keys` form, as in `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`.                   |
| `name`       | string | the comment of the key | A name of at most 64 characters. A comment that is not a valid name gives an empty name. |

The response `AddSSHKeyResponse` has the field `key`, an `SSHKey`.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                            | Code                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| The key is not one that hopbox takes, for example `invalid argument: invalid SSH key: the RSA key has 2048 bits, and hopbox takes at least 3072. Make an Ed25519 key with ssh-keygen -t ed25519` | `invalid_argument`   |
| A bad name                                                                                                                                                                                       | `invalid_argument`   |
| An account holds the key already, this one or another: `already exists: the install holds the key <fingerprint> already. Add another key`                                                        | `already_exists`     |
| The account holds 50 SSH keys: `usage limit exceeded: an account holds at most 50 SSH keys. Remove one first`                                                                                    | `resource_exhausted` |

```sh
cli -H 'Idempotency-Key: ssh-1' -d "{\"publicKey\":\"$(cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub)\"}" \
  $API/hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService/AddSSHKey
```

```json
{"key":{"id":"01a145b6-6c4e-72c0-b0ee-895c30b08f74","name":"ann@laptop","type":"ssh-ed25519","bits":256,"publicKey":"ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIAwqTIQ7y4LoYxC/02UEz3yB/6qT2C6Oj4OEOIHfnVze","fingerprint":"SHA256:DRdf39Nvm+zAXRzjpCOtwde9E/UUaXIbgz0+g1NA+10","createTime":"2026-10-16T17:15:45.613938Z"}}
```

### ListSSHKeys

Lists the SSH keys of the account, oldest first.

| Item              | Value                                                       |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService/ListSSHKeys`                      |
| Policy action     | `ssh_key.list`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account |
| Idempotent option | no                                                          |
| Audit entry       | none                                                        |

The request `ListSSHKeysRequest` has no fields. The response `ListSSHKeysResponse` has the field `keys`, a repeated `SSHKey`.

### RemoveSSHKey

Removes an SSH key from the account. The removal publishes the event `edge.access_changed`, so the edge servers end the open SSH connections of the key ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#checks-of-an-open-connection)).

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Procedure         | `/hopbox.v1.SSHKeyService/RemoveSSHKey`                                                                                 |
| Policy action     | `ssh_key.remove`: the `session` or `cli_token` of the account                                                           |
| Idempotent option | no                                                                                                                      |
| Audit entry       | action `ssh_key.remove`, org the personal org, target kind `ssh_key`, details `fingerprint`, `type`, `bits`, and `name` |

The request `RemoveSSHKeyRequest` has the field `id`, the UUID of the key. The response `RemoveSSHKeyResponse` has no fields.

| Error                              | Code               |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| The ID is not a UUID               | `invalid_argument` |
| The account has no key with the ID | `not_found`        |

## Audit entries

The sign-in calls write these entries in the transaction of the sign-in. Their actor is the new session: actor kind `session`, the account, and the session as the credential. Their org is the personal org of the account, so the account reads them with `ListAuditEntries`. [CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#audit-entries) lists the entries of the device flow, the CLI tokens, the API keys, and the SSH keys.

| Action                        | When                                                                                                                                                                                    | Target                                     | Details                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `account.create`              | A sign-in created the account.                                                                                                                                                          | the account                                | `method`, `email`, `personal_org`                                                                                            |
| `account.link_sign_in_method` | A sign-in linked its method to the account through a verified email.                                                                                                                    | the new method                             | `kind`, `email`                                                                                                              |
| `account.link_sign_in_method` | A link from a session added a method to the account ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#link-a-new-sign-in-method)). The actor is that session, not a new one. | the new method                             | `kind`, `email`, `session`, and `magic_link` or the details of the provider: `oauth_flow`, `subject`, and for GitHub `login` |
| `auth.sign_in`                | Every sign-in with a link.                                                                                                                                                              | the session                                | `method` (`email_link` or `login_link`), `email`, `new_account`, and `magic_link` or `login_link`: the UUID of the link      |
| `auth.sign_in`                | Every sign-in with GitHub or Google ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#audit-entries)).                                                                                | the session                                | `method` (`github` or `google`), `email`, `new_account`, `oauth_flow`, `subject`, and for GitHub `login`                     |
| `auth.sign_in`                | A poll of a device flow took the CLI tokens. The actor is the new CLI sign-in, with actor kind `cli_token`.                                                                             | the CLI sign-in, target kind `cli_sign_in` | `method` (`device`), `client_name`, `device_sign_in`                                                                         |
| `instance_admin.grant`        | A login link made the account an instance admin. This entry has no org.                                                                                                                 | the account                                | `login_link`                                                                                                                 |

# hopbox CLI

> The commands, flags, env vars, profiles, files, tokens, output, and exit status of the hopbox CLI. It also covers the managed SSH block and the prompt.

`hopbox` is the public CLI of hopbox. Users install it on laptops. It runs on macOS on Apple Silicon, and on Linux on x86_64 and arm64. On Windows, run the Linux build in WSL. The CLI calls the public API of an install through the Go client of [Go client](/reference/go-client/). It never reads the control store.

This page lists every command, flag, env var, file, output, and exit status of the CLI. [Install the hopbox CLI](/guide/install-cli/) installs the CLI, and [Use the hopbox CLI](/guide/cli/) shows it at work on an install. The code is in `cmd/hopbox`, `internal/cli`, and `internal/cli/config`.

## Usage

```sh
hopbox [global flags] <command> [args] [flags]
```

A global flag can come before or after the command. When you run `hopbox` without a command on a terminal, it opens [the prompt](#the-prompt), which runs one command after another. Without a terminal, it prints its usage and an error to stderr, and exits with status 80.

## Global flags

| Flag               | Env var                | Type   | Default                            | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ---------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-h`, `--help`     |                        | bool   | `false`                            | Prints the help of `hopbox`, or of the command that it follows, and exits with status 0.                                                             |
| `--profile=NAME`   | `HOPBOX_PROFILE`       | string | the active profile, else `default` | The profile of the command: one install and its sign-in. See [Profiles](#profiles).                                                                  |
| `--org=ORG`        | `HOPBOX_ORG`           | string | the active org of the profile      | The org of the command, by name or UUID. See [The org of a command](#the-org-of-a-command).                                                          |
| `--json`           |                        | bool   | `false`                            | Prints the result as JSON on stdout, and an error as JSON on stderr. See [Output](#output).                                                          |
| `--config-dir=DIR` | `HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR`    | path   | see [Files](#files)                | The dir of the config and the CLI tokens.                                                                                                            |
| `--debug`          | `HOPBOX_DEBUG`         | bool   | `false`                            | Logs each retry of a call and each refresh of the CLI tokens to stderr.                                                                              |
| `--no-ssh-config`  | `HOPBOX_NO_SSH_CONFIG` | bool   | `false`                            | Leaves `~/.ssh` alone: no managed block in `~/.ssh/config`, no line in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`, and no new key at `login`. See [SSH files](#ssh-files). |

A flag on the command line wins over its env var.

## Env vars

| Env var                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HOPBOX_PROFILE`       | The value of `--profile`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `HOPBOX_ORG`           | The value of `--org`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR`    | The value of `--config-dir`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `HOPBOX_DEBUG`         | The value of `--debug`, for example `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `HOPBOX_NO_SSH_CONFIG` | The value of `--no-ssh-config`, for example `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `HOPBOX_URL`           | The value of `login --url`. With `HOPBOX_API_KEY`, it is also the URL of the install for every command, and it is required.                                                                                                                               |
| `HOPBOX_API_KEY`       | An API key ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). If it is set, each command calls the API with the key, and not with the CLI sign-in of the profile. See [API keys in scripts](#api-keys-in-scripts). |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`      | If it is set and `HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR` is not, the config dir is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hopbox`.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `HOME`                 | The home dir, for the default config dir and for `~/.ssh`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `TERM`                 | The terminal type that `connect` and `exec --tty` send to the machine. Empty gives `xterm-256color` in the machine. With `dumb`, `hopbox` without a command opens no prompt.                                                                              |

## Profiles

A profile is one install that the CLI signs in to. It has a name, the URL of the install, and the active org. One CLI can hold many profiles, for example `default` for a hosted install and `dev` for an install on the laptop.

* The profile of a command is `--profile`, else the active profile of the config, else `default`.
* `hopbox login` makes or updates the profile of the command, and makes it the active profile.
* `hopbox profile use` changes the active profile. `hopbox profile remove` deletes a profile.

A profile name has 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `-`, and `_`. It starts with a letter or a digit. Another name fails with status 80.

## The org of a command

Each request that acts in an org carries an org ([the org API](/reference/org-api/#the-org-of-a-request)). The CLI picks it in this order:

1. `--org`, by name or UUID. A name matches one of your orgs. An exact match wins over a match that ignores case. If no org of yours has the name, the command fails with status 4. If two orgs have the name, the command fails with status 80 and lists their UUIDs.
2. The active org of the profile, which `hopbox org use` sets.
3. No org: the server takes the personal org of the account, or the org of an API key.

Sometimes `hopbox org delete` or `hopbox org leave` removes the active org. Then the command also drops the active org, and the profile acts in the personal org again.

## Files

The config dir is `$HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hopbox`, else `~/.config/hopbox`. macOS uses the same path. The CLI makes the dir with mode 0700 at its first write, such as at `hopbox login`. A command that only reads makes no dir.

`hopbox version` reads no config dir. With `HOPBOX_API_KEY`, only `login`, `logout`, `profile`, and `org use` read it. So a script with a key works with any config dir, or with none. `org create --use` and `org join --use` fail with status 80 while `HOPBOX_API_KEY` is set, as `org use` does.

| File               | Mode | Content                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config.toml`      | 0600 | The profiles. It holds no secret.                                                                                                  |
| `credentials.toml` | 0600 | The CLI tokens of each profile.                                                                                                    |
| `lock`             | 0600 | An empty file. Each process of the CLI takes an exclusive `flock` on it to change a file of the dir, or to refresh the CLI tokens. |
| `history`          | 0600 | The lines of [the prompt](#the-prompt), one per line, oldest first.                                                                |

The CLI writes a file to a temporary file in the same dir and renames it into place. So another process never reads half a file. The CLI does not use the keychain of the OS.

The CLI tokens are secrets, so the CLI checks the dir and `credentials.toml` before it uses them, as ssh checks `~/.ssh`. The dir can be a symlink, for example from a dotfile manager. The CLI then checks the dir that the link points to. It resolves the link once, at the start of the command or at its first write, and works only in that dir. So a link that someone points elsewhere during the command moves none of its files. `credentials.toml` itself cannot be a symlink. Each check that fails stops the command with status 1:

| Check                                                                                 | Error                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `credentials.toml` is a symlink.                                                      | `<path> is a symlink. The CLI tokens must live in a real dir and file. Set HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR to a dir of your own`                                                                                          |
| Another user owns the dir, the target of a linked dir, or `credentials.toml`.         | `<path> belongs to the user with uid <uid>, not to you. Set HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR to a dir of your own`                                                                                                         |
| Group or others can write the dir, the target of a linked dir, or `credentials.toml`. | `group or others can write <path> (mode <mode>). Run chmod go-w <path>`                                                                                                                                     |
| Group or others can read `credentials.toml`.                                          | `the file <path> holds secrets, but others can access it (mode <mode>). Run chmod 600 <path>`                                                                                                               |
| The file system of the dir has no file locks, such as some network file systems.      | `the file system has no file locks: the config dir <dir> cannot be locked, so two hopbox commands could refresh the CLI tokens at once and end the sign-in. Set HOPBOX_CONFIG_DIR to a dir on a local disk` |

The CLI opens `lock` and `credentials.toml` without following a symlink. After the open, it checks that the file that opened is the file that it checked. Else it fails with `<path> changed while the CLI read it. Run the command again`.

### config.toml

```toml
active_profile = "default"


[profiles.default]
url = "https://example.com"
org = "01a14a7c-be1e-74cc-9748-ff40254c5d55"
```

| Key                   | Type   | Default                      | Description                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `active_profile`      | string | empty, which means `default` | The profile of a command without `--profile`.                                                          |
| `profiles.<name>.url` | string | none                         | The URL of the install, as [URLs of an install](#urls-of-an-install) gives it. `hopbox login` sets it. |
| `profiles.<name>.org` | string | empty                        | The UUID of the active org. Empty means the personal org. `hopbox org use` sets it.                    |

You can edit the file. The CLI writes it again at the next change, without your comments.

### credentials.toml

```toml
[profiles.default]
url = "https://example.com"
account_id = "01a14a7c-813f-7a14-b6bc-44a4e57ac6ff"
cli_sign_in_id = "01a14a7c-abae-7e4d-bde7-34c1e1d6870d"
access_token = "hbxat_<token>"
access_token_expire_time = 2026-10-17T16:30:36Z
refresh_token = "hbxrt_<token>"
refresh_token_expire_time = 2026-11-16T15:30:36Z
```

| Key                                         | Type     | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `profiles.<name>.url`                       | string   | The install that issued the tokens. The CLI sends the tokens to this URL only. If the profile has another URL, the profile is not signed in. |
| `profiles.<name>.account_id`                | string   | The UUID of the account of the tokens.                                                                                                       |
| `profiles.<name>.cli_sign_in_id`            | string   | The UUID of the CLI sign-in ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)).                      |
| `profiles.<name>.access_token`              | string   | The access token, `hbxat_...`.                                                                                                               |
| `profiles.<name>.access_token_expire_time`  | datetime | The end of the access token, 1 hour after its issue.                                                                                         |
| `profiles.<name>.refresh_token`             | string   | The refresh token, `hbxrt_...`.                                                                                                              |
| `profiles.<name>.refresh_token_expire_time` | datetime | The end of the refresh token, 30 days after its issue.                                                                                       |

### SSH files

The CLI also keeps three things in `~/.ssh`, where `~` is `$HOME`. With them, `ssh box1.hop`, scp, rsync, and editors reach a machine through the SSH front door of the install. `--no-ssh-config` leaves `~/.ssh` alone.

| File                                             | When the CLI writes it                                                                       | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `~/.ssh/config`                                  | At `new`, `machine rename`, `machine delete`, and `list`                                     | The managed block: one `Host` entry for each machine                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `~/.ssh/known_hosts`                             | At `login`, and with each write of the managed block, once the install has an SSH front door | The managed block: one line with the host key of each install                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `~/.ssh/hopbox_ed25519` and `hopbox_ed25519.pub` | At `login`, for an account without an SSH key                                                | A new ed25519 key pair. The CLI adds the public key to the account. It takes the public key from the private key, so a stale `.pub` file changes nothing. A `.pub` file without its private key stops the CLI, and it makes no key next to it. |

A managed block starts with the line `# BEGIN hopbox` and ends with the line `# END hopbox`. The CLI changes only the lines between these markers. Every other byte of the file stays as it was. The CLI writes the new file to a temporary file in the same dir. Then it renames that file into place, so ssh never reads half a file. A file that exists keeps its mode. A new file gets mode 0600, and a new `~/.ssh` gets mode 0700. A file that is a symlink, for example from a dotfile manager, stays a symlink: the CLI writes the file that the link points to. For each change, the CLI takes an exclusive `flock` on the dir `~/.ssh`. So two commands at once never lose a change.

A file with a `# BEGIN hopbox` and no `# END hopbox`, a second block, or an `# END hopbox` alone is broken. The CLI then changes nothing in it, and logs `the managed SSH block was not updated` at level warn, with `the hopbox block markers do not pair up`. Fix the markers by hand. A failure to write a file of `~/.ssh` never fails a command, because the machine changed already. The command logs the warning and goes on.

Every value in a managed block comes from the API of an install. A hostile or broken install must not add lines of its own to `~/.ssh`. For example, a newline in a machine name can add a `ProxyCommand`. So the CLI checks each value before it writes it, and leaves out an entry or a key that fails. It then logs `the machine gets no entry in the managed SSH block` at level warn, or skips the whole write.

| Value                                              | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Machine name                                       | A lowercase DNS label: `a-z`, `0-9`, and `-`, 1 to 63 characters, from a letter, not ending with `-`                                                                                                                                           |
| Domain, `HostName`, and the host in `HostKeyAlias` | DNS labels of letters, digits, and `-`, at most 253 characters, or an IP address without a zone. No comma, space, `%`, `*`, or control character. The CLI writes the domain in lower case, and drops one dot at its end, as in `example.com.`. |
| Port                                               | 1 to 65535                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| User                                               | `user`, or another lowercase Linux user name                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Machine ID and org ID                              | A UUID in its canonical form                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Host key                                           | Exactly one public key. The CLI writes it in its canonical form, without options or a comment.                                                                                                                                                 |

The block of `~/.ssh/config`:

```text
# BEGIN hopbox
# The hopbox CLI writes this block at each create, rename, and delete of a machine. Edits inside it are lost.
Host box1.hop
  # hopbox machine=01a15e16-fe58-74f1-a778-d1350c527612 org=01a14a7c-813f-7a1c-946b-db123b23c342
  HostName example.com
  Port 10001
  User user
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/hopbox_ed25519
  IdentitiesOnly yes
  HostKeyAlias hopbox-example.com
Host *
# END hopbox
```

| Line             | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Host`           | The alias of the machine: its name and `.hop`, such as `box1.hop`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `# hopbox`       | The UUIDs of the machine and of its org. The CLI reads them back at the next change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `HostName`       | The domain of the install, from `GetInstallInfo`. An install without a domain gets the host of its URL.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Port`           | The SSH port of the machine on the edge servers. It never changes ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/#machine)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `User`           | `user`, the main Linux user of the default image                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `IdentityFile`   | `~/.ssh/hopbox_ed25519`, only while that file exists.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `IdentitiesOnly` | `yes`, with `IdentityFile` only. ssh then offers only that key, not each key of the agent. The SSH front door says yes to every offered key, and checks only signed keys. Without it, ssh signs with each key in turn, and a security key asks for a touch each time ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#sign-in)). To use another key, give it with `ssh -i`. |
| `HostKeyAlias`   | `hopbox-<domain>`. ssh looks the host key up under this name, without the port. So one line of `known_hosts` covers the SSH port of every machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

The entries are in the order of their aliases. A new block goes at the top of the file, because ssh takes the first value that it finds for each option. So a `Host *` of yours with another `User` or `Port` cannot change the entry of a machine. The block ends with `Host *`, so the lines of yours after the block still apply to every host, as they did before. You can move the block elsewhere in the file. The CLI then changes it where it is. When no machine is left, the CLI removes the block and its markers.

Each entry belongs to one machine, of one org, on one install. `new` adds the entry of the machine, and replaces an entry with the same machine UUID or the same alias. Another machine that had the alias, for example on another install, loses it, and the CLI logs `another machine had the SSH alias, and loses it` at level warn. `machine rename` replaces the entry. `machine delete` removes it. `list` makes the entries of the org and the install match the list: it adds the machines that another laptop or the console made, and removes the machines that are gone. The entries of other orgs and other installs stay.

The block of `~/.ssh/known_hosts` goes at the end of the file:

```text
# BEGIN hopbox
# The hopbox CLI writes this block at login and at each change of a machine. Edits inside it are lost.
hopbox-example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAI...
# END hopbox
```

Each line holds the `HostKeyAlias` of an install and the `ssh_host_key` of its `GetInstallInfo` ([the API server](/reference/api/)). The key comes over the API, which TLS protects, so the first `ssh box1.hop` asks no question about the host key. A new host key of the install replaces the line at the next write. An install without an SSH front door has no host key, so the CLI writes no line for it.

The certificate of TLS proves only the host of the URL of the install. So over `https`, the domain of `GetInstallInfo` must be the host of the URL. For another domain, the CLI uses the host of the URL in `HostName` and `HostKeyAlias`, and for the host key. It then logs `the install names another domain than its URL, so the managed SSH block uses the host of the URL` at level warn. So one install never writes the entries or the host key of another install. A loopback install without TLS, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7080`, gets its line for its domain. The trust then rests on the laptop, or on the SSH tunnel that leads to the install.

The block works only while ssh reads `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. A `UserKnownHostsFile` or `GlobalKnownHostsFile` in your config that leaves out this file makes ssh skip the block. Then ssh asks about the host key at the first connection, as for any new host.

## URLs of an install

`hopbox login --url` takes the URL of the install. The API serves at the root of the domain of the install, so the URL has no path.

* A bare domain gets `https://`. `example.com` is `https://example.com`.
* The CLI drops a `/` at the end, and writes the host in lower case. It also drops an empty port and the default port: 443 for `https`, 80 for `http`.
* Plain `http://` works only for a loopback host: `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, or `::1`. So a bearer token never crosses a network without TLS. A laptop install uses `http://127.0.0.1:7080`.
* A URL with a path, a query, a fragment, a user name, or a password fails with status 80.

The CLI speaks HTTP/2 to the install. To a loopback install without TLS, it speaks HTTP/2 with prior knowledge, because `exec` and `connect` need a stream in both directions ([Go client](/reference/go-client/#make-a-client)). It speaks no HTTP/1.1 there. So a proxy on a loopback address that speaks only HTTP/1.1 fails every call. `hopboxd` speaks both.

## Sign-in and tokens

`hopbox login` signs in with the device flow ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#the-device-flow)):

1. It calls `StartDeviceAuthorization` with the client name `hopbox CLI on <host name of the laptop>`, cut to 64 characters.
2. It prints the user code and the page `https://<domain>/device?code=<user code>` to stderr.
3. It polls `PollDeviceAuthorization` after each interval of the response, 5 s at first. A `SLOW_DOWN` answer makes the interval longer.
4. When a person approves the code in the console, the poll gets the CLI tokens. The CLI stores them in `credentials.toml`, sets the URL of the profile, and makes the profile active. The approval needs a sign-in to the console within the last 10 minutes ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#recent-sign-in)).
5. If the profile had a CLI sign-in before, the CLI ends it with `SignOut` and its old tokens.

Each command then calls the API with the access token. The CLI refreshes the tokens with `RefreshCLIToken` in two cases:

* The access token ends within 1 minute.
* The API refuses the access token with `unauthenticated`. The command then retries its call once with the new token.

A refresh token works once ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). So the CLI refreshes only under the lock of the config dir. It always uses the refresh token that `credentials.toml` holds at that moment, never a copy in memory. A second process that waits for the lock reads the new tokens of the first, and makes no refresh of its own. A process that holds an older access token reads `credentials.toml` again before a refresh. The grace of 10 s of the install covers only one second refresh with the same token. Without the lock, three processes that refresh at once end the sign-in, and the audit log records a reuse that no thief made. So the CLI refuses a config dir on a file system without `flock` ([Files](#files)).

If the refresh token ended, the profile is not signed in. If the install refuses the refresh token, the sign-in ended: someone ended it in the console, or a used refresh token came back. If `credentials.toml` still holds the refresh token that the CLI sent, the CLI then deletes the tokens of the profile. The command fails with status 2. Run `hopbox login` again.

If the CLI cannot write the new tokens, the command still finishes with them. The CLI logs `the refreshed CLI tokens could not be stored, so the next command must sign in again` at level warn. It also tries to delete the old tokens of the profile, so the next command asks for a new sign-in.

A refresh replaces the refresh token on the install before the CLI writes the new one. Two cases leave the old refresh token in `credentials.toml`: the write and the delete both fail, or the process dies between the refresh and the write. The next refresh then sends the old token again. The install ends the CLI sign-in, and its audit log records a refresh token reuse. Run `hopbox login` again. No token leaked, but the install cannot tell this case from a theft.

## API keys in scripts

If `HOPBOX_API_KEY` holds an API key, each command calls the API with that key and ignores the CLI sign-in of the profile.

* The URL of the install must be in `HOPBOX_URL`. Without it, the command fails with status 80. The CLI never sends the key to the URL of a profile, because the profile can name another install.
* A key works in its own org only ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#api-keys)). The active org of the profile does not apply. `--org` still applies, and the server refuses an org that is not the org of the key.
* `hopbox org use`, and `--use` of `org create` and `org join`, fail with status 80, because the active org has no effect on a key.
* No API key can make, list, or revoke API keys. Such a command fails with status 3.
* `hopbox login` and `hopbox logout` ignore the key. They act on the CLI sign-in of the profile.
* If the install refuses the key, the error says `Check the API key in HOPBOX_API_KEY`.
* The commands for machines work with a key too. They still keep the managed blocks in `~/.ssh`, so a script on a shared runner can add `--no-ssh-config`.

## Retries

Each call goes through the retries of the Go client ([Go client](/reference/go-client/#retries)). The CLI retries a call twice after `unavailable`, `resource_exhausted`, or `deadline_exceeded`, if the call is safe to run again. A read call, such as `ListMachines`, and a call with an idempotency key, such as `CreateMachine`, are safe.
