A client is an IPv4 address or the /64 of an IPv6 address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Open requests of one IPv6 network      | At most 4,096 at once, for all /64s of one IPv6 /48 together. A request past the bound gets `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After: 1` and `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1`. The count of its /64 does not matter. So one /48 can take at most a quarter of the 16,384. Watch `hopbox_edge_requests_total{to="refused"}` for the refusals of both bounds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| HTTP/2 frames                          | At most 16 KiB for each frame that a client sends.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Request body on HTTP/1.1               | A body that sends nothing for 1 minute ends. The edge role then answers, and closes the connection. A body that keeps sending has no time limit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Answer, HTTP/2 streams, and WebSockets | No timeout, so streams, downloads, and WebSockets can last.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Clients behind one network

The bounds of a client and of an IPv6 network count by address. So all people behind one address share its slots, also with their long streams, such as an office or a carrier with one NAT.

| Network          | What it shares                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One IPv4 address | 256 connections on each listener, and 1,024 open requests. A carrier NAT can put thousands of people behind one address. IPv4 has no bound of a wider network, because the next addresses often belong to other people.                                                                                           |
| One IPv6 /64     | 256 connections on each listener, and 1,024 open requests. One host usually holds a whole /64.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| One IPv6 /48     | 1,024 connections on each listener, and 4,096 open requests, for all its /64s together. One site, such as an office or a server of a hosting provider, usually holds a /48. A carrier or a hosting provider can also give many customers a /64 each in one /48. These customers then share the bounds of the /48. |

Without the bound of a /48, 64 /64s of one /48 fill the 16,384 connections of the HTTPS listener. With it, a client needs 16 /48s. A lower bound for each /48 keeps the listener open for more networks, but it stops more users of a shared /48. The bound is 1,024 connections for each /48. If the users of a large network reach the bound, `hopbox_edge_client_connection_refusals_total{bound="network"}` and `hopbox_edge_requests_total{to="refused"}` grow.

### Memory of stalled requests

A request can stall in two ways. Its target reads none of its body, or its client reads none of the answer. A stalled request holds memory in the edge until it ends, because no timeout ends an HTTP/2 stream. The bounds of open requests cap that memory. At the end of each request, the edge closes its body. So an HTTP/2 stream whose answer waits for the window of the client holds no body:

| Buffer of one request                            | Size                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The request header                               | At most 64 KiB.                                                                                                      |
| The body on HTTP/2                               | At most 256 KiB, the receive buffer of the stream.                                                                   |
| The answer of the control role                   | At most 64 KiB, the receive buffer of the stream to the control role.                                                |
| The frame buffer of the body to the control role | 64 KiB, the largest frame that the internal listener reads ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). |
| The copy buffers of the proxy                    | 32 KiB in each direction.                                                                                            |

So one request holds at most 512 KiB. A connection also holds memory without a request:

| Buffer of one HTTPS connection        | Size                                                     |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| The read buffer of the HTTP/2 framer  | At most 16 KiB, the largest frame.                       |
| The write buffer of the HTTP/2 framer | About 16 KiB.                                            |
| The TLS records                       | About 17 KiB in each direction.                          |
| The HPACK tables                      | 4 KiB in each direction.                                 |
| The save buffer of the HPACK decoder  | Up to about 64 KiB, for a header in CONTINUATION frames. |
| The stacks of its goroutines          | 16 KiB to 32 KiB each after the TLS handshake.           |
| The structs of the connection         | Some KiB.                                                |

The edge counts 256 KiB for one HTTPS connection. A connection of the HTTP listener holds a read buffer and a write buffer of 4 KiB. It also holds a stack, its structs, and the wrappers of the listeners. An idle one takes about 20 KiB. The edge counts 32 KiB for it. So the bounds are these:

| Who                | Most memory                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One client         | 584 MiB: 256 HTTPS connections of 256 KiB, 256 HTTP connections of 32 KiB, and 1,024 requests of 512 KiB.     |
| One IPv6 /48       | 2.3 GiB: 1,024 HTTPS connections of 256 KiB, 1,024 HTTP connections of 32 KiB, and 4,096 requests of 512 KiB. |
| The HTTPS listener | 12 GiB: 16,384 connections of 256 KiB, and 16,384 requests of 512 KiB.                                        |
| The HTTP listener  | 2 GiB: 65,536 connections of 32 KiB.                                                                          |

A test of `internal/edge` checks these bounds against the defaults.

The answer of a machine and the body of a request on HTTP/1.1 wait in the socket buffers of the kernel, not in `hopboxd`. The kernel parameters `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem`, `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem`, and `net.ipv4.tcp_mem` bound them. Each HTTP/1.1 connection to a machine also holds a read buffer and a write buffer of 4 KiB in the edge.

The unit `edge` of `hopboxd run` opens the listeners at its start ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). If another program holds a port, the start fails, and `hopboxd` exits with status 1. The error names the address, such as `edge: listen on :443: bind: address already in use`. Ports 443 and 80 need root, and `hopboxd.service` runs `hopboxd` as root ([Server layout](/reference/server-layout/#hopboxdservice)).

At a stop, the unit ends the SSH connections, closes the listeners, gives the open requests 2 s, and then ends the rest: streams, WebSockets, and long calls. The whole stop takes at most 5 s.

## TLS

The edge role serves one certificate: the wildcard certificate of the install, for the domain and `*.<domain>` ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/)). The control role pushes the certificate with its key over the control channel ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#edge-pushes)). The edge role keeps it only in memory.

| Rule                          | Value                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TLS versions                  | 1.2 and 1.3. The cipher suites are the defaults of Go.                                                                                                                            |
| Server name (SNI)             | Required. A handshake without a server name fails.                                                                                                                                |
| Host names                    | The domain, and each name under it. A handshake for another name fails.                                                                                                           |
| Before the first certificate  | Every handshake fails.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Certificate of another domain | When the domain of the install changes, the edge role refuses every handshake until the certificate of the new domain arrives. It never serves the certificate of the old domain. |

The edge role checks each certificate that the control role pushes before it serves it. It refuses a certificate in each of these cases, and keeps the certificate that it has:

* The domain of the message is not a domain in lowercase without a final dot.
* The leaf does not cover the domain, or a name under it.
* The leaf is not valid now.
* The key is not a PKCS #8 key, or it does not match the leaf.

A handshake that fails counts in `hopbox_edge_tls_refusals_total` ([Metrics](#metrics)).

## Routing

The edge role routes each HTTPS request by its host. The host is the `Host` header, or the `:authority` of HTTP/2, in lowercase, without a port and without a final dot.

| Request                                                                                                                                       | Answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The host is not the server name of the TLS connection, and one of the two is not a name of the certificate: the domain, or one label under it | `421 Misdirected Request`. A browser sends the requests of every name of a certificate on one HTTP/2 connection, so those pass. A host outside the certificate does not, also in a request in the absolute form, such as `GET https://other.example/`. |
| Method `CONNECT`                                                                                                                              | `405 Method Not Allowed`. The edge role is not a proxy.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Host `example.com`, path under `/hopbox.cluster.v1.`                                                                                          | `404 Not Found`. The cluster API is only for the servers of the install, on the internal listener.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Host `example.com`                                                                                                                            | Forwarded to the control role ([Forwarded requests](#forwarded-requests)).                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Host `<name>.example.com`                                                                                                                     | The machine `<name>` ([Machine URLs](#machine-urls)).                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Any other host under the domain, such as `sub.box1.example.com`                                                                               | `404 Not Found`. Subdomain routes come in phase 4.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Each HTTPS answer carries the header `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (HSTS). A browser then reaches the domain and every machine URL only over HTTPS for a year.

An HTTP/1.1 request with the body encoding `chunked` gets `Connection: close` on its answer. Such a request can also have had a `Content-Length` header, which the server drops. Two such headers can hide a second request behind the first one, so the connection ends after the answer (RFC 9112, section 6.1). The server of Go refuses the other ambiguous requests. Two different `Content-Length` values, and a space before the colon of a header name, get `400 Bad Request`. A `Transfer-Encoding` other than `chunked` gets `501 Not Implemented`. A header line that continues on the next line reaches a machine as one line. The edge role builds a new request for each request that it forwards, so a forwarded request never carries the framing of the client.

The pages of the edge role are plain text, with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. They also carry `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, so no page shows them in a frame. So do the redirects of the sign-in, and the pages of `/auth/machine`.

### HTTP to HTTPS

The HTTP listener answers each request for the domain or a name under it with `301 Moved Permanently` to the same host and path over HTTPS. For example, `http://box1.example.com/a?b=1` goes to `https://box1.example.com/a?b=1`. A request for another host, or before the edge role knows the domain, gets `404 Not Found`.

## Forwarded requests

The edge role forwards each request of the domain to the internal listeners of the control servers, at `channel.control_urls` of the bootstrap config ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/#forwarded-requests)). It sends the requests to the control servers in turn, one request after the other. Its `EdgeService` calls, such as the machine URL sign-in and the checks of the SSH front door, go the same way. A request that got no connection, because a dial or the TLS handshake failed, goes to the next control server with its body unread. The edge role then skips that control server for 10 s, so the next requests try the others first. A request that reached a control server and failed before its answer came does not go again, but the edge skips that control server for 10 s too. A request whose client went away, or whose deadline ended, marks no control server and goes to no other one. A short deadline of a caller says nothing of the control server. A dead control server still gets skipped: its connection fails the ping within 10 s, and a new dial to it fails within 3 s. A new connection to a control server has 3 s for its dial and 3 s for its TLS handshake: the control servers sit on the vRack, so a slower one is gone, and the request goes on to the next control server well within the deadline of its call. A control server that died hard leaves its HTTP/2 connection half open. So the edge pings a connection to a control server that sent nothing for 5 s, and closes it when the answer does not come within 5 s. The requests on it then fail, and the next requests go to the others. This covers Connect, gRPC, gRPC-Web, streams in both directions, trailers, the sign-in pages under `/auth/`, and the WebSocket of exec (`/api/ws/exec`). The admin API is public behind the edge too, for admin API keys.

| Item                                    | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Transport                               | Mutual TLS 1.3 with the server certificate of the edge server, against the install CA. HTTP/2 for every request but a WebSocket upgrade, which uses HTTP/1.1, because HTTP/2 cannot carry it.                                                                                                                                           |
| Host                                    | The host of the client request, such as `example.com`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Hopbox-Client-Addr`                    | The address of the client, `IP:port`. The edge role sets it over any value that the client sent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `X-Forwarded-For`                       | The IP address of the client alone. The edge role drops the value that the client sent.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` | The host of the request, and `https`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `Forwarded`                             | Dropped.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Flush                                   | Each write of the control role goes to the client at once, so streams do not wait.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| HTTP/2 receive buffer                   | 64 KiB for each stream, and 1 GiB for the connection, which holds the buffers of all 16,384 open requests. So an answer that one client does not read never stalls the answers of other clients.                                                                                                                                        |
| Failure                                 | `502 Bad Gateway` with a page that says that the control plane did not answer. If the request got no connection to the control role, because of a dial or TLS error to every control server, the answer also carries `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1`. After a connection, the control role can have run the call, so the answer has no such header. |

The header `Hopbox-Not-Run: 1` tells a client that the call changed nothing, so the client can retry it ([the API server](/reference/api/#answers-of-calls-that-changed-nothing)). The refusals of the bounds of open requests carry it too ([Listeners](#listeners)).

The control role trusts `Hopbox-Client-Addr` only on a connection whose certificate proves a server with the edge role. The rate limits of sign-in then count each client by its own address ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#rate-limits)).

## Machine URLs

The control role pushes the routes of the machine URLs over the control channel ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#edge-pushes)). A route names a machine that holds its name and is not on its way out. A running machine has a target: the address of the machine on its node, its URL port, and its lease ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#route_records)).

| Case                                                  | Answer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| No machine has the name                               | The same answers as a private URL without a sign-in ([Answers of a private URL](#answers-of-a-private-url)). So a client cannot tell which names have a machine. After the sign-in, `/auth/machine` answers `404 Not Found`, also for a machine that the account does not see.       |
| A path under `/__hopbox/` other than `/__hopbox/auth` | `404 Not Found`. The edge role keeps these paths for itself and never forwards one to a machine.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| A private URL without a valid sign-in                 | The sign-in ([Private machine URLs](#private-machine-urls)). A private URL tells nothing else about its machine before the sign-in.                                                                                                                                                  |
| An instance admin suspended the org of the machine    | `403 Forbidden`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The machine does not run                              | `503 Service Unavailable`, with the state of the machine, such as `The machine box1 is stopped. Start it, then retry.`                                                                                                                                                               |
| The lease of the target ended at the edge             | `503 Service Unavailable`. The node of the machine did not renew its lease lately, so the machine can run on another node now.                                                                                                                                                       |
| The target has no address                             | `503 Service Unavailable`, with the page `The machine box1 runs, but it has no network address on its node, so its URL cannot reach it.` Each machine gets an address at its create, so only a machine without one gets it ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#addresses)). |
| The machine does not answer on its URL port           | `502 Bad Gateway`, with a page that says to check that a server listens on that port in the machine                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Otherwise                                             | Forwarded to the machine                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

The edge role counts the lease of each target from the arrival of the routes. The control role sends the rest of the lease, less a tenth of the machine TTL. It also takes off the time that the routes waited in its queue. After each heartbeat of the edge server, it sends the changed routes, or only the rest of the lease of each target. So the lease of a live target never runs out. If the control channel of the edge server ends, the targets run out within the machine TTL of 30 s. The machine URLs then answer 503 until the channel is back.

The edge role keeps each request that it forwards to a machine until it ends, such as a WebSocket or a long download. New routes end an open request at once in three cases: the machine has no route any more, its org is suspended, or its URL turned private. A request of a public URL has no sign-in, so it cannot stay open on a private URL.

### What a machine gets

The edge role forwards a request to `http://<address>:<url port>` over HTTP/1.1, without TLS. The address is the address of the machine on its node ([the node network](/reference/node-network/)). In phase 1, the edge role runs on the node of the machine, so the traffic stays on that server.

| Item                                    | Value                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Host                                    | The machine host, such as `box1.example.com`.                                                                                                                       |
| `X-Forwarded-For`                       | The IP address of the client alone.                                                                                                                                 |
| `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` | The machine host, and `https`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `Forwarded`, `Hopbox-Client-Addr`       | Dropped. Only the control role reads `Hopbox-Client-Addr`.                                                                                                          |
| `Cookie`                                | Each cookie of the client, except the cookies of hopbox: every name that starts with `__Host-hopbox_`, in any case. The other cookies stay as the client sent them. |
| WebSocket                               | An upgrade over HTTP/1.1 passes.                                                                                                                                    |
| Answer header                           | At most 64 KiB.                                                                                                                                                     |

So the code of a machine never gets the machine cookie, nor a session cookie of the console. The cookies of the console are host-only `__Host-` cookies of the domain, so a browser never sends them to a machine host anyway ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/)).

The edge role also drops these `Set-Cookie` headers of an answer of a machine:

* A cookie whose name starts with `__Host-hopbox_`, in any case.
* A cookie with a `Domain` attribute other than the machine host. Such a cookie can reach the console and the other machines of the install, which are on the same site as the machine.

A cookie without a `Domain` attribute, or with the machine host as its domain, passes.

## Private machine URLs

The URL of each machine is private by default. Only an account that uses the machine opens it: its creator, and every member of its org once the creator shares it. An org admin cannot open the private URL of a private machine of another member, as with a shell. The rule is the policy action `machine.open_url` ([the API server](/reference/api/)). The creator makes the URL public with `SetMachineURLVisibility` ([the machine API](/reference/machine-api/)). A public URL needs no sign-in.

The sign-in of a private URL takes these steps. The machine is `box1`.

1. A browser asks for `https://box1.example.com/page?x=1` without a machine cookie. The edge role answers `303 See Other` to `https://example.com/auth/machine?machine=box1&path=%2Fpage%3Fx%3D1`. A path longer than 512 characters becomes `/`.
2. The control role reads the session cookie of the console at `/auth/machine`. With a live session of an account that uses the machine, it makes a one-time code, and answers `303 See Other` to `https://box1.example.com/__hopbox/auth?code=<code>&path=%2Fpage%3Fx%3D1`. Without a session, it answers `401 Unauthorized` with a page that says to sign in to the console first.
3. The edge role takes the code at `/__hopbox/auth`, and trades it for a token with `EdgeService.ExchangeMachineCode`. It sets the token in the cookie `__Host-hopbox_machine`, and answers `303 See Other` to the path. A path that is not a plain path on the host, such as `//other.example`, becomes `/`.
4. The browser asks for `https://box1.example.com/page?x=1` with the machine cookie. The edge role checks the token with `EdgeService.AuthorizeMachineRequest`, takes the cookie out of the request, and forwards the request to the machine.

The code never reaches the machine. The answers of steps 2 and 3 carry `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

| Item                 | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Code                 | 32 random bytes in base64url, 43 characters. The control store keeps only its SHA-256.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Code lifetime        | 60 s, one use, and only for the machine that it names.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Codes of one session | At most 30 in a minute. The next one gets `429 Too Many Requests`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Token                | 32 random bytes in base64url. The control store keeps only its SHA-256. A new token of the same browser and machine replaces the older one.                                                                                                                                           |
| Token lifetime       | The life of the console session that made it: 7 days without a use, and 30 days at most. A sign-out ends it at once. Each check of a token keeps its session alive, as a call of the console does.                                                                                    |
| Cookie               | `__Host-hopbox_machine=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`. The cookie is host-only, and it has no `Max-Age`. When the browser closes, it drops the cookie.                                                                                                              |
| Kept answers         | The edge role keeps each answer that allows a token on a machine. It keeps an answer for at most 1 minute, and never past the end of the console session. It keeps no refusal, so a new grant works at once. It keeps at most 10,000 answers. When it is full, it starts again empty. |

The control role tells the edge servers about each change that can end an access. A change event of a machine, such as an unshare or a delete, is about that machine. An event `edge.access_changed` is about every machine ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#the-event-edgeaccess_changed)). A sign-out, a member that leaves an org or that an admin removes, a deleted account, and a suspension of an org publish it. A change can arrive while an edge server has no channel. So each new control channel also brings a change of every machine.

At a change, the edge role drops the answers that it keeps for the machines of the change. It also checks each open request of their private URLs again in the background, such as a WebSocket or a long download. A token that lost its access ends its open requests at once. The edge role also checks every open request again each minute, because a console session can end by time, without a change event. So an open request never keeps an access for more than about a minute after its end.

### Answers of a private URL

| Case                                                                                          | Answer                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A top-level navigation by `GET` or `HEAD` without a valid machine cookie                      | `303 See Other` to `/auth/machine` (step 1)                                                                                           |
| Any other request without a valid machine cookie                                              | `401 Unauthorized`. A browser does not follow a redirect for these, so the page says to open the URL in a browser first.              |
| A request from a page of another origin, other than a top-level navigation by `GET` or `HEAD` | `401 Unauthorized`. It counts as a request without a machine cookie ([Requests of other sites](#requests-of-other-sites)).            |
| A WebSocket upgrade whose `Origin` is not the machine host                                    | `403 Forbidden`                                                                                                                       |
| Two different machine cookies                                                                 | It counts as a request without a machine cookie. The edge role sets one machine cookie on a host, so it cannot tell which one it set. |
| A token that names no live sign-in, such as after a sign-out                                  | The edge role clears the machine cookie with `Max-Age=0`, and starts the sign-in again.                                               |
| The account has no access to the machine now                                                  | `403 Forbidden`                                                                                                                       |
| The org of the machine is suspended                                                           | `403 Forbidden`                                                                                                                       |
| A code that is unknown, used, expired, or for another machine                                 | `403 Forbidden` with a page that says to open the URL again                                                                           |
| The control role does not answer                                                              | `502 Bad Gateway`                                                                                                                     |

### Requests of other sites

The machine hosts of an install share one site, such as `example.com`. A browser sends a `SameSite=Lax` cookie with each request inside a site. Without a check, a page of `box1` can send a fetch, a form `POST`, or a WebSocket to `box2`. The browser then adds the machine cookie of `box2`. So the code of one machine can act in the private URL of another account. The edge role reads the fetch metadata of the browser:

* A request with `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` or `cross-site` counts as a request without a machine cookie. Only a top-level navigation passes: `GET` or `HEAD` with `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, and `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document` or no `Sec-Fetch-Dest`. A link from another page then still opens the URL. A frame in a page of another machine has `Sec-Fetch-Dest: iframe`, so it shows the URL without the cookie.
* A WebSocket upgrade needs no `Origin`, or the origin `https://<machine host>`. A browser always sends the origin of its page with a WebSocket.
* `/__hopbox/auth` takes only a top-level navigation by `GET`. A request with another `Sec-Fetch-Mode` gets `405 Method Not Allowed`, so a page cannot plant a cookie with a code of its own.

A request from the page of the machine itself has `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, and uses the cookie. A client without fetch metadata, such as curl, also uses it.

### Answers of `/auth/machine`

`GET /auth/machine` is a plain HTTP endpoint of the public API on the domain of the install, outside of the Connect chain. Its parameters are `machine`, the name of the machine, and `path`, the path to return to. A path that is not a plain path on the host becomes `/`.

| Case                                                                                                               | Status                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| A code                                                                                                             | `303 See Other` to the machine host (step 2) |
| No live console session                                                                                            | `401 Unauthorized`                           |
| An account that uses no such machine, or no such machine                                                           | `404 Not Found`                              |
| An account that sees the machine, but does not use it, such as an org admin on a private machine of another member | `403 Forbidden`                              |
| More than 30 codes of the session in a minute                                                                      | `429 Too Many Requests`                      |
| The org of the machine is suspended, or the install has no domain                                                  | `409 Conflict`                               |

The answer is a plain text page with the reason and the request ID.

## EdgeService

`hopbox.cluster.v1.EdgeService` serves the edge servers on the internal listener ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). Every call needs the certificate of a server with the edge role. Another server gets `permission_denied`.

| Call                      | Request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Response                                                                                                    | Errors                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ExchangeMachineCode`     | `machine`: the name of the machine of the host. `code`: the code of the query.                                                                                                                                                                                       | `token`: the value of the machine cookie.                                                                   | `unauthenticated` for a code that is unknown, used, expired, malformed, or for another machine. `invalid_argument` for a name that breaks the name rules.                                                                                                                                             |
| `AuthorizeMachineRequest` | `machine`: the name of the machine of the host. `token`: the value of the machine cookie.                                                                                                                                                                            | `machine_id` and `account_id`, UUIDs. `valid_for`: how long the edge can keep the answer, at most 1 minute. | `unauthenticated` for a token that is unknown, malformed, for another machine, or of an ended console session. `permission_denied` for an account without access. `failed_precondition` for a suspended org.                                                                                          |
| `AuthorizeSSH`            | `ssh_port`, `public_key`, `linux_user`, and `client_ip` of an SSH connection, and `recheck` for a check of an open connection ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#edgeserviceauthorizessh)). Each allowed sign-in writes the audit entry `machine.ssh`. | `machine_id`, `machine_name`, `account_id`, and `valid_for`.                                                | `permission_denied` for every key, port, or user that opens nothing, with one message. `invalid_argument` for a sign-in without a valid `client_ip`, with the message `invalid argument: a sign-in needs the IP address of the SSH client` or `invalid argument: the client IP is not an IP address`. |

The edge role calls each one with a timeout of 10 s.

## Metrics

The edge role serves these metrics on the metrics listener of `hopboxd` ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/)).

| Metric                                         | Type    | Labels                                                        | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hopbox_edge_requests_total`                   | counter | `to`: `api`, `machine`, `redirect`, or `refused`              | The HTTP requests of the edge role, by where they went. A redirect goes to HTTPS, to a sign-in, or back from a sign-in. A refusal got a page of the edge role, also a refusal past the bounds of open requests. |
| `hopbox_edge_tls_refusals_total`               | counter | `reason`: `no_sni`, `unknown_host`, or `no_certificate`       | The TLS handshakes that the edge role refused.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `hopbox_edge_client_connection_refusals_total` | counter | `listener`: `https` or `http`. `bound`: `client` or `network` | The connections that the edge role closed at once. `client`: their IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 held 256 open connections on the listener. `network`: their IPv6 /48 held 1,024.                                    |
| `hopbox_edge_open_connections`                 | gauge   | `listener`: `https` or `http`                                 | The connections that the listener holds now.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `hopbox_edge_connection_limit`                 | gauge   | `listener`: `https` or `http`                                 | The most connections that the listener holds at once: 16,384 for `https`, and 65,536 for `http`. A connection past it waits in the backlog of the kernel.                                                       |
| `hopbox_edge_routes`                           | gauge   | none                                                          | The machines that the routes name.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `hopbox_edge_certificate_not_after_seconds`    | gauge   | none                                                          | The end of the certificate that the edge role serves, in seconds since the Unix epoch, or 0 before the first certificate.                                                                                       |

The metrics of the SSH front door start with `hopbox_edge_ssh_` ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#metrics)).

## Logs

The edge role logs with `component=edge`.

| Message                                                                 | Level | When                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `edge listening`                                                        | info  | The listeners are open, with `https` and `http`.                                                   |
| `serving a certificate`                                                 | info  | A new certificate, with `domain`, `not_after`, and `serial`.                                       |
| `serving the machine URLs of a domain`                                  | info  | The first routes, or the routes of a new domain, with `domain` and `machines`.                     |
| `forwarding a request to the control plane failed`                      | warn  | A forwarded request failed, with `path` and `err`.                                                 |
| `forwarding a request to a machine failed`                              | info  | A machine did not answer, with `host` and `err`.                                                   |
| `checking a machine URL sign-in failed`                                 | warn  | `AuthorizeMachineRequest` failed without an answer, with `machine` and `err`.                      |
| `trading a machine URL code failed`                                     | warn  | `ExchangeMachineCode` failed without an answer, with `machine` and `err`.                          |
| `ended the open requests of a machine URL sign-in that lost its access` | info  | A check refused a token with open requests. The fields are `machine`, `open_requests`, and `code`. |
| `ended the open requests of machine URLs that changed`                  | info  | New routes ended open requests, with `open_requests` ([Machine URLs](#machine-urls)).              |

The edge role can refuse a certificate or routes that the control role pushed. The agent of the control channel then logs `the edge role refused a push of the control plane, and keeps what it has` at error level, with `push` and `err`.

## Not in phase 1

These parts of the edge role come later:

* A machine in standby or hibernated wakes at the first request (phase 3). Until then, its URL answers 503.
* Subdomain routes, such as `sub.box1.example.com` (phase 4).
* Custom domains and org domains (phase 4).
* Raw TCP and UDP ports (phase 4).

# Go client

> The Go client of the public API: its options, idempotency keys, retries, typed errors, and credentials.

`internal/client` is the Go client of the public API `hopbox.v1`. The hopbox CLI uses it ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/)). It wraps the generated Connect clients of `gen/hopbox/v1/hopboxv1connect` with these rules: retries with backoff, idempotency keys on create calls, typed errors, and the bearer credential of the caller. The TypeScript SDK follows the same rules ([TypeScript SDK](/reference/ts-sdk/)). The package links no control code. The test `TestCLINeverLinksControlCode` of `tools/rolesplit` checks this for `internal/client`, `internal/cli`, and `cmd/hopbox`.

## Make a client

```go
c, err := client.New("https://example.com", client.Options{
  Credentials: client.BearerToken(os.Getenv("HOPBOX_API_KEY")),
})
if err != nil {
  return err
}
resp, err := c.Orgs.ListOrgs(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&hopboxv1.ListOrgsRequest{}))
if errors.Is(err, client.ErrPermissionDenied) {
  // The key cannot list orgs.
}
```

`New(rawURL, opts)` checks the URL with `ParseURL` and returns a `*Client`. A bad URL fails with an error that wraps `ErrBadURL`.

| `Options` field  | Type            | Default                          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `HTTPClient`     | `*http.Client`  | `DefaultHTTPClient()`            | Sends the calls. The default speaks HTTP/2 over TLS, with HTTP/1.1 for a server without HTTP/2. To a loopback install without TLS, it speaks HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c), as `hopboxd` does, because `Exec` needs a stream in both directions. A loopback server that speaks only HTTP/1.1 then fails the call. It follows no redirect, so the bearer token never goes to another host: a redirect fails the call. A client of your own must do the same. |
| `Credentials`    | `Credentials`   | nil                              | Gives the bearer token of each call. With nil, the calls carry no credential, as the device flow needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `UserAgent`      | string          | `hopbox-go-client (<os>/<arch>)` | The `User-Agent` header of each call. The CLI sends `hopbox-cli/<version> (<os>/<arch>)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `AttemptTimeout` | `time.Duration` | `DefaultAttemptTimeout`, 90 s    | The deadline of one try of a unary call. The server gives a call 30 s, and a lifecycle call of a machine 60 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `MaxRetryAfter`  | `time.Duration` | 0, no cap                        | The longest `Retry-After` that the client waits for. A longer one ends the call with its error, and `Error.RetryAfter` holds the wanted wait. With 0, the client waits as long as the server asks. The CLI sets 5 minutes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Logger`         | `*slog.Logger`  | no logs                          | Gets a debug record for each retry, and a record for each refresh of CLI tokens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

`Client` has the field `BaseURL`, the URL of `ParseURL`. It has one generated client for each service of `hopbox.v1`: `Install`, `Auth`, `Accounts`, `Orgs`, `APIKeys`, `SSHKeys`, `Machines`, `Vars`, and `Audit`. Each call of each one goes through the steps below.

## Install URLs

`ParseURL(raw)` returns the base URL of an install, such as `https://example.com`.

* A bare domain gets `https://`.
* The host is in lower case, and a `/` at the end goes.
* `http://` works only for a loopback host: `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, or `::1`.
* A path, a query, a fragment, a user name, or a password fails with `ErrBadURL`.

The error of a refused URL hides its user info. It shows `xxxxx` in place of all text between `://` and the last `@`, such as `https://xxxxx@example.com`. A password with a `/` or a `?` in it stays hidden too. A URL without an `@` shows as it is.

## The steps of a call

Each unary call passes these steps in order:

1. **Typed errors.** The error of the call becomes an `*Error`. See [Errors](#errors).
2. **User agent.** The step sets `User-Agent`.
3. **Idempotency key.** See [Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys).
4. **Retries.** See [Retries](#retries). The steps after this one run again on each try.
5. **Credential.** See [Credentials](#credentials).

A stream gets the steps 1, 2, and 5, without retries. If the credential fails, the first `Send` or `Receive` of the stream returns the error, and the stream sends no request.

## Idempotency keys

A method with the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)` needs an `Idempotency-Key` header ([the API server](/reference/api/#idempotency-keys)). Today these are `CreateMachine`, `CreateOrg`, `CreateAPIKey`, and `AddSSHKey`. The client puts a new UUIDv7 in the header of each such call that has no key yet. The step runs before the retries, so each try of one call sends the same key. The server then runs the call once. A key that the caller set stays.

## Retries

The client tries a unary call at most 3 times: the first try and `MaxRetries`, 2, retries.

| Code of the failed try | Retried                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unavailable`          | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `resource_exhausted`   | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| `deadline_exceeded`    | Only for a call that is safe to run again.             |
| Any other code         | No. An auth error or a bad request never gets a retry. |

A call is safe to run again in these cases:

| Case                                     | How the client knows it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The call only reads.                     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.read_only)`, or `idempotency_level` `NO_SIDE_EFFECTS` or `IDEMPOTENT` ([API definitions](/reference/api-definitions/#hopboxv1read_only)). Examples are `ListOrgs` and `GetMachine`.                                        |
| The call carries an idempotency key.     | Its method has the option `(hopbox.v1.idempotent)`, such as `CreateMachine` ([Idempotency keys](#idempotency-keys)).                                                                                                                                             |
| The try surely did not reach the server. | The try got no connection, because of a dial or TLS error, such as a refused connection. Or the answer of the try has the header `NotRunHeader`, `Hopbox-Not-Run`, with the value `1` ([the API server](/reference/api/#answers-of-calls-that-changed-nothing)). |

Each other call changes state and has no key, such as `CreateInvitation`. The client does not retry it after a lost answer, because the server can have run it. A second run can then act twice, for example with a second invitation. The client retries such a call only after a try that surely did not reach the server. The check holds for each try. A refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` on the first try, then a lost answer on the second try, ends the call with the error of the second try.

A try that ends without an answer can have run. A reset of an HTTP/2 stream, such as a server that drops the call, fails with `internal`, which never gets a retry. A try that waits for an answer until `AttemptTimeout` fails with `deadline_exceeded`. Only a call that is safe to run again then goes again.

`RefreshCLIToken` from a `TokenSource` is the one exception, as the owner decided on 2026-10-25. The refresh changes state and has no key. But the install takes a replaced refresh token once more within its `RefreshGrace` of 10 s ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). So after a lost answer, the client sends the refresh once more, if that retry starts within `RefreshReplayWindow`, 10 s, of the start of the first try. The wait before the retry counts. The same bound holds for every later try of the refresh after the lost answer, also a retry after a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run`, because each such try uses the one replay of the grace. The client gives up rather than start any of them later. Only `RefreshCLIToken` gets this retry, whatever the context of another call holds. The window starts before the install replaces the token, so a retry that reaches the install soon after its start falls within the grace. A retry that the network holds back past the grace counts as a reuse, and ends the CLI sign-in. A second lost answer fails the call. The other rules of the table still apply, so a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` before the lost answer does not use up the one retry.

The client reads `Hopbox-Not-Run` from the HTTP answer, so it also sees the header on an answer that is not a Connect error, such as the `502` page of an edge server. For this, `New` wraps the transport of `Options.HTTPClient` in a copy of that client. The wrapper also gives each HTTP request a copy of the header of the call. So a try that the attempt timeout ended can still be in the transport while the next try sets its header. The wrapper looks at each HTTP request of a try, and only the last one counts. The credential step can send a call twice in one try: after `unauthenticated`, it sends the call again with a new token. So a refusal with `Hopbox-Not-Run` before a request that ran does not let the call go again.

The client knows that a try got no connection from two signs. A `ConnectDone` event of `net/http/httptrace` reports a failed dial, before any `GotConn` event. Or the error is one that only a dial or a TLS handshake returns: a dial `*net.OpError`, a `*net.DNSError`, a `tls.RecordHeaderError`, or a `*tls.CertificateVerificationError`. Any other error counts as a try that can have run. So a transport of your own that reports no such events never makes a lost answer look like a request that never left. The edge servers use the same check (`internal/notrun`).

The wait before a retry has full jitter: a random time from 0 up to 500 ms before the first retry, and up to 1 s before the second. If the error has a `Retry-After` header, the client waits that time instead. The header holds seconds, or an HTTP date. The client reads at most `MaxRetryAfterHeader`, 24 hours, from either form, so a date far ahead counts as 24 hours. A wait of `LongWait`, 10 s, or more logs `retrying a call` at level warn. A shorter one logs it at level debug. The client does not retry in these cases:

* `MaxRetryAfter` is set, and `Retry-After` is longer.
* The wait ends after the deadline of the context of the call.
* The context of the call ends.
* The credential step failed, also for a read call. An example is a refresh of CLI tokens that failed after its own retries. One more refresh with the same token would end the CLI sign-in.

Each try has its own deadline, `AttemptTimeout`. A try that runs out of time fails with `deadline_exceeded`, and the table above applies.

## Errors

Each error of a call is an `*Error`. Other errors, such as one of the credential, stay as they are.

| `Error` field | Type              | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Code`        | `connect.Code`    | The code, such as `connect.CodeNotFound`.                                                                                                              |
| `Message`     | string            | The message of the server, without the code.                                                                                                           |
| `Procedure`   | string            | The call, such as `/hopbox.v1.OrgService/GetOrg`.                                                                                                      |
| `RequestID`   | string            | The `Hopbox-Request-Id` of the response ([the API server](/reference/api/#the-chain-of-a-call)). A call that did not reach the server has an empty ID. |
| `RetryAfter`  | `time.Duration`   | The `Retry-After` of the response, or 0.                                                                                                               |
| `Details`     | `[]proto.Message` | The typed details of the error, such as `*hopboxv1.MachineNameTaken`.                                                                                  |

`Error()` returns `<code>: <message>`, such as `not_found: not found: no org 01a1...`. `Unwrap` returns the `*connect.Error`, so `connect.CodeOf` works too.

`errors.Is(err, sentinel)` matches the code of an `*Error`. The codes are those of [the API server](/reference/api/#errors).

| Sentinel                | Code                  |
| ----------------------- | --------------------- |
| `ErrCanceled`           | `canceled`            |
| `ErrUnknown`            | `unknown`             |
| `ErrInvalidArgument`    | `invalid_argument`    |
| `ErrDeadlineExceeded`   | `deadline_exceeded`   |
| `ErrNotFound`           | `not_found`           |
| `ErrAlreadyExists`      | `already_exists`      |
| `ErrPermissionDenied`   | `permission_denied`   |
| `ErrResourceExhausted`  | `resource_exhausted`  |
| `ErrFailedPrecondition` | `failed_precondition` |
| `ErrAborted`            | `aborted`             |
| `ErrUnimplemented`      | `unimplemented`       |
| `ErrInternal`           | `internal`            |
| `ErrUnavailable`        | `unavailable`         |
| `ErrUnauthenticated`    | `unauthenticated`     |

| Other error    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ErrSignedOut` | The client has no live CLI sign-in: none in the store, the refresh token ended, the tokens belong to another install, or the install refused the refresh token. The way out is a new sign-in. |
| `ErrBadURL`    | `ParseURL` or `New` refused the URL.                                                                                                                                                          |

## Credentials

```go
type Credentials interface {
  Token(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}


type Renewer interface {
  Credentials
  Rejected(token string) bool
}
```

The client puts the token of `Credentials` in the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` of each try. If the credential fails, the call fails with that error, and no request goes out.

Sometimes the server refuses the token with `unauthenticated`, and the credential is a `Renewer`. Then the client calls `Rejected` with the token. If `Rejected` returns true, the client gets a token again. If the new token differs, the client sends the call once more with it. If getting the token fails with `ErrSignedOut`, the call returns that error.

`BearerToken` is a token that never changes, such as an API key. An empty `BearerToken` fails with `ErrSignedOut`.

### CLI tokens

`TokenSource` is a `Renewer` for the tokens of a CLI sign-in ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#cli-tokens)). `NewTokenSource(rawURL, store, opts)` makes one. It refreshes with its own client of `opts`, without a credential, because `RefreshCLIToken` must not carry an expired access token.

```go
type TokenStore interface {
  Lock(ctx context.Context) (unlock func(), err error)
  Load() (CLITokens, error)
  Save(CLITokens) error
  ClearIf(refreshToken string) error
}
```

The store keeps the tokens where every process of the CLI finds them. `Lock` holds off the `Lock` of every other process. With no tokens in the store, `Load` returns an error that wraps `ErrSignedOut`. The CLI keeps them in `credentials.toml` ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/#files)).

`CLITokens` has the fields `URL`, `AccountID`, `SignInID`, `AccessToken`, `AccessExpireTime`, `RefreshToken`, and `RefreshExpireTime`. `URL` is the install that issued the tokens. `TokensFrom(url, tokens)` makes `CLITokens` from the `CLITokens` message of the API.

`Token` works in these steps:

1. If the token in memory lives for more than `RefreshBefore`, 1 minute, and the server did not refuse it, return it.
2. Take the lock of the store, and load the tokens.
3. If the tokens belong to another install, fail with `ErrSignedOut`.
4. If the stored access token lives for more than 1 minute, and the server did not refuse it, keep it and return it. Another process refreshed meanwhile.
5. If the refresh token ended, fail with `ErrSignedOut`.
6. Call `RefreshCLIToken` with the stored refresh token. After a lost answer, the call goes once more within `RefreshReplayWindow` ([Retries](#retries)). If that answer gets lost too, fail, and keep the store as it is. The call waits at most `RefreshMaxRetryAfter`, 30 s, for a `Retry-After`. A shorter `MaxRetryAfter` of the options wins. The refresh holds the lock of the store, and every other process of the CLI waits for that lock. If the server refuses it, call `ClearIf` with that refresh token, and fail with `ErrSignedOut`. If the store still holds that refresh token, `ClearIf` deletes the stored tokens. Else it keeps them.
7. Save the new tokens, and return the new access token. If the save fails, call `ClearIf` with the old refresh token, log `the refreshed CLI tokens could not be stored, so the next command must sign in again` at level warn, and still return the token.

The install replaces the refresh token before step 7 saves the new one. Two cases leave the old refresh token in the store: the save and the `ClearIf` both fail, or the process dies between steps 6 and 7. The next refresh sends it again, and the install ends the sign-in as a reuse. The steps make this unlikely, but they cannot rule it out.

`Rejected(token)` forgets the token in memory, so the next `Token` reads the store again. Only a store that holds the same refused token leads to a refresh.

A replaced refresh token ends the sign-in, so these steps never send one. The store must have a real lock. The grace of 10 s of the install covers only one second refresh with the same token. So three processes that refresh at once without a lock end the sign-in. The store of the CLI refuses a dir without file locks ([hopbox CLI](/reference/cli/#files)). Two processes without a lock both get tokens through the grace, and the next refresh drops the second chain. Its process then reads the store again at the next refusal.

## Tests

* `internal/client/client_test.go` checks the retries, the waits, `Retry-After`, the idempotency keys, the typed errors, and the credentials against a fake API. Its table of retries covers a read call, a call with a key, and `CreateInvitation`, after a lost answer, an error code, an answer with `Hopbox-Not-Run`, and a refused connection. Other tests cover a reset stream, a hung answer, a resend with a new token after a refusal, a transport without connection events, and TLS with HTTP/2. `TestARefreshReplaysOnceWithinTheWindow` checks the one retry of a refresh, with a clock of the test, before and after the window.
* `internal/client/tokens_test.go` checks `TokenSource` with a store in memory.
* `internal/client/server_test.go` runs against a real install of `internal/api/apitest`. Four processes with one store make one refresh. Two processes without a lock both refresh through the grace, and the sign-in goes on after the next refresh. This shows the most that the grace covers. A sign-in that the console ends clears the store. One lost answer of a refresh recovers with no reuse, and the sign-in goes on. Two lost answers fail the call and keep the store as it is.

# hopboxd

> The commands, flags, logs, and exit status of hopboxd, with the start and stop order of hopboxd run, the leader jobs, install, upgrade and its rollback, enroll, preflight, and the admin commands for tokens, servers, admin API keys, orgs, machines, and images.

`hopboxd` is the server binary of hopbox. It runs on every server of an install.

## Usage

```sh
hopboxd [--log-level=LEVEL] <command> [flags]
```

When you run `hopboxd` without a command, it prints its help and an error, and exits with status 80.

## Global flags

A global flag goes before or after the command.

| Flag           | Type  | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ----- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--log-level`  | level | `info`  | The lowest level of the log records that `hopboxd` writes. The values are `debug`, `info`, `warn`, and `error`. Case does not matter. A value can also carry an offset, for example `info+2`, as in Go’s `log/slog`. |
| `-h`, `--help` | bool  | `false` | Prints the help of `hopboxd`, or of the command that it follows, and exits.                                                                                                                                          |

Example:

```sh
hopboxd --log-level=debug version
```

## Commands

| `admin maintenance off`               | Turns maintenance mode of the install off.                                                                                                                         |
| `admin db export`                     | Copies the control store of this server from the bundled Postgres to an empty external Postgres, in maintenance mode, and prints the config lines for it.          |
| `version`                             | Prints the version of `hopboxd`. See [the version command](/reference/version/).                                                                                   |
| `stop-guest`                          | Shuts down the guest of a machine unit. systemd runs it as the `ExecStop` of the unit. The help does not list it. See [stop-guest](#stop-guest).                   |

## run

```sh
hopboxd run [--config=PATH]
```

`run` reads the bootstrap config, starts the roles that the config lists, and runs until it gets `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`. Then it stops the roles and exits with status 0. [The bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/) lists the keys of the bootstrap config.

| Flag       | Type | Default                    | Description                |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `--config` | path | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config file. |

First, `run` starts the metrics listener. Then it starts the units of the control role, the DNS role, the edge role, and the node role, in this order. Then it starts the unit of the control channel. A role that the config does not list has no units. Each unit starts after the unit before it is ready.

| Order | Unit                | What it does
