Run hopboxd install first`                                                                                                      | The config or `/opt/hopbox/current` is missing.                                                                                                        |
| `the bundle <file> has the sha256 <got>, not <want>`                                                                                                                          | `--sha256` does not match. Nothing changed.                                                                                                            |
| `bundle: ...` or `the bundle <file>: ...`                                                                                                                                     | The bundle file is broken, unsafe, or differs from its manifest ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/#errors)). Nothing changed.                |
| `the release dir <dir> holds another build of <version>. Make the bundle with a new version`                                                                                  | Another build of the same version is in place.                                                                                                         |
| `this server has no previous release to roll back to`                                                                                                                         | `--rollback` before the first upgrade.                                                                                                                 |
| `the install of <version> failed, and <current> keeps running unless its start failed: ...`                                                                                   | The install of the new release failed. Its own error comes before this line. If it failed at the start of `hopboxd`, run `hopboxd upgrade --rollback`. |

### Tests of install and upgrade

| Test                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Where it runs                                 | What it checks                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `TestInstallUpgradeRollback`, `TestInstallCompletesADownloadedImage`, `TestInstallRefuses`, `TestFirstInstallNeedsADomain`, `TestInstallReportsAFailedStart`, `TestUpgradeRefuses`, `TestCheckSchema`, `TestInstallExternalPostgres`, `TestPlanConfig`, `TestReservePorts`, `TestLockRefusesASecondRun`, `TestLockAdoptsTheLockOfAnUpgrade`, `TestDirChecks`, `TestCheckIDs` | `make test`                                   | The steps of `internal/install` in temp dirs, with the bundled Postgres and a fake systemd. The tests cover a first install and a second install that changes nothing. They cover an upgrade that keeps the keys and the cluster, a rollback, and the removal of old releases. They also cover the Postgres guard, the schema check (`TestCheckSchema`), also with a newer migration that allows an older release, and each refusal with a config that stays the same. `TestInstallExternalPostgres` installs the control role on a TLS Postgres: a first install without a cluster and without users, the schema check on that Postgres, and a refusal of a wrong CA. Other tests cover the lock and its hand-off, and the checks of dirs and jailer IDs. They also cover a later run with another bootstrap key hash, and a restart that a stopped run left due. |
| `TestSystemdServer`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `make test-install`, and the CI job `install` | A Debian 13 container with systemd as PID 1. It refuses the node role on the overlay root, then installs from an unpacked bundle on a loop XFS. It checks the paths, modes, users, IDs, reserved ports, and `Type=notify`. A second install must not restart `hopboxd`. An install refuses a config of mode 0666, and a releases dir of another user. The upgrade refuses a bundle without `--sha256`, and a release that does not run with the newest schema migration of the store. An install with an enrollment token makes the server `ready`. It runs an upgrade with `--sha256` that keeps the domain and the key, refuses a bundle with Postgres 19, and rolls back. A transient unit in `hopbox-machines.slice` stands in for a microVM, and it keeps its process through every restart.                                                                  |

`make test-install` needs Docker that runs privileged containers, loop devices, and the kernel module `xfs`. It reads `PG_LINUX`, a Postgres install for `linux/amd64`. Without it, it runs `tools/pgdist -target linux/amd64`. The test is `internal/install/systemd_test.go`. It runs only with `HOPBOX_TEST_SYSTEMD=1`, and it reads the Postgres install from `HOPBOX_TEST_PG_LINUX`, or from `HOPBOX_PG_DIR` on a `linux/amd64` host.

## admin

```sh
hopboxd admin [--config=PATH] [--socket=PATH] <command> [flags]
```

`admin` calls the admin API of the `hopboxd` that runs on this server, through its admin socket ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#the-admin-socket)). The socket accepts only root and the user that runs `hopboxd`. On a server, `hopboxd` runs as root, so run `admin` with `sudo`. The audit log records each call, with the actor `local_root` ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#audit_log)).

| Flag       | Type | Default                    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--config` | path | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml` | The bootstrap config. `admin` calls the socket `<run_dir>/admin.sock` of this config ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). If the config does not load, `admin` prints `hopboxd: warning: <error>. Using the admin socket /run/hopbox/admin.sock` to standard error and calls that socket, so a bad config never locks you out. A missing default file gets no warning. |
| `--socket` | path | none                       | The admin socket. It overrides `--config`, and `admin` then reads no config.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

`admin` finds the admin socket in this order:

1. The path of `--socket`.
2. `<run_dir>/admin.sock` of the bootstrap config of `--config`, or of `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml`.
3. If the config does not load, `/run/hopbox/admin.sock`. Then `admin` prints a warning with the error of the config. If the default file does not exist, it prints no warning. Thus a broken config never locks the operator out of the socket.

Each `admin` command waits at most 40 s for its call.

### admin kek rotate

```sh
hopboxd admin kek rotate [--json]
```

Adds a new key-encryption key and makes it the current one. It calls `RotateKEK` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#rotatekek)) with a new idempotency key. It prints the ID of the new key.

Use `rotate` only with one control server. A rotation makes the new key current only on this server. So the command fails while the install has a control process on another host, live or not, with `failed_precondition: failed precondition: the install has a control server on <host> too, ...`. With more than one control server, run [admin kek stage](#admin-kek-stage) and then [admin kek promote](#admin-kek-promote).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                     |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"key_id":"<id>"}`, instead of the ID. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin kek rotate
file:2
```

### admin kek stage

```sh
hopboxd admin kek stage [--json]
```

Adds a new key-encryption key as a staged key file `<n>.staged` in the key dir of this server. A staged key opens values but seals none, so the current key stays the same. It calls `StageKEK` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#stagekek)). It prints the ID of the key, a tab, and the path of the file. Copy that file to the same path on every other control server, then run [admin kek promote](#admin-kek-promote) ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#several-control-servers)). hopbox does not copy the file for you yet. Use `scp` or `rsync` over SSH.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                               |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"key_id":"file:2","file":"/var/lib/hopbox/kek/2.staged"}`, instead of the line. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin kek stage
file:2  /var/lib/hopbox/kek/2.staged
```

### admin kek promote

```sh
hopboxd admin kek promote <id> [--json]
```

Makes the staged key `<id>`, such as `file:2`, the current key on every control server. It calls `PromoteKEK` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#promotekek)). It prints the ID when every other live control process seals with the key. The command can take longer than a few seconds, because it waits for the next renewal of each control process. It waits at most 40 s, like each `admin` command.

| Argument or flag | Type   | Default        | Description                                                       |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<id>`           | string | none, required | The ID of the staged key, such as `file:2`.                       |
| `--json`         | bool   | `false`        | Prints one JSON object, `{"key_id":"file:2"}`, instead of the ID. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin kek promote file:2
file:2
```

The command refuses while a live control process has no copy of the file. Copy the file and run the command again. If the 40 s end first, the command fails with `unavailable`, but the promote stays recorded and the control processes go on ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#several-control-servers)). See [Errors of admin](#errors-of-admin) for the errors.

### admin kek list

```sh
hopboxd admin kek list [--json]
```

Lists the key-encryption keys of the keyring, and the keys that sealed values name. It calls `ListKEKs` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listkeks)). Each line has the key ID, a tab, the number of sealed values that the key seals, a tab, and notes: `current` for the current key, `staged` for a staged key, and `missing from the keyring` for a key whose file is gone. The keys of the `.key` files come first, then the staged keys.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"keys":[{"id":"file:1","current":true,"staged":false,"in_keyring":true,"sealed_values":1}]}`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin kek list
file:1  1
file:2  0  current
```

A key with 0 sealed values can go. First back up the keyring dir ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#key-files)).

### admin kek rewrap

```sh
hopboxd admin kek rewrap [--json]
```

Moves every sealed value to the current key-encryption key. It calls `RewrapSealedValues` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#rewrapsealedvalues)). It prints `rewrapped <n> to <key ID>`, then the keys as `admin kek list` prints them.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                     |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `current_key_id`, `rewrapped`, and `keys`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin kek rewrap
rewrapped 1 to file:2
file:1  0
file:2  1  current
```

### admin config get

```sh
hopboxd admin config get [--json]
```

Prints the settings of the install. It calls `GetInstallConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getinstallconfig)).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `domain`, `public_addresses`, `acme_directory_url`, `acme_email`, `acme_terms_agreed`, `mail_transport`, `maintenance`, `version`, and `update_time`. `public_addresses` is an array. It is `[]` for an install without public addresses. `acme_terms_agreed` and `maintenance` are JSON booleans. |

The text output has one line for each setting: the name, a tab, and the value. An empty domain prints as an empty value. `public_addresses` joins the addresses by commas, in their order. An install without public addresses prints `-`. An empty `acme_email` prints `-`. `acme_terms_agreed` and `maintenance` print `true` or `false`. `mail_transport` prints `smtp` or `file` ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). `maintenance` is `true` in maintenance mode ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)).

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin config get
domain  example.com
public_addresses  203.0.113.10,2001:db8::10
acme_directory_url  https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
acme_email  ops@example.org
acme_terms_agreed  true
mail_transport  smtp
maintenance  false
version  4
update_time  2026-10-16T09:00:00Z
```

### admin config set

```sh
hopboxd admin config set [--domain=DOMAIN] [--public-address=IP,... | --no-public-addresses]
  [--acme-directory-url=URL] [--acme-email=EMAIL] [--[no-]acme-agree-terms]
  [--mail-transport=smtp|file] [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Changes the settings that the flags give, and keeps the others. It calls `UpdateInstallConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#updateinstallconfig)). Then it prints the settings, as `admin config get` does. Without a setting flag, it fails. A change of the domain or of the public addresses changes the zone of the DNS role ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/#the-zone-of-the-install)). The `--acme-` flags change the ACME settings ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/#settings)).

| Flag                    | Type                   | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--domain`              | string                 | none    | The new domain of the install. It must follow the rules in [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#install-domain).                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--public-address`      | IP address, repeatable | none    | A public address of the install, IPv4 or IPv6, at which the edge servers take traffic. Repeat the flag, or join the addresses by commas. The list replaces every public address of the install. Each address must follow the rules in [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#public-addresses). |
| `--no-public-addresses` | bool                   | `false` | Removes every public address of the install. It does not go with `--public-address`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--acme-directory-url`  | URL                    | none    | The ACME directory of the CA that issues the certificate of the install ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/#settings)). A new directory clears the agreement to the terms, unless `--acme-agree-terms` comes with it.                                                             |
| `--acme-email`          | string                 | none    | The contact email of the ACME account. An empty value, `--acme-email ""`, removes it from the install, but the CA keeps the old contact of the account.                                                                                                                                          |
| `--acme-agree-terms`    | bool                   | none    | Agrees to the terms of the CA of the ACME directory, so the install gets its certificate. `--no-acme-agree-terms` withdraws the agreement and stops new certificates. Without either flag, the agreement stays as it is.                                                                         |
| `--mail-transport`      | `smtp` or `file`       | none    | How the install delivers its mail ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)). `smtp` sends it through the SMTP server. `file` writes each mail to a file on the control server, for a dev or test install only. The SMTP config stays in both cases.                                             |
| `--expected-version`    | int                    | none    | The version `N` of the settings, as `admin config get` printed it. If the version is no longer `N`, the command fails with `aborted` and changes nothing.                                                                                                                                        |
| `--json`                | bool                   | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin config get --json` does.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin config set --domain example.com --json
{"domain":"example.com","public_addresses":[],"acme_directory_url":"https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory","acme_email":"","acme_terms_agreed":false,"mail_transport":"smtp","version":2,"update_time":"2026-10-16T09:00:00Z"}
$ sudo hopboxd admin config set --public-address 203.0.113.10 --public-address 2001:db8::10
domain  example.com
public_addresses  203.0.113.10,2001:db8::10
acme_directory_url  https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
acme_email  -
acme_terms_agreed  false
mail_transport  smtp
version  3
update_time  2026-10-16T09:05:00Z
$ sudo hopboxd admin config set --acme-email ops@example.org --acme-agree-terms
domain  example.com
public_addresses  203.0.113.10,2001:db8::10
acme_directory_url  https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
acme_email  ops@example.org
acme_terms_agreed  true
mail_transport  smtp
version  4
update_time  2026-10-16T09:06:00Z
```

| Error                                                                       | Cause                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `give at least one setting to change, such as --domain or --public-address` | The command has no setting flag.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `give --public-address or --no-public-addresses, not both`                  | The command has both flags.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `invalid_argument: invalid argument: invalid public address: ...`           | An address of `--public-address` breaks a rule of [Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#public-addresses), such as an address twice. The message names the address and the rule. |
| `invalid_argument: invalid argument: invalid ACME setting: ...`             | `--acme-directory-url` is not an `https` URL of a host, or `--acme-email` is not one plain email address.                                                                          |
| `--mail-transport "<value>" is not smtp or file`                            | `--mail-transport` has another value.                                                                                                                                              |
| `aborted: ...`                                                              | `--expected-version` is not the version of the settings now.                                                                                                                       |

### admin config smtp get

```sh
hopboxd admin config smtp get [--json]
```

Prints the SMTP config, without its password ([SMTP config](/reference/smtp/)). It calls `GetSMTPConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getsmtpconfig)). The text output has one line for each field: the name, a tab, and the value. The fields are `host`, `port`, `tls`, `username`, `password_set`, `from`, `mail_transport`, `version`, and `update_time`. An install without an SMTP config prints an empty host. `mail_transport` is the transport of the install, `smtp` or `file`. With `file`, the install does not use the SMTP server ([Mail](/reference/mail/#mail-transports)).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                  |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the same fields. |

### admin config smtp set

```sh
hopboxd admin config smtp set --host=HOST --from=ADDRESS [--port=PORT] [--tls=MODE]
  [--username=USER] [--password-stdin | --clear-password] [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Replaces the SMTP config, and prints it as `admin config smtp get` does. It calls `SetSMTPConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setsmtpconfig)). Without `--password-stdin` or `--clear-password`, the password that is set now stays.

| Flag                 | Type                         | Default                                    | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--host`             | string                       | none, required                             | The host name or the IP address of the SMTP server.                                                                                                                     |
| `--port`             | int                          | the usual port of `--tls`: 587, 465, or 25 | The TCP port.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--tls`              | `starttls`, `tls`, or `none` | `starttls`                                 | How the connection is encrypted ([SMTP config](/reference/smtp/#tls-modes)).                                                                                            |
| `--username`         | string                       | empty                                      | The SMTP login. It needs a password.                                                                                                                                    |
| `--password-stdin`   | bool                         | `false`                                    | Reads the password from standard input, at most 4096 bytes. A trailing newline is dropped. No flag takes the password, because the process list shows the command line. |
| `--clear-password`   | bool                         | `false`                                    | Removes the password.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--from`             | string                       | none, required                             | The sender, such as `"hopbox <no-reply@example.org>"`.                                                                                                                  |
| `--expected-version` | int                          | none                                       | The version `N` of the install config, as `admin config get` printed it. With another version, the command fails with `aborted` and changes nothing.                    |
| `--json`             | bool                         | `false`                                    | Prints one JSON object.                                                                                                                                                 |

A password needs a key-encryption key. [install](#install) makes the first one. On a server that `hopboxd install` did not set up, such as a dev run, run `admin kek rotate` first.

Example:

```text
$ printf '%s\n' "$SMTP_PASSWORD" | sudo hopboxd admin config smtp set \
    --host smtp.example.org --username hopbox@example.org --password-stdin \
    --from 'hopbox <no-reply@example.org>'
host  smtp.example.org
port  587
tls  starttls
username  hopbox@example.org
password_set  true
from  hopbox <no-reply@example.org>
mail_transport  smtp
version  3
update_time  2026-10-16T09:09:37Z
```

### admin config smtp clear

```sh
hopboxd admin config smtp clear [--json]
```

Removes the SMTP config and its password, so the install sends no more sign-in links. It calls `ClearSMTPConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#clearsmtpconfig)), and prints the empty config.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description             |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object. |

### admin config oauth get

```sh
hopboxd admin config oauth [get] [--json]
```

Prints the client of each sign-in provider, without its secret, and the redirect URI to register at the provider ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#redirect-uris)). It calls `GetOAuthConfig` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getoauthconfig)). `get` is the default, so `hopboxd admin config oauth` alone prints the same. The text output has one line for each provider, GitHub first. Each line has four fields with a tab between them: the provider, `on` or `off`, the client ID or `-`, and the redirect URI. Without a domain, the URI field is `- (set the domain first)`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object: `clients`, each with `provider`, `enabled`, `client_id`, `client_secret_set`, and `redirect_uri`, then `version` and `update_time`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin config oauth
github  on  Ov23liExampleClient  https://example.com/auth/github/callback
google  off  -  https://example.com/auth/google/callback
```

### admin config oauth set

```sh
hopboxd admin config oauth set PROVIDER --client-id=ID [--client-secret-stdin] [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Sets the client of one provider, and prints it as `admin config oauth get` does. It calls `SetOAuthClient` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setoauthclient)). `PROVIDER` is `github` or `google`.

| Flag                    | Type   | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--client-id`           | string | none, required | The client ID that the provider gave.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--client-secret-stdin` | bool   | `false`        | Reads the client secret from standard input, at most 4096 bytes. A trailing newline is dropped. No flag takes the secret, because the process list shows the command line. Without this flag, the secret that is set now stays. That works only for the same client ID. |
| `--expected-version`    | int    | none           | The version `N` of the install config, as `admin config get` printed it. With another version, the command fails with `aborted` and changes nothing.                                                                                                                    |
| `--json`                | bool   | `false`        | Prints one JSON object.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

A secret needs a key-encryption key, as an SMTP password does. On a server that `hopboxd install` did not set up, run `admin kek rotate` first.

Example:

```text
$ printf '%s\n' "$GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET" | sudo hopboxd admin config oauth set github \
    --client-id Ov23liExampleClient --client-secret-stdin
github  on  Ov23liExampleClient  https://example.com/auth/github/callback
```

| Message                                                                       | Cause                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `standard input holds no client secret`                                       | `--client-secret-stdin` read nothing.                                                                    |
| `invalid_argument: invalid argument: a new client ID needs its client secret` | The provider has no client with this client ID, and the command has no `--client-secret-stdin`.          |
| `invalid_argument: invalid argument: ...`                                     | The client ID or the secret breaks a rule of [Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#config). |
| `failed_precondition: ...`                                                    | The keyring has no key-encryption key.                                                                   |
| `aborted: ...`                                                                | `--expected-version` is not the version of the install config now.                                       |

### admin config oauth clear

```sh
hopboxd admin config oauth clear PROVIDER [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Removes the client of one provider and its secret, so nobody can start a sign-in with it. It calls `ClearOAuthClient` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#clearoauthclient)), and prints the empty client with its redirect URI. The sign-in methods of the provider stay on their accounts.

| Flag                 | Type | Default | Description                      |
| -------------------- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------- |
| `--expected-version` | int  | none    | As for `admin config oauth set`. |
| `--json`             | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object.          |

### admin certificate get

```sh
hopboxd admin certificate get [--json]
```

Prints the wildcard certificate of the install, without its key, and the state of the ACME job ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/)). It calls `GetCertificate` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getcertificate)).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `certificate` and `status`. `certificate` is `null` before the first certificate. Else it holds `domain`, `names` (an array), `serial`, `issuer`, `not_before`, `not_after`, `renew_time`, `directory_url`, and `update_time`. `status` holds `failures`, `last_attempt_time`, `last_error`, `next_attempt_time`, `ca_wait`, `terms_url`, and `renewals_stopped`. A time that is absent is `null`. |

The text output has one line for each field: the name, a tab, and the value. `names` joins the names by commas. An empty value prints `-`. Before the first certificate, the fields of the certificate are one line `certificate -`.

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin certificate get
domain  example.com
names  example.com,*.example.com
serial  4553a65221ea631b
issuer  CN=Pebble Intermediate CA 512ad8
not_before  2026-10-20T22:58:39Z
not_after  2027-01-18T22:58:38Z
renew_time  2026-12-19T22:58:38Z
directory_url  https://localhost:14000/dir
update_time  2026-10-20T22:58:44Z
failures  0
last_attempt_time  2026-10-20T22:58:38Z
last_error  -
next_attempt_time  -
ca_wait  false
terms_url  data:text/plain,Do%20what%20thou%20wilt
renewals_stopped  -
```

After a failed attempt, `last_error` names the cause:

```text
failures  1
last_attempt_time  2026-10-20T23:30:29Z
last_error  read the ACME directory: provisioning client: performing request: Get "https://localhost:1/dir": dial tcp [::1]:1: connect: connection refused
next_attempt_time  2026-10-20T23:31:30Z
ca_wait  false
terms_url  data:text/plain,Do%20what%20thou%20wilt
renewals_stopped  -
```

### admin login-link

```sh
hopboxd admin login-link --email=EMAIL [--json]
```

Prints a one-time sign-in link for the first instance admin. It calls `CreateLoginLink` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createloginlink)). The link works once, for 15 minutes. It signs in to the account of earlier login links for the email, or to a new account, and makes that account an instance admin. The email stays unverified, so the account never links to another sign-in method with that email ([Sessions, cookies, and sign-in links](/reference/sessions/#what-a-sign-in-does)).

The command prints the link on standard output, and the email and the end of the link on standard error. The install must have a domain. The audit log records the link with the actor `local_root`, but never its token. Treat the link as a password until its use or its end.

| Flag      | Type   | Default        | Description                                                             |
| --------- | ------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--email` | string | none, required | The email of the account.                                               |
| `--json`  | bool   | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the keys `url`, `email`, and `expire_time`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin login-link --email root@example.org
https://example.com/auth/login-link#token=tOzJ8YQyibHutrU34tIWLHnGd5XlzYs4WoIBXgSDh5I
The link signs in root@example.org once, until 2026-10-16T09:24:15Z.
```

[First sign-in on a new install](/guide/first-sign-in/) uses the link on a new install.

### admin instance-admin list

```sh
hopboxd admin instance-admin list [--json]
```

Lists the instance admins, in the order of their grant. It calls `ListInstanceAdmins` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listinstanceadmins)). Each line has the account ID, a tab, the emails, a tab, and the time of the grant. An unverified email ends with `(unverified)`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"admins":[...]}`. Each admin has the keys `account_id`, `display_name`, `emails` (each with `email` and `verified`), and `grant_time`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin instance-admin list
01a143f9-1cee-7ec0-9238-7976abaacfd6  root@example.org (unverified)  2026-10-16T09:09:21Z
```

### admin instance-admin grant

```sh
hopboxd admin instance-admin grant (--account-id=ID | --email=EMAIL)
```

Makes an account an instance admin, and prints its ID. It calls `GrantInstanceAdmin` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#grantinstanceadmin)). Root on a control server can always make an account an instance admin, as a way to recover.

| Flag           | Type   | Default | Description                                                            |
| -------------- | ------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--account-id` | string | none    | The UUID of the account.                                               |
| `--email`      | string | none    | A verified email of the account. An unverified email names no account. |

Give exactly one of the two flags.

### admin instance-admin revoke

```sh
hopboxd admin instance-admin revoke --account-id=ID
```

Takes the instance admin role from an account. It calls `RevokeInstanceAdmin` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#revokeinstanceadmin)). An install keeps at least one instance admin, so the command fails for the last one.

| Flag           | Type   | Default        | Description              |
| -------------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------------------ |
| `--account-id` | string | none, required | The UUID of the account. |

### admin account sign-in-method list

```sh
hopboxd admin account sign-in-method list (--account-id=ID | --email=EMAIL) [--json]
```

Lists the sign-in methods of an account, oldest first. It calls `ListAccountSignInMethods` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listaccountsigninmethods)). The text output has one line per method, with a tab between the fields: the ID, the kind, the subject, the email, and the time of the last use.

| Flag           | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--account-id` | string | none    | The UUID of the account. Give it or `--email`.                                                                                      |
| `--email`      | string | none    | A verified email of the account.                                                                                                    |
| `--json`       | bool   | `false` | Prints one JSON object: `account_id` and `methods`, each with `id`, `kind`, `subject`, `email`, `last_use_time`, and `create_time`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin account sign-in-method list --email erin@example.org
01a15c02-7d1e-7a4c-9b51-2b1c5e8f0a7d  github  4242  erin@example.org  2026-10-21T09:12:04Z
```

### admin account sign-in-method remove

```sh
hopboxd admin account sign-in-method remove --account-id=ID --method-id=ID [--allow-last]
```

Removes one sign-in method of an account. It calls `RemoveAccountSignInMethod` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeaccountsigninmethod)). Use it for a person who lost the only method of the account, for example the GitHub user ([Sign-in with GitHub and Google](/reference/oauth/#recover-a-lost-identity)). The command prints nothing. It does not end the sessions or the CLI sign-ins that the method started ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#removeaccountsigninmethod)).

| Flag           | Type   | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--account-id` | string | none, required | The UUID of the account, as `list` prints it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--method-id`  | string | none, required | The UUID of the method.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--allow-last` | bool   | `false`        | Removes also the last method. The account then has no identity of a provider, so it signs in through a new method that proves one of its verified emails, such as a magic link. An account without a verified email keeps its last method, and the command fails with `failed_precondition`. |

### admin enrollment-token create

```sh
hopboxd admin enrollment-token create [--pool=NAME] [--roles=ROLE,...] [--server=ID] [--json]
```

Makes an enrollment token with which one new server joins a pool, with some of the roles of the token. The token works once and expires after 1 hour. It calls `CreateEnrollmentToken` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createenrollmenttoken)) with a new idempotency key. It prints the token alone on one line, so a script can keep it in a variable. The token is a secret. The install keeps only a hash of its secret, so this output is its only copy. The first token of an install makes the install CA, so the install needs a key-encryption key first. [install](#install) makes it, and [admin kek rotate](#admin-kek-rotate) makes it on a server that `hopboxd install` did not set up.

| Flag       | Type                              | Default   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--pool`   | string                            | `default` | The pool that the new server joins. Every install has the pool `default`.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--roles`  | list of strings, joined by commas | `node`    | The roles that the new server can enroll with: `node`, `dns`, `edge`, or more than one.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `--server` | string                            | none      | The ID of an enrolled server. The token then adds the roles to that server alone, in its pool, and enrolls no new server ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/#add-roles-to-an-enrolled-server)). It ignores `--pool`. |
| `--json`   | bool                              | `false`   | Prints one JSON object with the keys `token`, `token_id`, `pool`, `roles`, `expire_time` (UTC), and `ca_hash`. A token with `--server` also has `server_id`.                                                                              |

Example:

```text
$ TOKEN="$(sudo hopboxd admin enrollment-token create)"
$ sudo hopboxd admin enrollment-token create --json
{"token":"hbxe_<id>_<secret>_<cahash>","token_id":"01a14404-...","pool":"default","roles":["node"],"expire_time":"2026-10-16T10:00:00Z","ca_hash":"<cahash>"}
```

### admin server list

```sh
hopboxd admin server list [--json]
```

Lists the enrolled servers, oldest enrollment first. It calls `ListServers` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listservers)). The text output is a table. Its columns are `ID`, `POOL`, `STATE`, `STATUS`, `ROLES`, `HOSTNAME`, `VERSION`, and `LAST HEARTBEAT`. `VERSION` is the version of `hopboxd` on the server. `LAST HEARTBEAT` is an RFC 3339 time. An empty value prints as `-`. With no server, the table has only its header.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"servers":[...]}`, with one object for each server, as `admin server get --json` prints it. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin server list
ID                                    POOL     STATE  STATUS  ROLES  HOSTNAME  VERSION  LAST HEARTBEAT
01a14404-ce7b-72d9-b18e-5006c3e462db  default  ready  ok      node   server1   v0.1.0   2026-10-16T09:00:05Z
```

### admin server get

```sh
hopboxd admin server get <id> [--json]
```

Prints the server with the ID `<id>`. It calls `GetServer` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getserver)). The text output has one line for each field: the name, a tab, and the value. The lines are these:

* `id`, `pool`, `hostname`, and `roles` (joined by commas)
* `state`, `cordoned` (`true` or `false`), `status`, and `problems` (joined by `; `)
* `labels` (`key=value` pairs sorted by key, joined by commas), and `labels_set_by_admin` (`true` or `false`)
* `hopboxd_version`, `kernel_release`, `cpu` (the arch, the vendor, and the model name), `cpu_template`, and `compatibility_class`
* `cpu_threads`, `memory_bytes`, `disk_bytes`, `disk_free_bytes`, `machine_count`, and `allocations` and `actions` (their counts)
* `last_heartbeat_time` (empty before the first heartbeat), `enroll_time`, `certificate_expire_time`, `version`, and `update_time`
* `mesh_address`, `mesh_vrack_address`, and `mesh_public_key`: the part of the server in the mesh, empty for a server outside the mesh ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/))

Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. `state` is `ready`, `cordoned`, `unresponsive`, or `decommissioned`. `status` is `ok`, `degraded`, or empty before the first heartbeat.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description             |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object. |

The JSON object has these keys:

* `id`, `pool`, `hostname`, `roles`, `state`, `cordoned`, `status`, and `problems`
* `labels`, `labels_set_by_admin`, `machine_count`, `hopboxd_version`, and `kernel_release`
* `cpu`: an object with `arch`, `vendor`, `family`, `model`, `stepping`, `model_name`, `microcode`, `flags_hash`, and `cpu_template`
* `compatibility_class`
* `capacity`: an object with `cpu_threads`, `memory_bytes`, `disk_bytes`, and `disk_free_bytes`
* `allocations`: a list of objects with `machine_id`, `vcpus`, `memory_bytes`, and `disk_bytes`
* `actions`: a list of objects with `machine_id`, `action`, and `start_time`
* `last_heartbeat_time` (`null` before the first heartbeat), `enroll_time`, `certificate_expire_time`, `version`, and `update_time`
* `mesh`: an object with `address`, `vrack_address`, and `public_key`, or `null` for a server outside the mesh

Lists and the `labels` object are empty, never `null`. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#server) describes each field.

### admin machine list

```sh
hopboxd admin machine list [--org-id=ID] [--json]
```

Lists the machines of every org, or of one org, in the order of their IDs, with metadata only. It calls `ListMachines` of the admin API, page by page, until the last page ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listmachines)). A machine whose current state is `deleted` is not in the list. Each line has six parts, with a tab between them. They are the machine ID, the name, and `org=` with the org ID. Then come the current state, `target=` with the target state, and `server=` with the server ID of its node. A state is printed as the domain names it, for example `running` ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-states)).

| Flag       | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------- | ------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--org-id` | string | none    | Lists only the machines of this org.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--json`   | bool   | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"machines":[...]}`. Each machine has the keys `id`, `org_id`, `name`, `state`, `target_state`, `size` (the size name), and `image_digest`. It also has `creator_account_id`, `creator_key_id`, `shared`, `server_id`, `ssh_port`, `url`, `delete_request_time`, `version`, and `create_time`. An unset ID is the empty string. An unset `delete_request_time` is `null`. The times are in RFC 3339 form, in UTC. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin machine list
01a1460c-1f6e-7b8a-9c42-3d5e7f8a9b10  box1  org=01a14565-8448-7753-9c1f-5ec0a86b8d92  pending  target=running  server=01a14403-6bd1-7522-9ab0-b3ab4517e0e4
```

### admin machine stop

```sh
hopboxd admin machine stop (--name=NAME | --id=ID) [--json]
```

Sets the target of any machine to `stopped`, also in a suspended org, and waits for it. It calls `StopMachine` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#stopmachine)). It prints one line per fact: a name, a tab, and a value. The facts are `id`, `name`, `state`, `target_state`, `duration`, and `done`.

The API waits for up to 60 s. But each `admin` command waits at most 40 s for its call. So the wait ends after about 39 s, 1 s before the deadline of the command. A wait that ends before the machine is stopped prints `done` `false`, and the command still succeeds. The machine goes on toward its target.

| Flag     | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name` | string | none    | The name of the machine. Give `--name` or `--id`, not both.                                                                                    |
| `--id`   | string | none    | The UUID of the machine.                                                                                                                       |
| `--json` | bool   | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `machine` (with the keys of `admin machine list --json`), `duration` (for example `39.001s`), and `done`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin machine stop --name box1
id  01a1460c-1f6e-7b8a-9c42-3d5e7f8a9b10
name  box1
state  stopped
target_state  stopped
duration  512ms
done  true
```

The executor of the node stops the microVM of the machine ([the node executor](/reference/executor/)). The guest of the default image shuts down in less than a second ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#stop)).

### admin machine delete

```sh
hopboxd admin machine delete (--name=NAME | --id=ID) [--json]
```

Sets the target of any machine to `deleted`, also in a suspended org, and waits for it, as `admin machine stop` does. It calls `DeleteMachine` of the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#deletemachine)). The name and the SSH port of the machine stay reserved for its org for 7 days. The output is that of `admin machine stop`.

| Flag     | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                  |
| -------- | ------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--name` | string | none    | The name of the machine. Give `--name` or `--id`, not both.                                                  |
| `--id`   | string | none    | The UUID of the machine.                                                                                     |
| `--json` | bool   | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `machine`, `duration`, and `done`, as `admin machine stop --json` does. |

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin machine delete --id 01a1460c-1f6e-7b8a-9c42-3d5e7f8a9b10
```

### The default image of the release

Each release ships its own default image, because the image holds `hopbox-guest` of the same commit ([Release bundle](/reference/release-bundle/#the-default-image-in-the-bundle)). So at each start, the control role registers the image of `control.release_image`, by default `/opt/hopbox/current/image/artifact.json` ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). New machines of the name `default` then take the guest agent of the release. Machines that exist keep their image.

The rules are simple:

* The start registers the image by its digest. If the install has the digest already, the start changes nothing and writes no audit entry. So a restart of the same release changes nothing. When two control servers start at once, one of them adds the image, and the other one finds it.
* A new image gets the audit entry `image.register` with the actor `local_root` and the detail `already` `false`, as `admin image register` as root does.
* The start registers only the image of the release, under its own name. It never changes or removes an image of another name.
* New machines take the image of a name that the install registered last. So an image that an operator registers after the start wins, also an older build. It wins until a release brings an image that the install does not have yet. To keep an image of your own across releases, give it another name, and create machines with that image name.
* A rollback does not bring its image back. `hopboxd upgrade --rollback` starts the older release, whose image the install has already. So new machines keep the image of the newer release, with its guest agent. A register of the older image changes nothing either, because the install has its digest. Each guest agent takes the versions of the guest link that its node speaks ([Guest link](/reference/guest-link/#versions)).
* In phase 2, an install can have control servers on two releases, for example during an upgrade. At its start, the control role skips the register when the install has an image of the same name that a newer release registered. It compares the releases as semver versions. So a control server on the older release never makes its image the newest. The start logs `the install has the default image of a newer release, so the control role registers none`, and changes nothing. The control role records its release on the images that it registers. An operator image has no release, and so has an image that a release before migration `0045` registered. Neither makes the control role skip. A version that is not semver, such as a build for development, skips nothing. The start does not compare the build times, because a reproducible build of the image has a fixed build time. The check and the register run in one transaction under the lock `LockKeyReleaseImages`, so two control servers of two releases that start at once never both register ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#advisory-lock-keys)). After a full rollback of every control server to the older release, the image of the newer release stays the newest of its name, because the older release skips its own. Register the older image by hand with `admin image register` if you want it back.

Only a server with the control role registers the image. The nodes still need the disk of the image: the install of a release puts it into the image cache of a node ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#the-image-cache)).

### admin image register

```sh
hopboxd admin image register ARTIFACT_JSON [--url=URL] [--json]
```

Adds an image from its `artifact.json`, for example the one of `make image` in `bin/image/` ([Default image](/reference/default-image/)). It reads the file and calls `RegisterImage` with its bytes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#registerimage)). New machines take the newest image of a name. A second call with the same file changes nothing, and prints `registered` `false`. Without `--json`, it prints the lines `id`, `name`, `digest`, and `registered`, each with a tab before its value.

| Argument or flag | Type   | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ARTIFACT_JSON`  | path   | none, required | The `artifact.json` of the image. A file that does not exist exits with status 80.                                                                                                                         |
| `--url`          | string | empty          | An https URL from which nodes download the compressed disk.                                                                                                                                                |
| `--json`         | bool   | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the keys `image` and `registered`. `image` has the keys `id`, `name`, `digest`, `arch`, `kernel_sha256`, `disk_size`, `disk_sha256`, `url`, `build_time`, and `register_time`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin image register bin/image/artifact.json --url https://dl.example.org/images/default/disk.raw.zst
id  01a1460a-7c21-7d4e-8f90-1a2b3c4d5e6f
name  default
digest  sha256:422d31d7a4fd5e6958162b22e3d772f71b5a1465cbd6255d253ae8c087873dc8
registered  true
```

### admin server cordon

```sh
hopboxd admin server cordon <id> [--json]
```

Stops new machines from landing on the server `<id>`. Its machines keep running. It calls `CordonServer` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#cordonserver)) and prints the server after the change, as `admin server get` does. A cordon of a cordoned server changes nothing. A server that is unresponsive stays unresponsive, and comes back `cordoned` with its next heartbeat.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin server get --json` does. |

### admin server uncordon

```sh
hopboxd admin server uncordon <id> [--json]
```

Lets new machines land on the server `<id>` again. It calls `UncordonServer` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#uncordonserver)) and prints the server after the change, as `admin server get` does. An uncordon of a server that is not cordoned changes nothing.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin server get --json` does. |

### admin server set-labels

```sh
hopboxd admin server set-labels <id> [--label=KEY=VALUE ...] [--json]
```

Replaces the labels of the server `<id>`. It calls `SetServerLabels` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setserverlabels)) and prints the server after the change, as `admin server get` does. The labels replace every label of the server. Without `--label`, the server gets no labels. From then on, the install keeps these labels, and `channel.labels` of the bootstrap config of the server has no effect. The hopbox Terraform provider runs this command over SSH on the first server of an install ([hopbox Terraform provider](/reference/terraform-provider/)).

| Flag      | Type        | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ----------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--label` | `KEY=VALUE` | none    | A label of the server. Repeat the flag for each label. The rules of `channel.labels` apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). |
| `--json`  | bool        | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin server get --json` does.                                                                                                       |

Example:

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin server set-labels 01a14404-ce7b-72d9-b18e-5006c3e462db --label zone=gra --label disk=nvme
```

### admin server decommission

```sh
hopboxd admin server decommission <id> [--json]
```

Takes the server `<id>` out of the install for good. Do not run it on a server that Terraform manages. Run `terraform destroy` instead. After a decommission outside Terraform, the provider keeps the first server in its state. A new create erases the install. It calls `DecommissionServer` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#decommissionserver)) and prints the server after the change, as `admin server get` does. The install refuses the certificates of the server from then on, and `hopboxd` on that server retries once a minute without success. The command refuses a server that still holds machines. It also refuses a server that hosts a live control process, while no live control process runs on another host and other servers belong to the install. A decommission of a decommissioned server changes nothing.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin server get --json` does. |

### admin control list

```sh
hopboxd admin control list [--json]
```

Lists the control processes that recorded themselves in the control store, oldest start first. A control process is one run of the control role, on this server or on another one. The control role never enrolls, so `admin server list` does not show it. The command calls `ListControlProcesses` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listcontrolprocesses)). A process that ended without its stop, for example after a crash, stays in the list for 24 hours with `LIVE` set to `false`. The text output is a table. Its columns are `ID`, `LIVE`, `HOSTNAME`, `INTERNAL URL`, `RELEASE`, `SCHEMA`, `KEKS`, `MAINTENANCE`, and `LAST RENEWAL`. `SCHEMA` is the schema version of the `hopboxd` of the process. `KEKS` joins the IDs of the key files and the staged key files of the process by commas. `MAINTENANCE` is `off`, `draining` while the process applies maintenance mode and still runs work that it stops, or `drained`. `LAST RENEWAL` is an RFC 3339 time in UTC. An empty value prints as `-`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                      |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"processes":[...]}`, with one object for each process. |

Each object has the keys `id`, `server_id`, `hostname`, `internal_url`, `release`, `schema_version`, `kek_ids`, `kek_current`, `maintenance`, `drained`, `live`, `start_time`, `renew_time`, `stop_time`, and `version`. `server_id` is empty when no role of the same `hopboxd` enrolled. `stop_time` is `null` unless the process stopped cleanly. `kek_ids` is an empty list, never `null`. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#controlprocess) describes each field.

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin control list
ID                                    LIVE  HOSTNAME  INTERNAL URL            RELEASE  SCHEMA  KEKS     MAINTENANCE  LAST RENEWAL
01a14404-ce7b-72d9-b18e-5006c3e462db  true  control1  https://172.31.0.11:7443  v0.2.0   45      default  off          2026-10-26T09:00:05Z
```

### admin pool create

```sh
hopboxd admin pool create <name> [--ovh-plan=PLAN] [--json]
```

Adds the pool `<name>` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createpool)). It sends a new idempotency key with the call. It prints the pool, one field on each line: the name of the field, a tab, and the value. The fields are `id`, `name`, `ovh_plan`, `hardware`, `server_count`, `size_count`, `version`, `create_time`, and `update_time`. `hardware` is `-` until the first server enrolls into the pool.

| Flag         | Type   | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ovh-plan` | string | none    | The OVHcloud plan code of the servers of the pool, such as `24adv01`. Leave it out for a pool of adopted servers.                                                                                                                         |
| `--json`     | bool   | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the fields of the message `Pool` as keys. `hardware` is `null` before the first enrollment, else an object with `cpu_model`, `cpu_threads`, `memory_bytes`, and `disk_bytes`. The times are in RFC 3339 form. |

Example:

```sh

```
