### admin pool list

```sh
hopboxd admin pool list [--json]
```

Lists the pools, by name, in a table ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listpools)). The columns are `NAME`, `OVH PLAN`, `SERVERS`, `SIZES`, and `HARDWARE`. `SERVERS` counts the servers that are not decommissioned, and `SIZES` the sizes that name the pool and are not retired. `-` stands for an empty plan, and for a pool without hardware.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"pools":[...]}`, with the keys of `admin pool create --json` for each pool. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin pool list
NAME     OVH PLAN  SERVERS  SIZES  HARDWARE
big      24adv01   2        1      AMD EPYC 4244P 6-Core Processor, 12 CPU threads, 62.5 GiB of RAM, disks 960 GB, 960 GB
default  -         1        0      -
```

### admin pool delete

```sh
hopboxd admin pool delete <name>
```

Deletes the pool `<name>` and frees its name ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#deletepool)). It prints nothing on success. It refuses the pool `default`, a pool with a server that is not decommissioned, and a pool that a live size names.

### admin size create

```sh
hopboxd admin size create <name> --vcpus=N --memory-gib=N --disk-gb=N [--pool=NAME] [--label=KEY=VALUE ...] [--json]
```

Adds the size `<name>` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createsize)). It sends a new idempotency key with the call. A size never changes. To change one, add a size with a new name, and retire the old one. The command prints the size, one field on each line: the name of the field, a tab, and the value. The fields are `name`, `vcpus`, `memory_bytes`, `disk_bytes`, `pool`, `labels`, `retire_time`, `version`, `create_time`, and `update_time`. `labels` holds the `KEY=VALUE` pairs, sorted by key and joined by commas. `retire_time` is empty while the size takes new machines.

| Flag           | Type        | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--vcpus`      | int         | none, required | The count of vCPUs, 1 to 32.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--memory-gib` | int         | none, required | The RAM, in GiB. It must be 1 or more.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--disk-gb`    | int         | none, required | The size of the sparse disk, in GB. It must be 1 or more.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--pool`       | string      | none           | The pool of the machines of the size. Leave it out for any pool.                                                                                                                                             |
| `--label`      | `KEY=VALUE` | none           | A label that a node must have to take a machine of the size. Repeat the flag for each label. The rules of the labels of a server apply ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). |
| `--json`       | bool        | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the fields of the message `Size` as keys. `retire_time` is `null` while the size takes new machines. The times are in RFC 3339 form.                                             |

Example:

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin size create large --vcpus 8 --memory-gib 32 --disk-gb 200 --pool big --label disk=nvme
```

### admin size get

```sh
hopboxd admin size get <name> [--json]
```

Prints the size `<name>`, also a retired one, as `admin size create` does ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getsize)).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin size create --json` does. |

### admin size list

```sh
hopboxd admin size list [--all] [--json]
```

Lists the sizes, smallest first, in a table ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listsizes)). The columns are `NAME`, `VCPUS`, `RAM`, `DISK`, `POOL`, `LABELS`, and `RETIRED`. `RAM` is in GiB, or in MiB for a size that is not a whole number of GiB. `DISK` is in GB, or in bytes for a size that is not a whole number of GB. `RETIRED` is the time of the retirement, or `-`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                           |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--all`  | bool | `false` | Also lists the retired sizes.                                                                         |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"sizes":[...]}`, with the keys of `admin size create --json` for each size. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin size list
NAME     VCPUS  RAM     DISK    POOL  LABELS     RETIRED
default  2      8 GiB   100 GB  -     -          -
large    8      32 GiB  200 GB  big   disk=nvme  -
```

### admin size retire

```sh
hopboxd admin size retire <name> [--json]
```

Stops new machines of the size `<name>` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#retiresize)). Its machines keep running and keep their size. Its name stays taken. It prints the size after the change, as `admin size create` does. A retirement of a retired size changes nothing. The command refuses the size `default`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, as `admin size create --json` does. |

### admin org list

```sh
hopboxd admin org list [--json]
```

Lists every org of the install, oldest first, with metadata only. It calls `ListOrgs` of the admin API, page by page, until the last page ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listorgs)). Each line has six parts, with a tab between them. They are the org ID, the name, and `personal` or `org`. Then come `members=` and the member count, `active` or `suspended`, and `machines=` with the machines in use, a slash, and their limit.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"orgs":[...]}`. Each org has the fields of the message `Org` of the admin API as keys ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#orgservice)). The times are in RFC 3339 form. An override without a value is `null`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin org list
01a14565-8448-7753-9c1f-5ec0a86b8d92  Personal  personal  members=1  active  machines=0/3
01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4  Team  org  members=2  active  machines=0/3
```

### admin org suspend

```sh
hopboxd admin org suspend --org-id=ID [--reason=TEXT] [--json]
```

Suspends an org, and prints it. It calls `SuspendOrg` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#suspendorg)). The members of the org see the reason. Its owners and admins see the audit entry. A suspended org stays as it is, with its first reason.

| Flag       | Type   | Default        | Description                                                           |
| ---------- | ------ | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--org-id` | string | none, required | The UUID of the org.                                                  |
| `--reason` | string | empty          | The reason, which the members of the org see. At most 256 characters. |
| `--json`   | bool   | `false`        | Prints the org as one JSON object, with the keys of `admin org list`. |

Without `--json`, the command prints one line per fact: a name, a tab, and a value. Each limit line holds the usage, a slash, and the limit, in bytes for RAM and disk.

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin org suspend --org-id 01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4 --reason 'spam reports'
id  01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4
name  Team
members  2
state  suspended
suspend_time  2026-10-16T15:47:41Z
suspend_reason  spam reports
machines  0/10
vcpus  0/6
memory_bytes  0/68719476736
disk_bytes  0/300000000000
version  3
```

A personal org also prints the line `personal_account_id`.

### admin org unsuspend

### admin org set-limits

```sh
hopboxd admin org set-limits --org-id=ID [--machines=N] [--vcpus=N] [--memory-gib=N] [--disk-gb=N] [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Replaces the usage limits of one org, and prints the org as `admin org suspend` does. It calls `SetOrgLimits` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setorglimits)). A limit that you leave out takes the default of the install. So `set-limits` with only `--org-id` puts the org back on the defaults.

| Flag                 | Type   | Default        | Description                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--org-id`           | string | none, required | The UUID of the org.                                                                                                |
| `--machines`         | int32  | the default    | The most machines.                                                                                                  |
| `--vcpus`            | int32  | the default    | The most vCPUs of all machines together.                                                                            |
| `--memory-gib`       | int64  | the default    | The most RAM of all machines together, in GiB (2^30 bytes).                                                         |
| `--disk-gb`          | int64  | the default    | The most disk of all machines together, in GB (10^9 bytes).                                                         |
| `--expected-version` | int64  | none           | The version that the org must have now. With another version, the command changes nothing and fails with `aborted`. |
| `--json`             | bool   | `false`        | Prints the org as one JSON object.                                                                                  |

Each limit is 0 or more. The command refuses a negative `--memory-gib` or `--disk-gb`, and the API refuses a negative `--machines` or `--vcpus` with `invalid_argument`.

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin org set-limits --org-id 01a14565-a2df-75a1-9401-ed28dfa37fc4 --machines 10 --memory-gib 64
```

### admin org default-limits get

```sh
hopboxd admin org default-limits get [--json]
```

Prints the limits of every org without its own limits. It calls `GetDefaultOrgLimits` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getdefaultorglimits)).

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                          |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object with the keys `limits`, `max_orgs_per_account`, `version`, and `update_time`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin org default-limits get
machines  3
vcpus  6
memory_bytes  25769803776
disk_bytes  300000000000

```

The version is that of the whole install config.

### admin org default-limits set

```sh
hopboxd admin org default-limits set [--machines=N] [--vcpus=N] [--memory-gib=N] [--disk-gb=N] [--expected-version=N] [--json]
```

Changes the default limits of every org, and prints them as `default-limits get` does. It calls `SetDefaultOrgLimits` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setdefaultorglimits)). A limit that you leave out keeps its value. The command needs at least one limit.

| Flag                                                 | Type                | Default       | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--machines`, `--vcpus`, `--memory-gib`, `--disk-gb` | as for `set-limits` | the value now | The new defaults.                                                                                                              |
| `--max-orgs-per-account`                             | int32               | the value now | The most orgs that one account owns besides its personal org.                                                                  |
| `--expected-version`                                 | int64               | none          | The version that the install config must have now. With another version, the command changes nothing and fails with `aborted`. |
| `--json`                                             | bool                | `false`       | Prints one JSON object.                                                                                                        |

### admin admin-key create

```sh
hopboxd admin admin-key create --name=NAME [--lifetime=DAYS | --expire-time=TIME] [--json]
```

Makes an admin API key, for the hopbox Terraform provider and scripts that call the admin API on the API listener ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#admin-api-keys)). It calls `CreateAdminKey` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#createadminkey)) with a new idempotency key. It prints the key alone on one line, so a script can keep it in a variable. The install keeps only a hash of the key, so this output is its only copy. Standard error gets the ID, the name, and the end of the key.

| Flag            | Type                    | Default        | Description                                                                                                                      |
| --------------- | ----------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`        | string                  | none, required | A name of 1 to 64 characters that tells the keys apart, such as `terraform`.                                                     |
| `--lifetime`    | `30d`, `90d`, or `365d` | `90d`          | The lifetime of the key.                                                                                                         |
| `--expire-time` | RFC 3339 time           | none           | A custom end of the key, such as `2027-01-31T00:00:00Z`, at most 365 days ahead. Give `--lifetime` or `--expire-time`, not both. |
| `--json`        | bool                    | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the keys `id`, `name`, `expire_time`, `last_use_time` (`null`), `create_time`, and `secret`.         |

```text
$ ADMIN_KEY="$(sudo hopboxd admin admin-key create --name terraform)"
The admin key 01a145b6-3fc1-7ba1-a54d-d1dceac38930 (terraform) works until 2027-01-14T17:15:34Z. This is its only copy.
$ curl -s -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" -d '{}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:7080/hopbox.admin.v1.InstallConfigService/GetInstallConfig
{"config":{"domain":"example.com","version":"2","updateTime":"2026-10-16T17:14:47.254670Z"}}
```

### admin admin-key register

```sh
hopboxd admin admin-key register --name=NAME --sha256=HASH [--lifetime=DAYS | --expire-time=TIME] [--json]
```

Makes an admin API key from the SHA-256 of a key that you made, so the key itself never reaches the server ([CLI tokens, API keys, admin API keys, and SSH keys](/reference/credentials/#admin-api-keys)). It calls `RegisterAdminKey` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#registeradminkey)) and prints the key as `admin-key list` does. A second registration of the same hash prints the first key, unchanged, and writes `An earlier call registered this hash already. The key stays as it was.` to standard error. It still exits with status 0.

| Flag            | Type                    | Default        | Description                                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | ----------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name`        | string                  | none, required | A name of 1 to 64 characters, such as `bootstrap`.                                                                                       |
| `--sha256`      | string                  | none, required | The SHA-256 of the whole key text, `hbxadm_` included, in 64 lowercase hex characters.                                                   |
| `--lifetime`    | `30d`, `90d`, or `365d` | `90d`          | The lifetime of the key.                                                                                                                 |
| `--expire-time` | RFC 3339 time           | none           | A custom end of the key, at most 365 days ahead.                                                                                         |
| `--json`        | bool                    | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the keys of `admin-key list --json`, plus `registered` (`false` for a hash that an earlier call registered). |

```sh
KEY="hbxadm_$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')"
sudo hopboxd admin admin-key register --name bootstrap --sha256 "$(printf '%s' "$KEY" | shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```

```text
01a145b6-400d-7c41-979e-14666fc2fe21  bootstrap  2027-01-14T17:15:34Z  never
```

### admin admin-key list

```sh
hopboxd admin admin-key list [--json]
```

Lists the admin API keys, oldest first. It calls `ListAdminKeys` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listadminkeys)). Each line has four fields, split by tabs: the ID, the name, the end of the key, and the time of its last use, or `never`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"keys":[...]}`. Each key has the keys `id`, `name`, `expire_time`, `last_use_time` (`null` for a key without a call), and `create_time`. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin admin-key list
01a145b6-3fc1-7ba1-a54d-d1dceac38930  terraform  2027-01-14T17:15:34Z  2026-10-16T17:15:34Z
```

### admin mail list

```sh
hopboxd admin mail list [--json]
```

Lists the mail files that the file mail transport wrote on this server, newest first ([Mail](/reference/mail/#the-file-transport)). With several control servers, each one writes the mail of the calls that it takes into its own folder, so run the command on each control server. It calls `ListMailFiles` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#listmailfiles)), which prunes the folder first. Each line has four fields, split by tabs: the name of the file, the time of the write in RFC 3339, the `To` header, and the `Subject` header. Without files, it prints `hopboxd: no mail files in <dir>` to standard error and nothing to standard output. The files stay after a switch back to the `smtp` transport, until a prune removes them.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints one JSON object, `{"dir":"/var/lib/hopbox/mail","files":[{"name":"...","create_time":"...","to":"<ann@example.org>","subject":"...","size_bytes":712}]}`. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin mail list
20261023T094602.118205000Z-0c8e1f2a9b3d4e5f.eml  2026-10-23T09:46:02Z  <bob@example.org>  Join Team on dev.example.org
20261023T094531.606059000Z-5cb912a8d0bb45d7.eml  2026-10-23T09:45:31Z  <ann@example.org>  Sign in to dev.example.org
```

### admin mail show

```sh
hopboxd admin mail show [NAME] [--raw | --json]
```

Prints one mail file of this server ([Mail](/reference/mail/#read-the-mail)). It calls `GetMailFile` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#getmailfile)). Without `NAME`, it calls `ListMailFiles` first and prints the newest file. The audit log records each read.

The output starts with the lines `name`, `create_time`, `to`, and `subject`, each with a tab and the value. An empty line and the text of the mail follow. The text is the body, decoded from quoted-printable, so a link is whole on one line.

| Argument or flag | Type   | Default         | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NAME`           | string | the newest file | The name of the file, as `admin mail list` prints it.                                                                                        |
| `--raw`          | bool   | `false`         | Prints the file as it is on disk: an RFC 5322 message with CRLF line ends, in quoted-printable. A mail client opens it.                      |
| `--json`         | bool   | `false`         | Prints one JSON object with the keys `name`, `create_time`, `to`, `subject`, `size_bytes`, `text`, and `content`. `content` is the raw file. |

Example:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin mail show
name  20261023T094531.606059000Z-5cb912a8d0bb45d7.eml
create_time  2026-10-23T09:45:31Z
to  <ann@example.org>
subject  Sign in to dev.example.org


Open this link to sign in to dev.example.org:


https://dev.example.org/auth/email#token=Zm9vYmFyYmF6cXV4cXV1eGNvcmdlZ3JhdWx0Z2FycGx5


The link works once, for 15 minutes. If you did not ask for it, you can ignore this email.
```

| Error                                                                              | Cause                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no mail files in <dir>`                                                           | `admin mail show` without `NAME`, and the folder holds no file.                                          |
| `invalid_argument: invalid argument: the name is not the name of a mail file, ...` | `NAME` is not the name of a mail file, for example a path.                                               |
| `not_found: not found: the mail file <name> is not in <dir>. ...`                  | No file has the name. A prune removes a file after 7 days. It also removes the oldest files beyond 1000. |

### admin maintenance on

```sh
hopboxd admin maintenance on [--json]
```

Turns maintenance mode of the install on ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)). It calls `SetMaintenance` with `maintenance` set to `true` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setmaintenance)). In maintenance mode, the API takes only the reads that write nothing, the control role ends every control channel and takes no new one, and the leader pauses its jobs. Every `hopboxd admin` command fails with `unavailable`, but `admin maintenance on` and `off`, because each other admin call writes an audit entry ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)). The machines keep running. Their URLs and the SSH front door answer no client until maintenance mode ends, because the edge servers lose their channels too. An open SSH session to a machine ends in the window, because its edge server cannot check its access again.

The command succeeds once the writes, the control channels, and the leader jobs that ran have ended while maintenance mode stayed on. This holds for every live control process of the install, not only for the one that takes the call. Each other live control process must report maintenance mode on and drained in a renewal of its row after the turn, and the call polls the rows every 250 ms. A control process that stops renewing its row counts as ended. The wait compares versions, not times. Each control process reports in its row the version of `install_config` at which it read maintenance mode (`maintenance_version`), and the call waits until every other live process reports maintenance mode on, drained, and a `maintenance_version` at least the version that the turn wrote. A control process of a release before migration `0045` records no row, so the command does not see it, and neither does the migration guard, the KEK promote, the decommission check, or the rolling upgrade order. Upgrade every control server before you rely on these checks. So after a success, no change of the API or of a server reaches the control store. `hopboxd admin db export` runs it first. On an install that is in maintenance mode already, it changes nothing, and waits the same way. Since every admin read is refused in maintenance mode, a second `admin maintenance on` is the harmless way to print the settings, `maintenance` among them, in that window.

It prints the settings of the install as [admin config get](#admin-config-get) does, with `maintenance` set to `true`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints the settings as one JSON object, as `admin config get --json` does. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin maintenance on
domain  example.com
...
maintenance  true
version  5
update_time  2026-10-25T10:00:00Z
```

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unavailable: unavailable: <n> calls, control channels, or leader jobs still run: context deadline exceeded`                                                                                                        | Some work did not end within the deadline of the call. Maintenance mode stays on. Run the command again.                                                                                          |
| `failed_precondition: failed precondition: the control process <id> on <host> (hopboxd <rel>) knows the migrations up to <n>, and only a hopboxd that knows migration 44 honors maintenance mode. Upgrade it first` | A live control process runs a `hopboxd` of schema version 43 or less. Maintenance mode stays off. Only releases from migration `0045` on write rows, so this guards the rows of a future release. |
| `unavailable: unavailable: maintenance mode is on, but the control process <id> on <host> (hopboxd <rel>) did not report that its calls, control channels, and leader jobs ended: ...`                              | Another control process did not report that it is drained before the deadline of the call. Maintenance mode stays on. Run the command again.                                                      |
| `unavailable: unavailable: maintenance mode turned off while it waited for the calls, control channels, and leader jobs to end`                                                                                     | Maintenance mode turned off during the wait, for example by `admin maintenance off` in another shell. The work runs again. Run the command again.                                                 |

### admin maintenance off

```sh
hopboxd admin maintenance off [--json]
```

Turns maintenance mode of the install off. It calls `SetMaintenance` with `maintenance` set to `false`. The admin socket takes this call also in maintenance mode, because no other write could turn it off. The API takes writes again, the servers dial their control channels again within 30 s, and their heartbeats bring new grants of the machine leases. The leader runs its jobs again, and gives the servers 20 s to dial before it marks a silent server `unresponsive`.

It prints the settings of the install, with `maintenance` set to `false`.

| Flag     | Type | Default | Description                                                                |
| -------- | ---- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--json` | bool | `false` | Prints the settings as one JSON object, as `admin config get --json` does. |

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin maintenance off
domain  example.com
...
maintenance  false
version  6
update_time  2026-10-25T10:05:00Z
```

### admin db export

```sh
sudo hopboxd admin db export --to=URL --ca-file=PATH --password-file=PATH [--json]
```

Copies the control store of this server from the bundled Postgres to an external Postgres, such as managed PostgreSQL. An install with one server uses it once, to move to the external Postgres that several control servers share. [Run the control store on an external Postgres](/guide/external-postgres/#move-a-one-server-install-to-the-external-postgres) has the whole move. The code is in `internal/dbexport`.

| Flag              | Type | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--to`            | URL  | none, required | The external Postgres, in the form of `postgres.url`: `postgres://<user>@<host>[:<port>]/<database>?sslmode=verify-full`, without a password ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#keys)). Its database must be empty. |
| `--ca-file`       | path | none, required | The PEM file of the CA of the certificate of the external Postgres, as `postgres.ca_file` takes it. A relative path becomes absolute.                                                                                                          |
| `--password-file` | path | none, required | The file that holds the password of the user of `--to`, as `postgres.password_file` takes it. As root, only root may read it. A relative path becomes absolute.                                                                                |
| `--json`          | bool | `false`        | Prints one JSON object with the keys `target`, `target_version`, `migration`, `tables`, `rows`, `duration` (in nanoseconds), and `config` (the config lines).                                                                                  |

Run it as the user of `hopboxd`, root on a server. It reads the bootstrap config of `--config` for the paths. The server must have the control role, and no `postgres.url`. The export takes these steps:

1. It connects to the bundled Postgres over its socket, and to the target with TLS and `sslmode=verify-full`, with the CA file and the password file. It checks the files as `hopboxd run` checks them.
2. It checks the target. The target must run the major version of the bundled Postgres or a newer one (plan question Q68), so Postgres 18 or later. Its user must be able to create tables in the schema `public`. Its database must hold no table, view, or sequence outside the catalogs, except those of an extension. A refusal of steps 1 and 2 changes nothing.
3. It turns maintenance mode on through the admin socket, and waits until the writes and the control channels of the install ended ([admin maintenance on](#admin-maintenance-on)).
4. It opens a read-only transaction on the bundled Postgres, and exports its snapshot. In that snapshot, it checks that the flag of maintenance mode is on, reads the last migration, and counts the rows of each table of the schema `public`. A store out of maintenance mode, for example after `admin maintenance off` during the export, is refused, because it can still change. Then `pg_dump` dumps the bundled Postgres in that snapshot, in the custom format, to `<data_dir>/export/hopbox-<time>.dump`. The export makes the dir `<data_dir>/export` with mode `0700`, and sets that mode also on a dir that exists. It makes the dump file first, empty, with mode `0600`, and `pg_dump` writes into it and keeps that mode, whatever the umask. The dump holds the sealed secrets of the install, so no other user may read it. So the counts describe the dump exactly.
5. `pg_restore` restores the dump into the target in one transaction, and stops at the first error. Every object gets the user of `--to` as its owner, and keeps no grant of the bundled Postgres. A failed restore leaves the target empty.
6. It checks the copy: the same last migration in `schema_migrations`, the same tables, and the same row count in each table.
7. It deletes the rows of `control_processes` on the copy, and clears `servers.channel_process` there. They name the processes of the source, which never run on the copy, and a row that still looks live would hold back the checks of the new control servers ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#control_processes)).
8. It removes the dump, prints the config lines, and tells the operator to stop `hopboxd` on this server.

Steps 4 and 5 run these two programs of `<postgres.install>/bin`:

```text
pg_dump --format=custom --snapshot=<snapshot> --file=<data_dir>/export/hopbox-<time>.dump --dbname=<the socket of the bundled Postgres>
pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges --single-transaction --exit-on-error --dbname=<--to, with sslrootcert=<--ca-file>> <dump>
```

They run with the env `LC_ALL=C`, `TZ=UTC`, `PGAPPNAME=hopboxd-export`, and `OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null`, and no other env of the caller. So the bundled OpenSSL reads no `openssl.cnf` of the host. The password reaches `pg_restore` in a password file in the form of `.pgpass`, `<data_dir>/export/pgpass-<random>`, with mode `0600`, which the env var `PGPASSFILE` names. It never shows in the arguments or the env of `pg_restore`, and the export removes the file after the restore.

On success, it prints the config lines for the new control server to standard output. Add them to the table `[postgres]` of its bootstrap config:

```text
$ sudo hopboxd admin db export --to 'postgres://avnadmin@db.example.org:20184/hopbox?sslmode=verify-full' \
    --ca-file /etc/hopbox/postgres-ca.pem --password-file /etc/hopbox/postgres-password
hopboxd: copied the control store to postgres://avnadmin@db.example.org:20184/hopbox (Postgres 18.1): migration 44, 61 tables, 2317 rows, in 4s.
hopboxd: the install stays in maintenance mode. Stop hopboxd on this server now, so that two control planes never run: sudo systemctl stop hopboxd. Then give the new control server these lines in its bootstrap config and the key files of /var/lib/hopbox/kek, start it, and run hopboxd admin maintenance off there.
[postgres]
url = "postgres://avnadmin@db.example.org:20184/hopbox?sslmode=verify-full"
ca_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-ca.pem"
password_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-password"
```

The lines that start with `hopboxd:` go to standard error. The export also writes log records to standard error, with `component=dbexport`:

| Message                                                  | Level | Fields                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------- |
| `maintenance mode is on, so the store no longer changes` | info  |                                     |
| `dumped the control store`                               | info  | `tables`, `migration`               |
| `restored the control store`                             | info  | `target`, the URL without its query |
| `the copy holds every row of the control store`          | info  | `tables`, `rows`, `duration`        |

The install stays in maintenance mode, and so does the copy, because the flag lives in the store. So neither control plane serves. In maintenance mode, no call writes to the store, also no read that would write its audit entry ([the API server](/reference/api/#maintenance-mode)). Only the internal writes of the control process go on, such as the renewals of the leader lease. So the copy misses no change of the API or of a server. Stop `hopboxd` on this server right after the export, so it never serves again. Its bundled cluster stays on disk. A new control server then starts on the copy with these lines, the key-encryption keys of `<data_dir>/kek` ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#key-files)), and `control` in `roles`. Then `hopboxd admin maintenance off` on that server lets the servers dial it, and their heartbeats bring new grants of the machine leases, with new epochs.

A failed step 3 can leave maintenance mode off or on: a turn to on can commit, and then fail in its wait for the calls that run. So after a failed step 3, the export reads the flag back from the bundled Postgres. After a failed step 3 with the flag on, or a failed step 4 or later, the install stays in maintenance mode, except after the refusal of a store out of maintenance mode in step 4. Fix the cause and run the export again, or run `hopboxd admin maintenance off` on this server to go back to the bundled Postgres. The export takes at most 1 hour.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                   | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `the config <path> names no control role, so this server holds no control store`                                                                                                        | The server has no control role.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `the control store of this server is the external Postgres of postgres.url in <path> already. db export copies only the bundled Postgres`                                               | The config has `postgres.url`.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `dbexport: refused: --to: "<url>" needs sslmode=verify-full, so hopboxd checks the certificate of the server and its host name. The export changed nothing`                             | `--to` breaks a rule of `postgres.url`. Each error of `postgres.url` can come here ([the bootstrap config of hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd-config/#errors)).                                        |
| `dbexport: refused: postgres.password_file: ...` or `dbexport: refused: postgres.ca_file: ...`                                                                                          | A file is missing, or fails a check of the files of the bootstrap config.                                                                                                                         |
| `dbexport: refused: connect to the target <url>: ... x509: certificate signed by unknown authority ...`                                                                                 | The CA of `--ca-file` did not sign the certificate of the target.                                                                                                                                 |
| `dbexport: refused: the target runs Postgres <version>, older than the Postgres <n> of this server. Give a Postgres <n> or newer`                                                       | The target runs an older major version.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `dbexport: refused: the user <user> cannot create tables in the schema public of the database <db>. Make the user the owner of the database`                                            | The user of `--to` lacks the right to create tables.                                                                                                                                              |
| `dbexport: refused: the database <db> of the target holds <n> tables, such as <schema>.<name>. Give an empty database, because the copy goes into one transaction and replaces nothing` | The database is not empty, for example after an earlier export. Drop and make the database again.                                                                                                 |
| `dbexport: refused: the bundled Postgres of this server holds no control store`                                                                                                         | The bundled Postgres has no schema.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `connect to the bundled Postgres of this server: ...`                                                                                                                                   | `hopboxd` does not run, or the export runs as another user than `hopboxd`.                                                                                                                        |
| `turn maintenance mode on: ...`                                                                                                                                                         | The call to the admin socket failed ([admin maintenance on](#admin-maintenance-on)).                                                                                                              |
| `dbexport: maintenance mode is off in the snapshot of the dump, so the store can still change. Turn maintenance mode on, and run the export again`                                      | Maintenance mode turned off after step 3. The export dumped nothing, and the install runs as before.                                                                                              |
| `pg_dump: ...` or `pg_restore: ... The restore ran in one transaction, so the target stays empty`                                                                                       | The program failed. The error ends with the last 4 KiB of its output.                                                                                                                             |
| `dbexport: check the copy: ... The copy stays in the target, so drop the database of <url> and make it again, empty, before the next export`                                            | The copy differs from the dump: another migration, other tables, or another row count. The copy stays in the target, so the next export refuses the database until you drop it and make it again. |

Each error that leaves the install in maintenance mode ends with `The install stays in maintenance mode, and this server keeps its bundled Postgres. Fix the cause and run the export again, or run hopboxd admin maintenance off to go back`: each error of step 4 or later but that refusal, and an error of step 3 after which the flag of the bundled Postgres is on. An error of step 3 with the flag off ends without it, and the install runs as before.

If the source must come back instead, run `hopboxd admin maintenance off` on it. Do not roll it back to a release older than schema version 44 while it is in maintenance mode: such a release does not know the flag and serves writes again.

`make test` runs `TestExport` and `TestExportRefusals` of `internal/dbexport` against a TLS Postgres of the bundled install, whose user is no superuser ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#tests)). `TestExport` then runs the migrations, a write, a change event, and the leader election on the copy. `TestExportRefusals` covers a target with a table, a wrong CA, a URL without `verify-full`, a user that cannot create tables, and a failed dump, which keeps maintenance mode on and the target empty. `TestCompareMajor` covers the refusal of an older major version. The fleet test runs the export with live nodes.

## stop-guest

```sh
hopboxd stop-guest --api-socket PATH [--timeout DURATION]
```

The unit of each machine runs `stop-guest` as its `ExecStop` ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#a-stop-through-systemd)). So a reboot of the server, or a `systemctl stop` of the unit, shuts the guest down cleanly. You do not run it yourself. The help of `hopboxd` does not list it.

| Flag           | Type     | Default        | Description                                       |
| -------------- | -------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `--api-socket` | path     | none, required | The API socket of the Firecracker of the machine. |
| `--timeout`    | duration | `30s`          | How long to wait for the end of Firecracker.      |

`stop-guest` reads the process ID of Firecracker from the env var `MAINPID`, which systemd sets for `ExecStop`. Without `MAINPID`, Firecracker ended already, and `stop-guest` exits with status 0 at once. Otherwise it sends `SendCtrlAltDel` through the API socket, and waits for the end of the process. If Firecracker ends within the timeout, it exits with status 0. If Firecracker does not end in time, it exits with status 1. If the call fails, and Firecracker does not end within 2 s, it exits with status 1 too. The unit ignores the status, and systemd then ends Firecracker with `SIGTERM`. It logs to the journal of the unit, at level info. Without `MAINPID`, it logs `Firecracker ended before the stop, so the guest needs no shutdown`. Otherwise it logs `asking the guest to shut down`, with `pid` and `timeout`, and after the end of Firecracker `the guest shut down`, with `duration`.

The flags of `stop-guest` stay the same in each release. A unit keeps the command line of the release that booted the machine, and runs the `hopboxd` of the current release.

## Logs

`hopboxd` writes its logs to standard error. Each record is one JSON object on one line, with the fields `time`, `level`, and `msg`, plus the fields of the record. Under systemd, standard error goes to journald.

This record shows the format only. `hopboxd` does not write this message:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-16T09:00:00.000000000Z","level":"INFO","msg":"example","machine":"box1"}
```

A field of type duration is a number of nanoseconds.

`run` writes these records. The records of the daemon have `component=daemon`.

The parts of the control role write their own records:

* Postgres ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#logs)) and the migrations ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#schema-migrations))
* the leader election ([Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#leader-election))
* the API ([the API server](/reference/api/#logs)) and the admin socket ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#logs-of-the-socket))
* the control channels ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/))

It writes the records of the mesh device with `component=mesh` ([the mesh](/reference/mesh/#logs)). The DNS role writes its records with `component=dns` ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/#logs)). The edge role writes its records with `component=edge` ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)).

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0      | The command succeeded. For `run`, the roles stopped after `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`, and every unit stopped well.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 1      | The command failed. For `run`, the bootstrap config is not valid, or a unit failed to start, to run, or to stop. For `enroll`, the preflight check or the enrollment failed. For `preflight`, a check of severity `fail` failed. For `install` and `upgrade`, a check refused, a step failed, or `hopboxd` did not start. For `stop-guest`, the guest did not shut down in time. `hopboxd` prints `hopboxd: error: <message>` to standard error. |
| 80     | The command line is not valid, for example an unknown command or flag, or a bad flag value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

# The bootstrap config of hopboxd

> Every key and default of the bootstrap config /etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml, and its errors.

The bootstrap config holds the few settings that `hopboxd` needs before it can reach the control store: its roles, its dirs, its listeners, and the address of the control role. `hopboxd run` reads it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)). The settings of the whole install, such as its domain, live in the control store and change through the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/)). The code is in `internal/config`.

## File

| Item     | Value                                                                  |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Path     | `/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml`. `hopboxd run --config` gives another path. |
| Format   | [TOML](https://toml.io)                                                |
| Encoding | UTF-8                                                                  |

`hopboxd install` writes the file ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#install)). It sets `roles` from `--roles`, and `channel.control_urls` (or the old key `channel.control_url`) and `channel.labels` from `--control-url` and `--label`. With one `--control-url`, it writes the old key `channel.control_url`, unless the file has `channel.control_urls` already. So a rollback to a `hopboxd` from before `control_urls`, which refuses that key, still reads the file. With more than one `--control-url`, it writes `channel.control_urls` and deletes `channel.control_url`. It keeps every other key of a file that exists, and writes a file with the mode `0644`. Before it reads a file that exists, it makes the owner and mode checks below. So root never takes values from a file that another user can change.

`hopboxd run` reads the file once, at start. A change takes effect at the next start. An install that changes the file restarts `hopboxd`. `hopboxd admin` reads it to find the admin socket ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin)). `hopboxd enroll` and `hopboxd preflight` read it for the roles, the data dir, and the control URLs ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#enroll)).

The file names the Postgres binaries that `hopboxd` runs and the external Postgres that it trusts, so a `hopboxd` that runs as root refuses a file that another user can change:

* The file must be a regular file of at most 64 KiB.
* As root, the path must not be a symlink. `hopboxd` opens it with `O_NOFOLLOW`.
* As root, the file must belong to root.
* As root, group and others must not be able to write the file. Mode `0644` or `0600` is fine.
* As root, the dir of the file, such as `/etc/hopbox`, must be a real dir, not a symlink. It must belong to root, and group and others must not be able to write it. Otherwise another user can swap the file. `hopboxd` checks only this dir, not the dirs above it, such as `/etc`. The install owns `/etc/hopbox`, and the OS owns the dirs above it.

## Keys

| Key                       | Type                    | Default                                       | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `roles`                   | array of strings        | none, required                                | The roles of this server: `control`, `node`, `dns`, `edge`, or more than one. Each role appears at most once. The control role runs the control store, the API, the internal listener, and the admin socket. The node role runs machines. The DNS role answers DNS queries for the zones of the install ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/)). The edge role serves HTTPS for the domain of the install and for every machine URL ([the edge role](/reference/edge/)). It also runs the SSH front door of the machines ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)). A server with a role other than `control` enrolls with the control role. It keeps a control channel to it ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `data_dir`                | absolute path           | `/var/lib/hopbox`                             | The state of the server. The bundled Postgres keeps its cluster in `<data_dir>/pg` ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#paths-on-a-server)), the file keyring keeps its key-encryption keys in `<data_dir>/kek` ([Sealing](/reference/sealing/#key-files)), and an enrolled server keeps its identity in `<data_dir>/server` ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). The control role keeps the mail of the file mail transport in `<data_dir>/mail` ([Mail](/reference/mail/#the-mail-folder)). The reflink check of the preflight check runs in this dir ([the preflight check](/reference/preflight/)). The node role keeps its images, kernels, disks, and jails here ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#files-of-a-machine)). On a server with the node role, the path has at most 25 characters, because each jail holds unix sockets. `hopboxd` and `hopboxd install` refuse a longer path with `data_dir: "<path>" has <n> characters. With the node role, it has at most 25, because each jail in it holds unix sockets`. |
| `run_dir`                 | absolute path           | `/run/hopbox`                                 | The sockets of the server. The bundled Postgres has its socket in `<run_dir>/pg`, and the admin socket is `<run_dir>/admin.sock` ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#the-admin-socket)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `control.api_listen`      | `host:port`             | `127.0.0.1:7080`                              | The TCP address of the API listener of the control role ([the API server](/reference/api/#listener)). The host must be a loopback IP address, such as `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. Port `0` picks a free port.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `control.internal_listen` | `host:port`             | `127.0.0.1:7443`                              | The TCP address of the internal listener of the control role, which serves the cluster API over TLS to the servers of the install ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)). The host must be an IP address, of any kind, such as `127.0.0.1` or `10.0.0.5`. `0.0.0.0` listens on every address. Port `0` picks a free port. It must differ from `control.api_listen`, except when both use port `0`. With several control servers, use the vRack IP of the server, because the other control processes reach this listener at the address that it names. A listener on every address gets no forwarded data streams ([the internal listener](/reference/internal-listener/)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `control.release_image`   | absolute path           | `/opt/hopbox/current/image/artifact.json`     | The `artifact.json` of the default image of the release. At each start, the control role registers this image, unless the install has it already or has an image of the same name from a newer release ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#the-default-image-of-the-release)). A missing file gives a log record at level info, and a file that is not valid gives one at level error. In both cases, the start goes on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `channel.control_urls`    | array of URLs           | `["https://127.0.0.1:7443"]`                  | The URLs of the internal listeners of the control servers. List 1 to 8 URLs, each one once. A server with a role other than `control` enrolls at the first URL that answers ([Enrollment and the install PKI](/reference/enrollment/)). It keeps one control channel, to one URL at a time. The first channel goes to the URL that a CRC-32 of the server ID picks, so the channels of a fleet spread over the control servers. After a lost or refused channel, the next dial goes to the next URL of the list ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#the-agent)). The edge role also sends the requests of the API and the console to these URLs, in turn ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#forwarded-requests)). Each URL must be an `https` URL of a host, with an optional port, and without user info, a path other than `/`, a query, or a fragment. Without a port, the port is 443. On a server that also has the control role, a URL names the internal listener of the same `hopboxd`.                                                                        |
| `channel.control_url`     | URL                     | none                                          | The old key of `channel.control_urls` with one URL. `hopboxd` moves its value into `channel.control_urls` when it reads the file. A file with both keys fails ([Errors](#errors)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `channel.labels`          | table of strings        | empty                                         | The labels of the server, for example `zone = "gra"`. Each heartbeat reports them, and the registry keeps them ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/)), until an instance admin sets the labels through the admin API. From then on, the registry keeps the labels of the admin ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#setserverlabels)). At most 64 labels. A key has 1 to 63 characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, and `-`, and starts with a lowercase letter. A value is valid UTF-8 of at most 255 bytes, without control characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `dns.listen`              | array of `host:port`    | `[":53"]`                                     | The addresses of the DNS role ([the DNS role](/reference/dns/)). It listens on UDP and on TCP at each address. List 1 to 16 addresses, each one once. The host is empty, which listens on every address, or an IP address, such as `203.0.113.10`. A host name is refused. The port is a number. Port `0` picks a free port, and UDP and TCP share that port. The DNS role opens its sockets at the start of `hopboxd run`, so a port that another program holds fails the start ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `edge.https_listen`       | `host:port`             | `:443`                                        | The address of the HTTPS listener of the edge role ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#tls)). The host is empty, which listens on every address, or an IP address, such as `203.0.113.10`. A host name is refused. Port `0` picks a free port. The edge role opens the listener at the start of `hopboxd run`, so a port that another program holds fails the start ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#run)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `edge.http_listen`        | `host:port`             | `:80`                                         | The address of the plain HTTP listener of the edge role. It answers each request for a host of the install with a redirect to HTTPS ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#routing)). The rules of `edge.https_listen` apply. The two addresses must differ. Only port `0` can appear in both.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `edge.ssh_listen`         | `host:port`             | `:2222`                                       | The address of the listener of the SSH front door ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#listener)). The rules of `edge.https_listen` apply. Its port must be outside the SSH ports 10000 to 30000, and it must differ from the two HTTP listeners. Only port `0` can appear twice. With `edge.ssh_redirect`, the host must be empty or `::`. The redirect sends each connection to the address of the network interface that took it. So a listener on one address, such as a floating IP, gets no client, and `0.0.0.0` gets no IPv6 client.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `edge.ssh_redirect`       | bool                    | `true`                                        | Makes `hopboxd` replace the nftables table `inet hopbox_edge` at the start of the edge role. The table sends every TCP connection to a port from 10000 to 30000 of the server to `edge.ssh_listen` ([the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/#redirect-of-the-ssh-ports)). A stop deletes it. On a system without nftables, such as macOS, the edge role logs a warning and serves only `edge.ssh_listen`, which reaches no machine. If the operator makes the redirect, set it to `false`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `acme.name_servers`       | array of `host:port`    | empty                                         | The addresses at which the ACME job of the control role checks that each name server serves a change of the zone ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/#the-name-server-check)). Empty means port 53 at the addresses of `ns1` and `ns2` of the zone. At most 16. Each host is an IP address. A host name is refused. When the DNS role listens on another port, set it, such as `["127.0.0.1:15353"]` on a laptop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `acme.ca_file`            | absolute path           | empty                                         | A PEM file of more root certificates for the HTTPS of the ACME directory. The ACME job trusts them, for example the root of the test CA Pebble ([the certificate of the install](/reference/acme/#test-with-pebble)). Empty means the roots of the system only. A file that does not load, or holds no certificate, fails the start of `hopboxd run`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `postgres.install`        | absolute path           | `/opt/hopbox/current/postgres`                | The bundled Postgres: a dir with `bin/`, `lib/`, and `share/` ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#the-install)). `hopboxd admin db export` runs `pg_dump` and `pg_restore` from it ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#admin-db-export)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `postgres.user`           | string                  | `hopbox-pg`                                   | The OS user that runs Postgres when `hopboxd` runs as root ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#os-users-and-database-roles)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `postgres.url`            | URL                     | empty                                         | An external Postgres for the control store, such as managed PostgreSQL ([the bundled Postgres](/reference/postgres/#external-postgres)). With it, the control role starts no bundled Postgres and connects over TLS. The form is `postgres://<user>@<host>[:<port>]/<database>?sslmode=verify-full`. The scheme can also be `postgresql`. It must name one host, a user, and a database, and have `sslmode=verify-full`. It must not hold a password, or the parameters `password`, `passfile`, `sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslpassword`, `sslcertmode`, `service`, `servicefile`, `host`, `hostaddr`, `port`, `dbname`, or `user`. Other parameters of libpq and pgx, such as `connect_timeout`, pass on.
