It needs `postgres.ca_file` and `postgres.password_file`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `postgres.ca_file`        | absolute path           | empty                                         | The PEM file of the CA that signed the certificate of the external Postgres. `hopboxd` checks the certificate against it, and the host name of `postgres.url` against the certificate. For managed PostgreSQL, it is the CA certificate that OVHcloud gives for the service. It needs `postgres.url`. As root, `hopboxd` makes the owner and mode checks of the bootstrap config on it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `postgres.password_file`  | absolute path           | empty                                         | A file that holds the password of the user of `postgres.url`, on one line. A newline at the end is fine. It needs `postgres.url`. As root, the file must belong to root, must not be a symlink, and group and others must not read or write it: mode `0400` or `0600`. Its dir has the checks of the dir of the bootstrap config. At most 4 KiB.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `metrics.listen`          | `host:port`             | `127.0.0.1:9464`                              | The TCP address of the Prometheus metrics ([Metrics](/reference/metrics/)). The host must be a loopback IP address. Every role uses it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `vmm.firecracker`         | absolute path           | `/opt/hopbox/current/firecracker/firecracker` | The Firecracker binary of the node role ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/)). Its file name must be `firecracker`, because the jailer names the jail of each machine after it. Each boot uses the file at this path, so an upgrade moves new boots to the Firecracker of the new release. A running microVM keeps its own copy. The compatibility class takes its snapshot format version ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#compatibility-class)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `vmm.jailer`              | absolute path           | `/opt/hopbox/current/firecracker/jailer`      | The jailer binary of the node role. The unit of each machine runs it ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#the-unit-of-a-machine)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `vmm.kernel`              | absolute path           | `/opt/hopbox/current/kernel/vmlinux`          | The guest kernel of the release. At each start, `hopboxd run` adds it to the kernel cache ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/#the-kernel-cache)). A missing file gives a warning, and the start goes on.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `network.nameservers`     | array of IPv4 addresses | empty                                         | The resolvers of the machines of the node role, at most 3, each once ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#the-resolvers-of-the-machines)). The guest agent writes them to `/etc/resolv.conf` of each machine, and the machines reach them on port 53. Empty takes the IPv4 resolvers of the host, from `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` or `/etc/resolv.conf`. A loopback, unspecified, link-local, or multicast address, or an address of the install range `10.240.0.0/12`, is refused. A resolver on the node itself does not work, because a machine reaches no service of its node.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The API listener has no TLS. So `hopboxd` refuses a `control.api_listen` that is not a loopback address, and the API never leaves the server in clear text. A host name, even `localhost`, is refused, because a name can resolve to an address that is not loopback. The internal listener has TLS, and every call on it except `Enroll` needs a server certificate, so `control.internal_listen` can be any IP address. On an install with one server, it stays on `127.0.0.1`. `hopboxd` refuses a host name there too.

`hopboxd` checks the keys of `[postgres]` on every server, but only the control role uses them. `hopboxd run` reads `postgres.ca_file` and `postgres.password_file` at its start, so a change of either file takes effect at the next start. `hopboxd` checks the keys of `[control]` only on a server with the control role. It checks the keys of `[channel]` only on a server that enrolls: one with a role other than `control`. It checks the keys of `[dns]` only on a server with the DNS role. It checks the keys of `[edge]` only on a server with the edge role. It checks the keys of `[acme]` only on a server with the control role. It checks the keys of `[vmm]` and `[network]` only on a server with the node role.

### The old name `[node]`

Before the DNS role, `[channel]` had the name `[node]`. This release still reads `[node]` as `[channel]`, and the next release refuses it. With `[node]`, `hopboxd run` logs this record at level warn, with the path of the file in `config`:

```json
{"level":"WARN","msg":"the bootstrap config uses an old name","config":"/etc/hopbox/hopboxd.toml","warning":"the section [node] of the bootstrap config is now [channel]. Rename it. hopboxd install renames it, and the next release of hopboxd refuses [node]"}
```

`hopboxd enroll` prints the same warning on stderr, after `hopboxd: warning: `. When `hopboxd install` writes the file, it renames `[node]` to `[channel]`. An error about a key of `[node]` names the key under `channel`, such as `channel.labels`. A file with both sections is refused.

The paths of the sockets have a limit: a unix socket path has at most 103 bytes on macOS. So keep `run_dir` short. The admin socket needs 11 bytes more for its temp name ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#the-admin-socket)).

## Examples

The smallest file. Every other key has its default:

```toml
roles = ["control"]
```

A server with the control role and the node role. The node role reaches the control role of the same `hopboxd` at the default `channel.control_urls`:

```toml
roles = ["control", "node"]
```

A control server on an external Postgres, such as managed PostgreSQL. The control role starts no bundled Postgres ([Run the control store on an external Postgres](/guide/external-postgres/)):

```toml
roles = ["control", "node"]


[postgres]
url = "postgres://hopbox@db.example.org:5432/hopbox?sslmode=verify-full"
ca_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-ca.pem"
password_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-password"
```

The same server, with the resolvers of its machines:

```toml
roles = ["control", "node"]


[network]
nameservers = ["213.186.33.99", "9.9.9.9"]
```

A DNS server of the install. It enrolls with the control role at `channel.control_urls`, and answers DNS on port 53 of one address:

```toml
roles = ["dns"]


[channel]
control_urls = ["https://10.0.0.5:7443"]
labels = { zone = "gra" }


[dns]
listen = ["203.0.113.10:53"]
```

An edge server of the install. It enrolls with the control role at `channel.control_urls`, and sends the API and the console there:

```toml
roles = ["edge"]


[channel]
control_urls = ["https://10.0.0.5:7443", "https://10.0.0.6:7443"]


[edge]
https_listen = "203.0.113.10:443"
http_listen = "203.0.113.10:80"
ssh_listen = ":2222"
```

A file with every key:

```toml
roles = ["control", "node", "dns", "edge"]
data_dir = "/var/lib/hopbox"
run_dir = "/run/hopbox"


[control]
api_listen = "127.0.0.1:7080"
internal_listen = "127.0.0.1:7443"


[channel]
control_urls = ["https://127.0.0.1:7443"]
labels = { zone = "gra" }


[dns]
listen = [":53"]


[edge]
https_listen = ":443"
http_listen = ":80"
ssh_listen = ":2222"
ssh_redirect = true


[acme]
name_servers = ["203.0.113.10:53"]
ca_file = "/etc/hopbox/acme-roots.pem"


[postgres]
install = "/opt/hopbox/current/postgres"
user = "hopbox-pg"
url = "postgres://hopbox@db.example.org:5432/hopbox?sslmode=verify-full"
ca_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-ca.pem"
password_file = "/etc/hopbox/postgres-password"


[metrics]
listen = "127.0.0.1:9464"
```

## Errors

`hopboxd run` refuses a file that breaks a rule, and exits with status 1. The error names the file, and then each broken rule on its own line.

| Error                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Cause                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config: open <path>: no such file or directory`                                                                                                                                                                              | The file does not exist.                                                                                                                |
| `config: <path> belongs to uid <n>, and hopboxd runs as root, so the file must belong to root`                                                                                                                                | As root, the file belongs to another user.                                                                                              |
| `config: <path> has mode <mode>, which lets group or others change it, and hopboxd runs as root`                                                                                                                              | As root, group or others can write the file.                                                                                            |
| `config: <path> is not a regular file`                                                                                                                                                                                        | The path is a dir or a device.                                                                                                          |
| `config: <path> is a symlink, and hopboxd runs as root, so it reads only a real file`                                                                                                                                         | As root, the path is a symlink.                                                                                                         |
| `config: the dir <dir> belongs to uid <n>, and hopboxd runs as root, so the dir must belong to root`                                                                                                                          | As root, the dir of the file belongs to another user.                                                                                   |
| `config: the dir <dir> has mode <mode>, which lets group or others change it, and hopboxd runs as root`                                                                                                                       | As root, group or others can write the dir of the file.                                                                                 |
| `config: the dir <dir> is a symlink, and hopboxd runs as root`                                                                                                                                                                | As root, the dir of the file is a symlink.                                                                                              |
| `config: <path> is larger than 65536 bytes`                                                                                                                                                                                   | The file is too large.                                                                                                                  |
| `config: <path>: toml: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                   | The file is not valid TOML, or a value has the wrong type, for example `roles = "control"`.                                             |
| `config: <path>: unknown keys: <keys>`                                                                                                                                                                                        | The file has a key that is not in the table above, for example a typo such as `control.listen`. A typo never falls back to a default.   |
| `roles: list at least one role. This hopboxd runs the roles: control, node, dns, edge`                                                                                                                                        | `roles` is missing or empty.                                                                                                            |
| `roles: unknown role "<role>". This hopboxd runs the roles: control, node, dns, edge`                                                                                                                                         | A role that this `hopboxd` does not have, such as `proxy`.                                                                              |
| `roles: the role "<role>" appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                                      | A role is in the list twice.                                                                                                            |
| `<key>: "<value>" is not an absolute path`                                                                                                                                                                                    | `data_dir`, `run_dir`, `postgres.install`, `postgres.ca_file`, or `postgres.password_file` is a relative path.                          |
| `postgres.url: the value is not a URL`                                                                                                                                                                                        | `postgres.url` does not parse.                                                                                                          |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" holds a password. Put the password in its own file, and name that file`                                                                                                                                | The URL has a password. Errors show the URL without its password and its query.                                                         |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" is not a postgres:// URL, such as postgres://hopbox@db.example.org:5432/hopbox?sslmode=verify-full`                                                                                                    | The scheme is not `postgres` or `postgresql`.                                                                                           |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" names no host, such as ...`                                                                                                                                                                            | The URL has no host.                                                                                                                    |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" names more than one host. Name the one host of the service, whose failover keeps its name`                                                                                                             | The host part lists hosts with a comma.                                                                                                 |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" names no user, such as ...`                                                                                                                                                                            | The URL has no user.                                                                                                                    |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" names no database, such as ...`                                                                                                                                                                        | The path is empty, or has more than one segment.                                                                                        |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" has a fragment`                                                                                                                                                                                        | The URL ends with `#...`.                                                                                                               |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" has the parameter <name>. The CA comes from postgres.ca_file, the password from postgres.password_file, and the host, the user, and the database from the URL itself`                                  | The query has a parameter of the refused list of `postgres.url`.                                                                        |
| `postgres.url: "<url>" needs sslmode=verify-full, so hopboxd checks the certificate of the server and its host name`                                                                                                          | `sslmode` is missing, appears twice, or has another value.                                                                              |
| `postgres.ca_file: postgres.url needs it`                                                                                                                                                                                     | `postgres.url` is set, and `postgres.ca_file` is not. The same error exists for `postgres.password_file`.                               |
| `postgres.ca_file and postgres.password_file need postgres.url`                                                                                                                                                               | A file is set without `postgres.url`.                                                                                                   |
| `postgres.ca_file: <path> holds no PEM certificate`                                                                                                                                                                           | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file holds no certificate.                                                                           |
| `postgres.ca_file: config: ...` or `postgres.password_file: config: ...`                                                                                                                                                      | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file is missing, or fails a check of the file of the bootstrap config, such as `belongs to uid <n>`. |
| `postgres.password_file: config: <path> has mode <mode>, which lets group or others read it, and it holds a secret. Give it mode 0400`                                                                                        | As root, group or others can read the password file.                                                                                    |
| `postgres.password_file: <path> must hold the password on one line`                                                                                                                                                           | The file is empty, or holds more than one line.                                                                                         |
| `control.api_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                         | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                             |
| `control.api_listen: "<value>" is not a loopback IP address. ...`                                                                                                                                                             | The host is not a loopback IP address.                                                                                                  |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                    | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                             |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" has no port`                                                                                                                                                                              | The address ends with `:`.                                                                                                              |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                                  | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                |
| `control.internal_listen: "<value>" is also control.api_listen. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                           | Both listeners have the same address, with a port other than `0`.                                                                       |
| `acme.name_servers: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                                        | A name server is a host name.                                                                                                           |
| `acme.name_servers: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                          | A name server has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                           |
| `acme.name_servers: <n> addresses, more than 16`                                                                                                                                                                              | The list is too long.                                                                                                                   |
| `acme.ca_file: "<value>" is not an absolute path`                                                                                                                                                                             | The path is relative.                                                                                                                   |
| `control.release_image: "<value>" is not an absolute path`                                                                                                                                                                    | The path is relative.                                                                                                                   |
| `acme.ca_file: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                                           | At the start of `hopboxd run`, the file does not open, or holds no PEM certificate.                                                     |
| `[node] is the old name of [channel]. Keep only [channel]`                                                                                                                                                                    | The file has both `[node]` and `[channel]`.                                                                                             |
| `network.nameservers: "<value>" is not an IPv4 address that a machine can reach, such as 9.9.9.9`                                                                                                                             | A resolver is not IPv4, or is a loopback, unspecified, link-local, multicast, or machine address.                                       |
| `network.nameservers: <address> appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                                | A resolver is in the list twice.                                                                                                        |
| `network.nameservers: <n> resolvers, more than 3`                                                                                                                                                                             | The list is too long.                                                                                                                   |
| `channel.control_url is the old key of channel.control_urls. Keep only channel.control_urls`                                                                                                                                  | The file has both keys.                                                                                                                 |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" is not a URL: ...`                                                                                                                                                                           | A value does not parse as a URL.                                                                                                        |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" is not an https URL of a host, such as https://127.0.0.1:7443`                                                                                                                               | The scheme is not `https`, the host is missing, or the URL has user info, a path, a query, or a fragment.                               |
| `channel.control_urls: <n> URLs, more than 8`                                                                                                                                                                                 | The list is too long.                                                                                                                   |
| `channel.control_urls: "<value>" appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                               | A URL is in the list twice.                                                                                                             |
| `channel.labels: invalid label: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                          | A label breaks a rule of `channel.labels`. The rest of the message names the label and the rule.                                        |
| `dns.listen: list 1 to 16 addresses, such as ":53"`                                                                                                                                                                           | `dns.listen` is empty, or has more than 16 addresses.                                                                                   |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                                 | The address has no `:`, or does not parse.                                                                                              |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" has no port number`                                                                                                                                                                                    | The port is empty, is not a number, or is larger than 65535.                                                                            |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 203.0.113.10:53, or a port alone, such as :53`                                                                                                                | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                |
| `dns.listen: "<value>" appears twice`                                                                                                                                                                                         | An address is in the list twice.                                                                                                        |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                          | The address has no `:`, or does not parse. The same errors exist for `edge.http_listen`.                                                |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" has no port number`                                                                                                                                                                             | The port is empty, is not a number, or is larger than 65535.                                                                            |
| `edge.https_listen: "<value>" is not an IP address and a port, such as 203.0.113.10:443, or a port alone, such as :443`                                                                                                       | The host is a name, such as `localhost`.                                                                                                |
| `edge.http_listen: "<value>" is also edge.https_listen. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                                   | Both listeners of the edge role have the same address, with a port other than `0`.                                                      |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" is in the SSH ports 10000 to 30000, which the redirect sends to it. Pick a port outside them, such as :2222`                                                                                      | The port of the SSH listener is an SSH port of a machine. The errors of `edge.https_listen` also exist for `edge.ssh_listen`.           |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" listens on one address, but the redirect of the SSH ports sends each connection to the address of the interface that took it. Give a port alone, such as :2222, or set edge.ssh_redirect = false` | `edge.ssh_redirect` is true, and the host of `edge.ssh_listen` is one address.                                                          |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "0.0.0.0:<port>" takes only IPv4, so the IPv6 clients that the redirect of the SSH ports sends to it get no answer. Give a port alone, such as :2222, or set edge.ssh_redirect = false`                     | `edge.ssh_redirect` is true, and the host of `edge.ssh_listen` is `0.0.0.0`.                                                            |
| `edge.ssh_listen: "<value>" is also an HTTP listener. Give each listener its own address`                                                                                                                                     | The SSH listener has the address of `edge.https_listen` or `edge.http_listen`, with a port other than `0`.                              |
| `metrics.listen: "<value>" is not a loopback IP address. ...`                                                                                                                                                                 | The host of the metrics listener is not a loopback IP address.                                                                          |
| `metrics.listen: "<value>" is not host:port: ...`                                                                                                                                                                             | The address has no port, or does not parse.                                                                                             |

# Host kernel

> The build, the kernel configuration, and the install of the tested host kernel, with the scripts in build/hostkernel/.

This page covers the host kernel of hopbox servers: its build from kernel.org sources, its config, and its install. The host kernel is the Linux kernel of the server that runs Firecracker. The tested kernel is `6.18.57-hopbox1` on Debian 13. Firecracker supports the host kernel 6.18 but not 6.12, the kernel of Debian 13, so hopbox builds 6.18 from kernel.org sources.

## Files

| File                                      | What it holds                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `build/hostkernel/build.sh`               | The build script. It downloads the source, checks it, and builds Debian packages.                                                               |
| `build/hostkernel/install.sh`             | The install script. It installs the kernel package and makes it the GRUB default.                                                               |
| `build/hostkernel/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` | The final kernel config. It is the same file as `/boot/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` on the [tested server](/reference/preflight/#the-tested-server). |

## Pinned values

Each script pins its versions and checksums in variables at its top. To move to a new kernel release, change these values, `config-<release>`, and this page in one change.

| Variable            | Script       | Value                                                              | Meaning                                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `KERNEL_VERSION`    | `build.sh`   | `6.18.57`                                                          | The kernel.org release. It was the longterm 6.18 release on 2026-10-15.        |
| `KERNEL_SHA256`     | `build.sh`   | `5bd9acdc82ec5efc3790ae840e5aaa40dfde7efff261cf6dde902dc570acf98c` | The sha256 of `linux-6.18.57.tar.xz`.                                          |
| `LOCAL_VERSION`     | `build.sh`   | `-hopbox1`                                                         | The suffix of the kernel release. `uname -r` prints `6.18.57-hopbox1`.         |
| `GREGKH_FPR`        | `build.sh`   | `647F28654894E3BD457199BE38DBBDC86092693E`                         | The key of Greg Kroah-Hartman. It signs the tarball.                           |
| `AUTOSIGNER_FPR`    | `build.sh`   | `B8868C80BA62A1FFFAF5FDA9632D3A06589DA6B1`                         | The key of the kernel.org checksum autosigner. It signs `sha256sums.asc`.      |
| `DEBIAN_PACKAGE`    | `build.sh`   | `linux-image-6.18.15+deb13-amd64`                                  | The Debian package that holds the base config. It comes from trixie-backports. |
| `DEBIAN_DEB_SHA256` | `build.sh`   | `d38a7af6260782a47cd615ad717347a528b45f076245b4deabb3f1ecf8459186` | The sha256 of the Debian package file.                                         |
| `KERNEL_RELEASE`    | `install.sh` | `6.18.57-hopbox1`                                                  | The kernel release that the script installs.                                   |
| `PACKAGE_VERSION`   | `install.sh` | `6.18.57-1`                                                        | The version of the Debian package that `build.sh` writes.                      |

## Environment variables of build.sh

| Variable             | Default                 | Meaning                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WORK_DIR`           | `$PWD/hostkernel-build` | The folder for the downloads, the source tree, and the packages. It needs about 40 GB of free space. |
| `JOBS`               | the output of `nproc`   | The number of parallel `make` jobs.                                                                  |
| `ALLOW_CONFIG_DRIFT` | `0`                     | With `1`, the build goes on after `make olddefconfig` changes the config.                            |

## Requirements

* An amd64 host with Debian 13.
* A normal user for `build.sh`. The build needs no root.
* The build packages in the `BUILD_DEPS` list of `build.sh`. If one is missing, `build.sh` prints the `apt-get install` command and stops.
* Root for `install.sh`.
* UEFI Secure Boot off. The kernel has no Secure Boot signature.

These are the build packages:

```sh
sudo apt-get install bc bison build-essential cpio debhelper dwarves flex gawk gnupg \
  kmod libdw-dev libelf-dev libncurses-dev libssl-dev python3 rsync xz-utils zstd
```

## Build

```sh
build/hostkernel/build.sh
```

The script takes these steps:

1. It downloads `linux-6.18.57.tar.xz`, `linux-6.18.57.tar.sign`, and `sha256sums.asc` from `cdn.kernel.org`.
2. It checks the tarball against `KERNEL_SHA256`, and it checks that `sha256sums.asc` lists the same sha256.
3. It gets the kernel.org keys over WKD into a temporary GnuPG home. The autosigner key must sign `sha256sums.asc`, and the key of Greg Kroah-Hartman must sign the tarball.
4. It unpacks the source into `$WORK_DIR/linux-6.18.57`.
5. It copies `config-6.18.57-hopbox1` to `.config` and runs `make olddefconfig`. If the config changes, the script prints the change with `scripts/diffconfig` and stops.
6. It runs `make bindeb-pkg` and writes `SHA256SUMS.debs`.

The build writes these files into `$WORK_DIR`:

| File                                                  | What it holds                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`     | The kernel and its modules. `install.sh` installs only this package.          |
| `linux-image-6.18.57-hopbox1-dbg_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb` | The debug symbols, about 1 GB. The config keeps `DEBUG_INFO`, as Debian does. |
| `linux-headers-6.18.57-hopbox1_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`   | The headers for modules outside the kernel tree. hopbox does not use them.    |
| `linux-libc-dev_6.18.57-1_amd64.deb`                  | The kernel headers for user programs. hopbox does not use them.               |
| `SHA256SUMS.debs`                                     | The sha256 of each package.                                                   |

On the tested server, the build took 48 minutes with 12 jobs, Debian gcc 14.2.0-19, and pahole 1.30.

## Config

The config starts from the Debian 6.18.15 config. `build.sh config` makes `config-6.18.57-hopbox1` again from that base:

1. It downloads the Debian package with `apt-get download` and checks it against `DEBIAN_DEB_SHA256`. If the archive no longer has the package, put the file in `$WORK_DIR/dl/` by hand. The script then uses that file.
2. It copies `/boot/config-6.18.15+deb13-amd64` from the package to `.config` and runs `make olddefconfig`.
3. It applies the changes below with `scripts/config` and runs `make olddefconfig` again.
4. It writes the result to `build/hostkernel/config-6.18.57-hopbox1` and prints the difference to the Debian config.

These changes are on purpose:

| Option                                                            | Debian 6.18.15  | 6.18.57-hopbox1 | Reason                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LOCALVERSION`                                                    | `""`            | `"-hopbox1"`    | The release name shows a hopbox build. `LOCALVERSION_AUTO` stays off.                                                   |
| `MODULE_SIG`                                                      | `y`             | `n`             | hopbox does not sign modules. Unsigned modules on a kernel with `MODULE_SIG=y` mark the kernel as tainted at each load. |
| `MODULE_SIG_ALL`                                                  | `y`             | not set         | It depends on `MODULE_SIG`.                                                                                             |
| `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM`                                           | `y`             | `n`             | It selects `MODULE_SIG`. `MODULE_SIG` cannot go off while this option is on.                                            |
| `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM_EARLY`                                     | `y`             | `n`             | It depends on `SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM`.                                                                                  |
| `MODULE_SIG_KEY`, `SYSTEM_TRUSTED_KEYS`, `SYSTEM_REVOCATION_KEYS` | not in the file | `""`            | The build makes no signing key and embeds no key. Kconfig then drops `MODULE_SIG_KEY` and `SYSTEM_REVOCATION_KEYS`.     |

Kconfig also drops the options that depend on the options above, such as `CRYPTO_FIPS`, the other `MODULE_SIG_*` options, and `LOCK_DOWN_KERNEL_FORCE_*`.

`make olddefconfig` on the build host makes these changes:

* Rust is off, because the tested server has no `rustc` and no `bindgen`. The Rust drivers and `ANDROID_BINDER_IPC` drop out.
* The options that exist only in the Debian kernel patches drop out, such as `LOCK_DOWN_IN_EFI_SECURE_BOOT` and `SECURITY_PERF_EVENTS_RESTRICT`.
* The options that are new in 6.18.16 to 6.18.57 take their defaults, such as `CXL_RAS=y` and `UNWIND_USER=y`.
* `ACPI_PLATFORM_PROFILE` changes from `m` to `y`.

A different toolchain on the build host can change the config. For example, a host with `rustc` turns Rust on. Then `build.sh` stops at step 5 of the build.

The config has these features that hopbox needs:

| Feature            | Options                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| KVM                | `CONFIG_KVM=m`, `CONFIG_KVM_INTEL=m`, `CONFIG_KVM_X86=m`                                                                       |
| vsock to the guest | `CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK=m`, `CONFIG_VHOST=m`, `CONFIG_VSOCKETS=m`                                                                  |
| tap devices        | `CONFIG_TUN=m`                                                                                                                 |
| cgroup v2          | `CONFIG_CGROUPS=y`, `CONFIG_MEMCG=y`, `CONFIG_BLK_CGROUP=y`, `CONFIG_CGROUP_PIDS=y`, `CONFIG_CPUSETS=y`, `CONFIG_CGROUP_BPF=y` |
| nftables           | `CONFIG_NF_TABLES=m`, `CONFIG_NF_TABLES_INET=y`, `CONFIG_NFT_NAT=m`, `CONFIG_NFT_MASQ=m`                                       |
| XFS with reflink   | `CONFIG_XFS_FS=m`. Reflink has no option in 6.18. `xfs.ko` always has it.                                                      |
| btrfs              | `CONFIG_BTRFS_FS=m`                                                                                                            |
| WireGuard          | `CONFIG_WIREGUARD=m`                                                                                                           |

## Install

```sh
sudo build/hostkernel/install.sh /path/to/hostkernel-build
```

The argument is the `WORK_DIR` of the build. Its default is `$PWD/hostkernel-build`. The script takes these steps:

1. It checks that it runs as root on Debian 13 amd64.
2. It checks the image package against `SHA256SUMS.debs`.
3. It installs the image package with `dpkg -i`. The package makes `/boot/initrd.img-6.18.57-hopbox1` and runs `update-grub`.
4. It writes `/etc/default/grub.d/20_hopbox_kernel.cfg` and runs `update-grub` again.
5. It checks that `/boot/grub/grub.cfg` has the entry of the new kernel. If the entry is missing, the script removes the file of step 4, runs `update-grub`, and stops with an error.

The script does not reboot. Reboot by hand.

The file of step 4 pins the GRUB default by the ID of the menu entry. GRUB names each entry after the UUID of the root file system:

```sh
GRUB_DEFAULT="gnulinux-advanced-<root-uuid>>gnulinux-6.18.57-hopbox1-advanced-<root-uuid>"
```

A Debian kernel upgrade through `linux-image-amd64` does not change this default. The script does not edit `/etc/default/grub`.

After the reboot, these commands show a good host:

```sh
uname -r                      # 6.18.57-hopbox1
cat /proc/sys/kernel/tainted  # 0
ls /dev/kvm /dev/vhost-vsock
```

On the tested server, SSH answered 187 to 319 seconds after the reboot command.

## Fallback

The Debian kernels stay installed. They are in the “Advanced options” menu of GRUB.

To boot a Debian kernel once, run `sudo grub-reboot '<entry ID>'` and reboot. On the tested server, the GRUB environment block is on mdraid, and GRUB cannot clear `next_entry` at boot. `grub-reboot` prints a warning about this. After the reboot, clear it by hand:

```sh
sudo grub-editenv /boot/grub/grubenv unset next_entry
```

To go back to the Debian default for good, remove the pin and update GRUB:

```sh
sudo rm /etc/default/grub.d/20_hopbox_kernel.cfg
sudo update-grub
```

# The machine API

> The machine calls of the public API, MachineService: who can do what, the messages, the lifecycle calls, the access calls, sharing, settings, the suspension, the audit entries, and the change events.

The service `hopbox.v1.MachineService` of the public API creates, reads, and changes the machines of an org. [Placement](/reference/placement/) covers how a create picks the node of a machine. [The admin API](/reference/admin-api/#machineservice) covers the calls of instance admins on machines, and [the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#imageservice) the images that new machines start from. [The API server](/reference/api/) covers the parts that every call shares: the request gate, the policy check, the idempotency keys, and the error codes. The generated reference is [Public API](/api/public/). The code is in `internal/service` (`machines.go`, `machine_lifecycle.go`, `machine_admin.go`, `machine_events.go`) and `internal/api` (`handlers_machine.go`). The access calls are in `machine_access.go` and `handlers_machine_access.go`.

| Calls                                                                            | What they do                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `CreateMachine`                                                                  | Makes a machine and places it on a node.                                                                                                                                 |
| `GetMachine`, `ListMachines`, `WatchMachines`                                    | Read the machines that the caller sees, once or as a stream of changes.                                                                                                  |
| `ListMachineSizes`                                                               | Reads the sizes that a machine can have.                                                                                                                                 |
| `StartMachine`, `StopMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, `DeleteMachine` | Set the target state of a machine, then wait for it ([Lifecycle calls](#lifecycle-calls)).                                                                               |
| `ShareMachine`, `UnshareMachine`                                                 | Open a private machine to the whole org, or make it private again.                                                                                                       |
| `UpdateMachine`                                                                  | Changes the restart policy, the start command, or the auto-delete timeout.                                                                                               |
| `SetMachineURLPort`, `SetMachineURLVisibility`                                   | Change the port that the URL of a machine reaches, and who can open the URL.                                                                                             |
| `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`                                | Run a command in a machine, copy files in and out, and read its log ([Access calls](#access-calls)). The WebSocket `/api/ws/exec` carries the same exec for the console. |

The examples on this page use the shell function `browser` of [the sign-in, account, and audit API](/reference/auth-api/), with the session cookie of the caller. [Create and manage machines](/guide/machines/) runs the whole flow on a server.

## What runs the machines

The machine API sets the target state of a machine and waits for it. The executor of the machine on its node moves the machine there, and reports each step back ([the node executor](/reference/executor/), [the executor protocol](/reference/executor-protocol/)). The waits of the lifecycle calls end once the machine got there ([Lifecycle calls](#lifecycle-calls)).

On a server with the node role, `hopboxd run` runs the executors with the Firecracker driver ([the Firecracker driver](/reference/firecracker-driver/)). A new machine reaches `running` once its guest agent applied the configuration of the machine. The first boot of an image on a node also unpacks the image. For the default image on the [tested server](/reference/preflight/#the-tested-server), the whole create takes about 25 s.

Each machine gets an IPv4 address of the subnet of its node at its create ([the node network](/reference/node-network/#addresses)). Its URL and the SSH front door reach it at this address ([the edge role](/reference/edge/), [the SSH front door](/reference/ssh-front-door/)). When the subnet of the node has no free address, the create fails with `no capacity`. Exec, file copy, and the log run over the guest link, without the network ([the node executor](/reference/executor/#exec-file-copy-and-logs)). Env vars and secrets reach a machine through its spec ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/)).

## The org of a request

`CreateMachine`, `ListMachines`, and `WatchMachines` act in one org. They have the field `org_id`, an optional string. Leave it out to act in the default org of the caller: the org of an API key, or else the personal org of the account. A caller without either acts in no org, and the policy refuses it.

The service layer reads the role of the caller in the org before the policy check. A caller that is not a member has no role. So an org that does not exist gets the same `permission_denied` as an org of others. An `org_id` that is not a UUID gets `invalid_argument`.

## Naming a machine

A call on one machine names it in the oneof field `machine`: either `id`, the UUID of the machine, or `name`, its name. Machine names are unique in the whole install ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-names)), so a name alone finds the machine.

| Case                         | Code               | Message                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Neither field is set         | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: the request names no machine`                                           |
| `id` is not a UUID           | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: the machine ID "<id>" is not a UUID`                                    |
| `name` breaks the name rules | `invalid_argument` | `invalid argument: invalid name: ...`, or `invalid argument: reserved machine name: "ns1"` |
| No machine has the ID        | `not_found`        | `not found: no machine has the ID <id>`                                                    |
| No machine has the name      | `not_found`        | `not found: no machine has the name "<name>"`                                              |

A machine that is being deleted keeps its name in its row until its executor deleted it. Meanwhile, a new machine of the same org can take the name back. A name then names two machines for a while. The lookup by name returns the one that holds the name live, else the newest. A lookup by name never finds a machine whose current state is `deleted`. A lookup by ID still finds it, until the leader drops its row ([hopboxd](/reference/hopboxd/#leader-jobs)).

## Who can do what

The creator of a machine is the account that made it, or the org key that made it. A machine starts private to its creator. Its creator can share it with the whole org.

| Call                                                                                                 | The creator | A member, on a shared machine | A member, on a private machine of another | An org admin or owner, on a private machine of another |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GetMachine`, and the machine in `ListMachines` and `WatchMachines`                                  | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | yes                                                    |
| `StopMachine`, `DeleteMachine`                                                                       | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | yes                                                    |
| `StartMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, `UpdateMachine`                                    | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |
| `ShareMachine`, `UnshareMachine`, `SetMachineURLPort`, `SetMachineURLVisibility`                     | yes         | no, `permission_denied`       | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |
| `Exec`, `Upload`, `Download`, `StreamMachineLogs`, and the WebSocket of exec (action `machine.exec`) | yes         | yes                           | no, `not_found`                           | no, `permission_denied`                                |

These rules hold for each caller that acts in the org of the machine:

* A `session` or a `cli_token` acts in each org where its account has a role.
* A `member_key` acts only in its own org, as its account, while the account has a role there.
* An `org_key` acts only in its own org. It has the rights of a member, without private machines. It is never an org admin. A machine that an org key makes is shared from the start, and its creator is that key.
* An instance admin has only the rights of its own roles here. It acts on the machines of others through the admin API ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#machineservice)).

A caller that cannot read a machine gets `not_found`, with the same message as for a machine that does not exist. So the call tells nothing about the private machines of others.

`RenameMachine`, `UpdateMachine`, `SetMachineURLPort`, and `SetMachineURLVisibility` check their fields before they look up the machine. So a bad value gets `invalid_argument`, also for a machine that does not exist, or that the caller cannot read. The check reads only the request, so it tells nothing about the machine. An anonymous caller still gets `unauthenticated` first. A caller that can read the machine, but not do the action, gets `permission_denied` with the message `permission denied: a caller of kind <kind> may not do <action>`.

The API listener resolves session cookies, CLI tokens, and API keys ([the API server](/reference/api/#request-gate)). A CLI token acts as its account. A member key acts as its account, in the org of the key only. An org key acts as a member of its org without private machines.

## Messages

### Machine

| Field                 | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                  | string                      | The UUID of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `org_id`              | string                      | The UUID of the org of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `name`                | string                      | The name of the machine, unique in the install. It is the first label of its URL.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `state`               | `MachineState`              | The current state ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#machine-states)).                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `target_state`        | `MachineState`              | The state that the machine must reach.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `size`                | `MachineSize`               | The size of the machine. The machine keeps the numbers of its size from its create.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `image_name`          | string                      | The name of the image that the machine started from, for example `default`.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `image_digest`        | string                      | The digest of that image: `sha256:` and 64 hex digits.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `creator_account_id`  | string                      | The UUID of the account that made the machine. Empty for a machine that an org key made, and after the delete of the account.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `creator_key_id`      | string                      | The UUID of the org key that made the machine, or empty.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `shared`              | bool                        | `true` for a machine that is open to the whole org.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `restart_policy`      | `RestartPolicy`             | The action of the executor after the machine stops by itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `start_command`       | string                      | The command that the guest agent runs after each boot, or empty.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `auto_delete_timeout` | `google.protobuf.Duration`  | The time without use after which hopbox deletes the machine. Unset means off. The delete comes 1 to 2 minutes after this time from the last recorded use ([Auto-delete](#auto-delete)).                                                                                           |
| `url`                 | string                      | `https://<name>.<domain>`, for example `https://box1.example.com`. Empty while the install has no domain.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `url_port`            | int32                       | The port in the machine that the URL reaches. The default is 8000.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `url_visibility`      | `URLVisibility`             | Who can open the URL. The default is `URL_VISIBILITY_PRIVATE`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ssh_port`            | int32                       | The SSH port of the machine on the edge servers, 10000 to 30000. It never changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `reboot_pending`      | bool                        | `true` while a boot that a request asked for did not run yet, and the target is `running`. A machine with another target has no pending boot. For example, a stop that comes before the boot of a start ends it.                                                                  |
| `skipped_env_vars`    | int32                       | The count of env vars and secrets that the guest agent of the running machine left out, because their names break its rules ([the env var API](/reference/vars-api/#names-and-values)). 0 is the normal case.                                                                     |
| `last_activity_time`  | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The last use of the machine, for the auto-delete timeout ([Auto-delete](#auto-delete)).                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `state_change_time`   | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the last change of the current state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `delete_request_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the delete request. Unset for a machine whose target is not `deleted`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `version`             | int64                       | The version of the machine. It starts at 1 and grows by 1 with each change of the machine. A request makes such a change. A report of its executor makes one too. So does a new count of skipped env values. So does a change of an env var or a secret that reaches the machine. |
| `create_time`         | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The creation time of the machine.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `update_time`         | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | The time of the last change that a request made.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

In the JSON codec, a field with its default value is left out, for example `shared` false or an empty `start_command`.

### MachineSize

| Field          | Type   | Description                                  |
| -------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | string | The name of the size, for example `default`. |
| `vcpus`        | int32  | The count of vCPUs.                          |
| `memory_bytes` | int64  | The RAM, in bytes.                           |
| `disk_bytes`   | int64  | The size of the sparse disk, in bytes.       |

A fresh install has one size, `default`: 2 vCPUs, 8 GiB of RAM, and a sparse disk of 100 GB ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#sizes)). An instance admin can add other sizes ([the admin API](/reference/admin-api/#sizeservice)).

### MachineState

| Value                       | State                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `MACHINE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response.                                                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_PENDING`     | `pending`: the machine exists, but no node acted on it yet.                    |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STARTING`    | `starting`: the microVM boots.                                                 |
| `MACHINE_STATE_RUNNING`     | `running`: the microVM runs.                                                   |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STANDBY`     | `standby`: the microVM is paused, and its memory stays in the RAM of the node. |
| `MACHINE_STATE_HIBERNATED`  | `hibernated`: the memory is in a file on disk, and the microVM does not run.   |
| `MACHINE_STATE_STOPPED`     | `stopped`: the microVM does not run. The disk stays.                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_FAILED`      | `failed`: an action failed. The saved state of the machine stays.              |
| `MACHINE_STATE_DELETED`     | `deleted`: the machine and its saved state are gone.                           |
| `MACHINE_STATE_MOVING`      | `moving`: a drain moves the machine to another node.                           |

### RestartPolicy

| Value                        | Policy                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `RESTART_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response. In `CreateMachineRequest`, it takes the default `always`. In `UpdateMachineRequest`, it keeps the policy.                                     |
| `RESTART_POLICY_ALWAYS`      | `always`: the executor starts the machine again after a crash, a shutdown from inside, or a node reboot ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#restart-policy)). |
| `RESTART_POLICY_NEVER`       | `never`: the machine and its start command stay stopped.                                                                                                           |

A value that is not in the enum gets `invalid_argument` with the message `invalid argument: the restart policy <n> is not known`.

### URLVisibility

| Value                        | Visibility                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `URL_VISIBILITY_UNSPECIFIED` | Never in a response. A request cannot use it.                                                                                                                    |
| `URL_VISIBILITY_PRIVATE`     | `private`: only an account that uses the machine can open its URL, in a browser with a console session ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#private-machine-urls)). |
| `URL_VISIBILITY_PUBLIC`      | `public`: anyone can open the URL, without an account.                                                                                                           |

The edge servers serve the URL of a machine ([the edge role](/reference/edge/#machine-urls)). A change of the URL port or of the visibility reaches them with the next routes, within a second or two ([the control channel](/reference/control-channel/#edge-pushes)).

## Lifecycle calls

`StartMachine`, `StopMachine`, `RebootMachine`, `RenameMachine`, and `DeleteMachine` are the lifecycle calls. Each one takes these steps:

1. It checks the policy, then its input.
2. It locks the rows in the order of [Control store tables](/reference/control-store/#orgs): the key lock of the creator account, the org row, then the machine row. It checks the policy again under the locks, because the role or the machine can change in between.
3. It refuses a call that the suspension of the org blocks ([Suspension](#suspension)).
4. It sets the new target state, as `Apply(target, current)` of the domain gives it ([Domain rules](/reference/domain-rules/#lifecycle-actions)). An action that the states do not allow gets `failed_precondition`, for example `failed precondition: machine action not allowed: cannot reboot a machine that is pending`.
5. It writes the audit entry and the change event in the same transaction, and commits.
6. It waits for the machine, then returns it.

A request that asks for the target that the machine has already changes nothing. It writes no audit entry and no event, and the version stays. The call still waits. For example, a stop of a machine with the target `stopped` waits for the state `stopped`. The rule has three exceptions. A reboot always asks for a new boot. A start of a `failed` machine asks for a new boot too, even with the target `running` already ([StartMachine](#startmachine)). A delete of a machine whose target is `deleted` fails with `failed_precondition` and the message `failed precondition: machine action not allowed: cannot delete a machine that is being deleted`.

### The wait

The executor of the node moves the machine toward its target. The call waits for that, and ends its wait at the first of these events:

| Event                                                                                                                                                                        | `done`  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| The machine reached what the call asked for.                                                                                                                                 | `true`  |
